Google Chat help

This guide holds Google’s own help for Google Chat, gathered from support.google.com on 14 November 2026. It covers messages, spaces, calls, files and notifications in Chat, on its own and inside Gmail.

Google writes the same article once for each device it runs on, so where an article differs by platform the heading says which one it is for: Computer, or iPhone and iPad. Google’s Android editions are left out, as this collection covers Windows, the web, iPhone and iPad, and Alexa. The categories are Google’s own topics: Google no longer puts a trail above each article, so each article is filed under the topic its help centre lists it in.

The help text belongs to its publisher and is gathered here unchanged for accessible reading. This guide’s own arrangement and wording are available under CC BY-SA 4.0.

Create and join spaces

Add a Google Group to a space

Through Google Groups, a set of users like project teams, departments, and classmates, can communicate and collaborate on common interests. When a group is added to a space, its members are automatically synced from groups to spaces in Chat.

  • Any changes to the group’s membership, such as addition and removal of members, are also automatically reflected in the space.
  • This feature is available for Google Workspace accounts only.

Learn about group restrictions

  • Add a group
    • If you can’t add a group to a space, contact the group owner or manager. Your admin may have restricted this feature.
  • Guest access
    • If Allow people outside your organization to join is enabled, the group and its members are invited to the space.
    • If a group has external members added to it and the space doesn’t have Allow people outside your organization to join enabled, the external members are excluded in the space.
  • Leave a space
    • Group member memberships are tied to the space via the group. To leave the space, you must leave the group through Google Groups. Learn how to leave a group.
    • A group member can’t be removed from the space directly in a space in Chat. Either the member has to be removed from the group or the group has to be removed from the space.
  • Tip: If you can’t leave directly from the space, you can mute the space instead.
  • Tasks
    • Tasks can’t be assigned to someone who isn’t a member of the space or was added to the space through a Google Group.
  • Space limit
    • If the total number of members in the groups within a space exceeds the space limit, all groups are removed from the space.

Add a group to a space

If you have permissions to manage members, you can add a group to a space. When you add a group, it may take some time to sync all group members with the space. You can still post messages in the space while the group and its members sync with the space. Group members who join the space after the messages are posted will have these messages marked as unread.

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.

  • On the left, click Spaces select a space.

  • At the top left, click the dropdown next to chat team Manage members.

  • At the top right, click + Add.

  • Enter the name of the group you want to add.

  • Click Add. Tips:

  • If you can’t add a group to a space, contact the group owners and managers. Your administrator may have restricted this action to the group owners and managers.

  • Group members can be promoted to space owners or managers. Learn about your role as a space owner or manager.

Remove a group from a space

Important: If you remove a group from a space, its members also lose access to the files previously shared with the space. However, if these files were directly shared with the Groups or its members, the members retain access.

If you have permissions to manage members, you can remove a group from a space. After you remove a group, it may take some time to remove the group members from the space. After group members are removed from the space, they can’t:

  • Perform any actions in that space
  • View that space’s message history
  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • On the left, click Spaces select a space.
  • At the top right, click Members Manage members.
  • Next to the group name, click More options Remove from space. Tip: To remove an individual group member from a space, remove the member from Google Groups. Only group owners, or group members with the right permissions, can remove members from a group.

View groups in a space

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.

  • On the left, click Spaces select a space.

  • At the top right, click Members Manage members. Group memberships may not be viewable if:

  • Your group’s member visibility isn’t set to owners, managers, or members.

  • You’re on a mobile device. Some members may appear grayed out

  • Group sync may take some time.

  • External members in a group are always grayed out because they’re automatically excluded in spaces with guest access turned off.

Learn about changes in how to sync groups & memberships

You can add groups directly to spaces.

  • To sync groups and memberships, add any currently invited groups again.
  • If you want users to join the space instead, make the space discoverable or open and share a link to the space. Learn more about spaces with different access levels. Important: Groups invited to the space before October 17, 2023 appear under the “Invited” section of the member list. These group members weren’t automatically added and joined the space on their own.

How to download your data in Google Takeout

You can download messages sent by direct members of a space as part of the Google Chat data in Google Takeout. You can download messages sent by group members of a space as part of the Google Groups data in Google Takeout. Learn how to download your data.

Add or remove someone in a space

To add more people to a space in Google Chat, add them to the member list or mention them directly in the space.

Tips: If you use Chat with a Google Workspace account:

  • You can add a Google Group to the space. Learn how to add a Google Group to a space.
  • Your administrator can create a space that everyone in your organization can find. For example, your administrator can add a group named everyone@yourcompany.com to a space.
  • By default, any member can remove another member without administrator approval or restrictions, unless the space settings explicitly restrict membership management.

Add someone to a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • On the left, select the space.

  • In the chat header, click the dropdown Manage members.

    • A list of current members displays.

  • At the top right, click + Add.

  • Enter the name or email address of the person or group.

  • Click Add. Tips:

  • To quickly add a new person to a space, in the reply area, enter @ followed by the person’s name.

  • To view people that you’ve invited to the space, click Manage members Invited. Learn how space invites work

  • An email invite is sent to someone if:

    • They haven’t had a conversation with you before.
    • They belong to another organization and the space was created by your Google Workspace account.

  • Someone you invite to a space is added directly if:

    • They’ve had a conversation with you before.
    • You’re in the same organization.

  • People added directly to spaces don’t get email notifications.

  • If you have a Google Workspace account, members of your organization may get an email invite or added directly to a space.

Remove someone from a space

Important: If you have the ability to manage members, you can remove members from a space. After you remove someone, they can’t:

  • Participate in the conversation.
  • View that space’s message history.
  • Access shared files in the space.
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • In the chat header, click the dropdown Manage members.
  • To the right of the person or group name, click More options Remove from space. Tip: If a person was added as part of a Google Group, remove them from the group first and then from the space.

Copy space member email addresses

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • In the chat header, click the dropdown Manage members.
  • Click Copy member emails .

Block & report a space

If you experience abusive behavior in a Google Chat space, you can block and report the space. You can also preview spaces marked as spam, then choose to block or join the space.

Learn what happens when you block a space

When you block a space:

  • Posts you made in the space stay visible to others.

  • You no longer get updates from the space.

  • The space won’t appear in your “Spaces” list or space searches.

  • You won’t get any future invitation notifications for the space, but your name appears as an invited member. If you get an invitation to a space you blocked:

  • You appear as an invited member, but you won’t get any notifications or be added to the space.

  • The space organizer or other members won’t know you blocked the space. Tips:

  • Blocked users can’t add you to a space, nor can you add blocked users to a space.

  • When you unblock a space, you can only rejoin the space if add appears in “Browse spaces.”

Block a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

  • Choose one:

    • On the left, under “Spaces,” next to the space name, click More options Block space.
    • Select the space you want to block Click the space details drop-down Block space.

  • Click Block. Tips:

  • To report the space as spam or abuse, check the box next to Report this space as spam or abuse.

  • If you report a space for abuse, a copy of the last 50 messages in the space is sent to Google for review.

  • To rejoin a space that you blocked, another member of that space must invite or add you again.

Unblock a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Choose an option:
    • In Chat, at the top, click Settings Manage blocked spaces.
    • In Gmail, at the top, click Settings See all settings Chat and Meet Manage chat settings Manage blocked spaces.
  • Next to the space, click Unblock.

Block a space marked as spam

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • In Chat, click New Chat Browse spaces.
  • Click Browse spaces menu items Spam invites.
  • Next to the space, click Preview.
    • For your protection, you can’t download links or find images when you preview the space.
  • To block the space and future invitations, click Block. Optional: To report the space, click the box next to “Report this space as spam or abuse” Block.

Join a space marked as spam

  • In Chat, click New Chat Browse spaces.
  • Click Browse spaces menu items Spam invites.
  • Next to the space, click Preview.
    • For your protection, you can’t download links or find images when you preview the space.
  • Click Join. Tip: When you join a space marked as spam, the spam label is removed and the space is added to your list of joined spaces.

Manage spam space invites

Space invites that appear to be spam are filtered into a separate section. You can choose to join or block the space.

You can prevent future invites from spaces marked as spam if you block the space. If you think Google wrongly filtered a space as spam, you can still join the space.

Related resources

  • Block & report someone
  • Leave or rejoin a space

Change the space access level

For work or school accounts, you can restrict access to a space to specific members or make the space discoverable or open to everyone in your organization.

Learn how private, discoverable & open spaces work

Learn about private spaces
  • Ideal for discussion amongst teams, projects, and groups.
  • To join a space, a space member must invite or add you to the space.
  • Unless you’re a member or invited to the space, you can’t browse for it in Chat.
Learn about discoverable spaces
  • Ideal for topics that aren’t limited to specific individuals or teams.
  • When a space is discoverable, you can:
    • Find the space in “Browse spaces.”
    • See the name and description.
    • If the space owners and managers allow it, request to join.
Learn about open spaces

  • Ideal for topics that aren’t limited to specific individuals or teams.

  • When a space is open, you can:

    • Find the space in “Browse spaces.”
    • See the name and description.
    • Preview messages.
    • Join the space.

  • If you have a link to the space, you can join it with the link. Google Workspace plans that support open spaces

Update the space access level

Important: To change the access level for a space, you need to be a space owner or manager. Learn about your role as a space owner or manager.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • On the left, select a space.

  • At the top, click the space name Space settings .

  • Under the “Access” section, select a space access level:

    • Private: Users can’t find or join this space unless you add them.
    • Discoverable: Anyone in your organization can find the space.
    • Open: Anyone in your organization can find and join the space and preview messages.

  • If your space is private, discoverable, or open to a group of users that is smaller than your entire organization, you can choose whether users are allowed to request to join the space.

  • Click Save. If you have multiple target audiences:

  • Next to “Advanced access settings,” click Advanced .

  • Select who can join and who can find your space.

    • You can add only one audience in the “Who can join” field and multiple audiences in the “Who can find” field.

  • Turn Request to join on or off.

  • Click Done. Tips:

  • If a space is open to everyone in your organization, you can’t invite people outside your organization to join.

  • You can find additional access options your administrator creates. If you have questions about available access options, contact your administrator.

  • If your administrator deletes the target audience you select for your space, ” Deleted Audience” displays in the space history and space access is private by default.

Add new members to an open space

You can add new members to an open space by either:

  • Copying a link to the space and sharing with others.

  • Directly adding or inviting them. Add members with an open space link

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • At the top, click the space name Copy link to this space.

  • Share the link to anyone you’d like to invite or reference the space with. Add members to your space directly

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • At the top, click the space name Manage members.

  • Click Add.

  • Enter the name, email, or Google Group, or select suggested contacts to invite.

  • Click Add.

  • Use threads in a space

Create & assign tasks in Google Chat

As a member of a space in Google Chat, you can create and manage group tasks and assign tasks to other space members. You can view tasks in the space where they’re created. If a task is assigned to you, it appears in your personal task list in Google Tasks. When someone creates or updates a task, a notification appears in the space.

Tips:

  • If you use a work or school account and don’t have the “Tasks” tab in a space, contact your Google Workspace administrator to turn on this feature.
  • When a space becomes too large, you can no longer:
    • Assign tasks
    • Mention anyone through “@”

Create & assign a task in a space

Important: When you delete a task, it’s deleted for all members of the space and from the assignee’s personal task list.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail, on the left, click Chat.

  • Select the space where you want to create a task.

  • At the top right, click Tasks .

  • At the bottom of the panel, click Add.

  • Enter details about the task, such as:

    • Title
    • Details
    • Date
    • Assignee

  • Click Add. Tips:

  • If you add a date to your task, you get notifications in Chat for the scheduled dates.

  • If the assignee leaves the space, the task remains in the space and in their personal task list in Google Tasks.

  • Users may have restrictions when they assign tasks to a subset of members. Learn more about group restrictions.

Edit a task

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • At the top right, click Tasks .

  • Click the title, details, date, or assignee and make the changes. Tips: If you have a task in your personal task list:

  • You can edit the task title, details, and date from your personal task list.

  • Changes update the task for everyone in the space and a notification displays.

Mark a task complete

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • At the top right, click Tasks .

  • Next to the task, point to Incomplete and click Complete . Tips: If you have a task in your personal task list:

  • You can edit the task title, details, and date from your personal task list.

  • Changes update the task for everyone in the space and a notification displays.

Mark a task incomplete

  • In Chat, select the space.
  • At the top right, click Tasks .
  • Next to “Completed,” to view the tasks, click Expand .
  • Next to the task, click Complete to change the status to Incomplete .

Delete a task

Important: When you delete a task, it’s deleted for all members of the space and from the assignee’s personal task list.

  • In Chat, select the space.
  • Select the space.
  • At the top right, click Tasks .
  • At the top right, click Delete Delete.

Create & assign tasks in Google Chat (Computer)

As a member of a space in Google Chat, you can create and manage group tasks and assign tasks to other space members. You can view tasks in the space where they’re created. If a task is assigned to you, it appears in your personal task list in Google Tasks. When someone creates or updates a task, a notification appears in the space.

Tips:

  • If you use a work or school account and don’t have the “Tasks” tab in a space, contact your Google Workspace administrator to turn on this feature.
  • When a space becomes too large, you can no longer:
    • Assign tasks
    • Mention anyone through “@”

Create & assign a task in a space

Important: When you delete a task, it’s deleted for all members of the space and from the assignee’s personal task list.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail, on the left, click Chat.

  • Select the space where you want to create a task.

  • At the top right, click Tasks .

  • At the bottom of the panel, click Add.

  • Enter details about the task, such as:

    • Title
    • Details
    • Date
    • Assignee

  • Click Add. Tips:

  • If you add a date to your task, you get notifications in Chat for the scheduled dates.

  • If the assignee leaves the space, the task remains in the space and in their personal task list in Google Tasks.

  • Users may have restrictions when they assign tasks to a subset of members. Learn more about group restrictions.

Edit a task

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • At the top right, click Tasks .

  • Click the title, details, date, or assignee and make the changes. Tips: If you have a task in your personal task list:

  • You can edit the task title, details, and date from your personal task list.

  • Changes update the task for everyone in the space and a notification displays.

Mark a task complete

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • At the top right, click Tasks .

  • Next to the task, point to Incomplete and click Complete . Tips: If you have a task in your personal task list:

  • You can edit the task title, details, and date from your personal task list.

  • Changes update the task for everyone in the space and a notification displays.

Mark a task incomplete

  • In Chat, select the space.
  • At the top right, click Tasks .
  • Next to “Completed,” to view the tasks, click Expand .
  • Next to the task, click Complete to change the status to Incomplete .

Delete a task

Important: When you delete a task, it’s deleted for all members of the space and from the assignee’s personal task list.

  • In Chat, select the space.
  • Select the space.
  • At the top right, click Tasks .
  • At the top right, click Delete Delete.

Create & assign tasks in Google Chat (iPhone and iPad)

As a member of a space in Google Chat, you can create and manage group tasks and assign tasks to other space members. You can view tasks in the space where they’re created. If a task is assigned to you, it appears in your personal task list in Google Tasks. When someone creates or updates a task, a notification appears in the space.

Tips:

  • If you use a work or school account and don’t have the “Tasks” tab in a space, contact your Google Workspace administrator to turn on this feature.
  • When a space becomes too large, you can no longer:
    • Assign tasks
    • Mention anyone through “@”

Create & assign a task in a space

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • In the bottom navigation menu, tap Spaces select the space.
  • On the top, tap the Tasks tab.
  • At the bottom right, tap New task .
  • Enter a title for the task.
  • Optional: To add a description or more details, tap Details and enter the information.
  • Optional: To add a date, tap Google Calendar select a date tap Done.
  • Tip: If you add a date to your task, you get notifications at the scheduled dates.
  • Optional: To assign the task to a member of the space, tap Person tap the name of the person. To assign the task to someone who isn’t a member of the space, invite them to the space first.
  • Tap Save. Important: When you delete a task, it’s deleted for all members of the space and from the assignee’s personal task list.

Edit a task

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • On the bottom, tap Spaces select the space.

  • On the top, tap the Tasks tab select the task.

  • Tap the title, details, date, or assignee and make the changes.

  • Tap Back . Tips: If you have a task in your personal task list:

  • You can edit the task title, details, and date from your personal task list.

  • Changes update the task for everyone in the space and a notification displays.

Mark a task complete

  • In Chat, select the space.

  • At the top, tap the Tasks tab select the task.

  • At the top right, tap Mark as complete . Tips: If you have a task in your personal task list:

  • You can edit the task title, details, and date from your personal task list.

  • Changes update the task for everyone in the space and a notification displays.

Mark a task incomplete

  • In Chat, select the space.
  • On the bottom, tap Spaces select the space.
  • On the top, tap the Tasks tab.
  • Next to Completed, tap Expand to view the tasks.
  • Next to the task, tap Complete to change the status to Incomplete .

Delete a task

Important: When you delete a task, it’s deleted for all members of the space and from the assignee’s personal task list.

  • In Chat, select the space.
  • On the bottom, tap Spaces select the space.
  • On the top, tap the Tasks tab select the task.
  • At the top right, tap Delete .

Delete a space

When you no longer want to use a space, you can delete it. When a space is deleted, you can’t recover it.

Important:

  • You can only delete a space if you have the space owner role.
  • When you delete a space, all messages and tasks in the space are deleted. Permissions on Drive files are removed, but the file isn’t deleted.
  • If you’re the last space owner and want to leave, you must make someone else the space owner or delete the space.
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open the space that you want to delete.
  • At the top, click the space name Delete.
  • To confirm, click Delete. Tip: If you didn’t create the space, learn how to leave a space.

Email a space in Google Chat

You can create an email address for spaces in Google Chat to easily send emails to the space.

How to generate an email address from a space

You can generate an email address from a space in Google Chat to easily send emails to the space. Emails sent to the generated email will also post in the space.

Important: Only space managers can generate email addresses.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open the space you want to generate an email for.
  • Select the space name at the top of Chat.
  • From the drop-down menu, click Space settings .
  • Under “Email,” click Generate email .
    • “Generate email” creates a space email address for you. This space email is backed by a Google Group email address.
    • Space managers (also the owners of the backing Group in this case) can:
      • Update space email settings. Select Manage email Advanced settings.
      • Customize email address. Learn more about customizing your email address.
  • To send emails to the space, copy and paste the generated email address into the “to” or “cc” of the email you want sent to the space.
    • Emails sent to the space are displayed in plain text in an email card. The email card includes a snippet of the email to help space members understand the email context.
    • To view the full email in Google Groups, including links and attachments, tap View message in the email card. To view the entirety of the email within the chat space, click Show more.
  • To remove this feature, you can disable or delete the email address.
  • Mobile users can view and copy the space’s email address to send emails to the space, but they can’t generate or manage (e.g., customize, disable & delete) the email address.
  • Space managers added after the email is created can disable the email, but can’t delete the email unless they’re an owner in Google Groups. Learn how to assign someone as a group owner.
  • Existing Groups policies are respected. For example, if your admin has disabled group creation, those users will be restricted from generating emails for spaces in Chat. If your admin has disabled access to Groups (groups.google.com), users also can’t view the full email or manage the email in Groups.
  • You can’t use this space email currently to invite a space and its members to a Calendar event.

How to update a space email address

You can change the email address to make it more recognizable to members. However, when you update the address, emails sent to the previous address will no longer be posted in the space. Additionally, email cards that were previously sent to the space (via the old address) will remain in the space, but clicking on the “View message” buttons in the card will no longer open the full email.

To update the space email:

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open the space you want to update the email for.
  • Select the space name at the top of Chat.
  • From the drop-down menu, click Space settings .
  • Select Manage email Advanced settings (redirects to Google Groups).
  • Under group email, type the new email address for your space.
  • Click Save changes. Tip: To view the updated email address in the space settings page in Chat, refresh the page.

How to disable or delete the space email address

To disable or delete an email generated from a space:

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open the space you want to disable or delete the email address.
  • Select the space name at the top of Chat.
  • From the drop-down menu, click Space settings .
  • Next to the generated email, click Manage email then choose one of the available options:
    • Disable email address:
      • Emails sent to this address will no longer be posted in the space.
      • Emails will continue to post in the underlying Google Group.
    • Delete email address:
      • The generated email address will be permanently deleted.
      • Emails cards that were previously sent to space will remain in space, but clicking on the “View message” buttons in the card will no longer open the full email.
      • Space managers will need to create a new email to make spaces emailable again. Tip: Space managers added after the email is created can disable the email, but can’t delete the email unless they’re an owner in Google Groups. Learn how to assign someone as a group owner.

Learn how email subject line threading works

  • When you send emails to a Google Chat space, Chat ignores content in square brackets “[]” at the start of the subject line when it threads messages.
  • If emails use different content inside square brackets but have the same subsequent subject text, Chat might group them incorrectly. For example, “[Ticket-123] Alert” and “[Ticket-456] Alert” merge into the same conversation thread.
  • To force separate threads with unique identifiers, use curly braces “{}” or parentheses “()” instead of square brackets “[]”. For example, “{Ticket-123} System Alert” and “{Ticket-456} System Alert” correctly result in two separate threads.

Join a space in Google Chat (Computer)

When you’re invited to join a space, you can preview the space and view its message history.

When you leave a space, you can’t:

  • Rejoin unless another member adds or invites you.
  • Get updates on active conversation threads. If you rejoin a space, you can view all message history. If someone removes you from a space, you’ll need to be invited again.

Tip: If the space is open, you can rejoin at any time. Learn about open spaces.

Join a space

Important: If the space owner or manager turns off the request option, you can’t request to join a space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, click New chat Browse spaces .
  • Search for a space.
    • The spaces that you’re invited to appear at the top of the list.
  • Click the space name or View.
    • If the space is open, click Join. You can also preview the messages.
    • If the space is private or discoverable and the space allows it, you can submit a request to join. Tip: If you request to join a space, your username, email address, and avatar are shared with the space owner and manager once they receive your request. Some spaces may not allow requests to join.

Leave a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Next to a space name, click More options Leave Leave space.

Rejoin a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, click New chat Browse spaces .
  • Search for a space.
  • Click the space name or View.
    • If the space is open, click Join. You can also preview the messages.
    • If the space is private or discoverable and the space allows it, you can submit a request to join. Tip: You can delete a space you created. Learn how to delete a space.

Learn about spaces

To communicate with a group of people or an organization about a topic, project, or shared interest, create a space in Google Chat. For example, you can create a space to discuss timelines for a future marketing campaign.

With spaces you can:

  • Focus your conversation on a common area of interest or your projects, or make organizational announcements.
  • Create threads for things that require detailed discussion.
  • Share files and assign tasks to members.
  • Add apps to create easy workflows within your space.

Use spaces for collaboration or announcements

Important: If you use Chat with your personal Google Account, you can only create spaces for collaboration.

Use spaces for collaboration
  • Available for personal, work, or school accounts.
  • Use this type of space for important project or team updates, or connect around shared interests such as travel or cooking.
  • Everyone in the group can post, react, and reply to messages.
  • You can send a message to the entire group in the main conversation window or reply directly to a message and create a thread.
Use spaces for announcements
  • Available for work or school accounts.
  • Use this type of space to share important news and updates with your team.
  • As a space owner or manager, you can:
    • Post announcements in the main conversation window.
    • Respond to space member comments on your announcement.
    • Turn off replies.
  • As a space member, you can only react and reply directly to announcements.
  • After you create a space for announcements, you can’t change the type of space.

Organize spaces with threads

In addition to the main conversation in the space, you can reply to any message and create a separate thread. You can use threads to track important discussions and prevent the main conversation from being cluttered.

In a thread, you can:

  • Send and reply to messages.
  • Follow or unfollow the thread.
  • Change how you’re notified of new messages in a thread. Use threads in a space.

Manage access to the space

In work or school accounts, you can make the space private, discoverable, or open to everyone or a target audience in your organization.

Learn about private spaces
  • Ideal for discussion among teams, projects, and groups.
  • To join a space, a space member must invite or add you to the space.
  • Unless you’re a member or invited to the space, you can’t browse for it in Chat.
Learn about discoverable spaces
  • Ideal for topics that aren’t limited to specific individuals or teams.
  • When a space is discoverable, you can find the space, check the name and description, and if the space allows it, request to join.
  • If you have a link to the space, you may be able to request to join with the link.
Learn about open spaces
  • Ideal for topics that aren’t limited to specific individuals or teams.
  • When a space is open, you can browse, preview, and join the space.
  • If you have a link to the space, you can join it with the link.

Differences between spaces & direct messages

You can communicate with a group of people through spaces or direct messages in Chat. Both forms of communication work in different ways and serve different purposes:

  • Spaces: A central place where people can share files, assign tasks, and stay connected.
  • Direct messages: Chat directly with a group. For example, use direct messages to have a quick discussion after a meeting. Spaces

Direct messages

Message history

Your admin determines whether message history is on by default and if users can change this setting. Learn more about message history.

For personal accounts, you can turn history on or off. For Google Workspace accounts, history depends on your organization’s settings. Learn more about message history.

Name

If you use a Google Workspace account, the “Who can modify space board and details” permission controls who can modify the name and description.

If the space was created by a personal account, any space member can change the space name.

Member names are listed.

Description

If you use a Google Workspace account, the “Who can modify space board and details” permission controls who can modify the name and description.

If the space was created by a personal account, any space member can change the space description.

Direct messages don’t have descriptions.

Default Notifications

Members are notified for conversations they’re in or when @mentioned.

Members are notified for every message.

Membership

Members can leave a space. To rejoin the space, another member must add or invite them again.

Tip: If the space is open, you can rejoin any time.

Members can leave and rejoin.

Tip: For direct messages created before December 2020, members can’t leave.

Multiple chat spaces with the same people

Can have 2 or more spaces with the same group.

Can have 2 or more conversations with the same group.

Create and assign tasks

Can create and assign tasks to other space members.

Unnamed group conversations don’t have task features.

Shared files

Can share files and find a list of files shared with the space.

Can share files with the group, but can’t find a list of the files.

Learn about your role as a space owner or manager

When you create a space in Google Chat, you automatically become the space owner. As a space owner, you can:

  • Remove and add participants.

  • Promote other members to be space managers, or remove them from the list of space managers.

  • Delete a space.

  • Delete messages.

  • Edit the space name, avatar, and description. As a space manager, you have all the permissions of a space owner except the ability to:

  • Promote other members to be space owners.

  • Remove space owners from the list of space owners.

  • Delete a space. Space owners who use a work or school account can update additional settings, such as space access and permissions. Learn how to change space access and permissions.

Add members

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • Click the space name Manage members.
  • Click + Add.
  • Enter the name or email of the person or group that you want to add.
  • Click Add.

Remove members

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • Click the space name Manage members.
  • Point to the person and click More actions Remove from space.

Change a user’s role

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • Click the space name Manage members.
  • Next to the person’s name, under “Role,” click the dropdown.
    • To make someone a space owner: Select Owner.
    • To make someone a space manager: Select Manager.
    • To make someone a space member: Select Member. Tips:
  • Not all users can change other users’ roles.
  • The last space owner can’t leave a space unless they delete the space or make someone else a space owner.

Delete messages

Important: The “Delete messages” feature is only available to specific subscriptions and might not be available on your work or school account.

Space owners and managers can delete any message in a space. Space members can only delete their own messages. Learn how to delete a message as a space member.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • Point to the message you want to delete.
  • Click More actions Delete .
  • In the window that opens, click Delete. Tip: When a message is deleted in a space, a time stamp may appear. The time stamp remains for 30 days or longer based on the retention policy of your company.

  • Enter the name or email of the person or group that you want to add.
  • Click Add.

Remove members

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • Click the space name Manage members.
  • Point to the person and click More actions Remove from space.

Change a user’s role

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

Delete messages

Important: The “Delete messages” feature is only available to specific subscriptions and might not be available on your work or school account.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select the space.
  • Point to the message you want to delete.
  • Click More actions Delete .
  • In the window that opens, click Delete. Tip: When a message is deleted in a space, a time stamp may appear. The time stamp remains for 30 days or longer based on the retention policy of your company.

Manage space settings

As a space owner or manager, you can:

  • Control who can join a space.

  • Control who can manage members and groups.

  • Change whether the space is accessible to anyone in your organization or only to people you invite.

  • Control permissions for space members.

  • Control whether non-members can request to join a space. Important:

  • To manage space settings, you need a Google Workspace account.

  • When you create a space, you can invite people outside of your organization into a space. However, they won’t have access to some features, such as updating space details or adding people. Learn more about chatting with people outside your organization.

Update space access settings

If you’re a space owner or manager, you can make a space accessible to anyone in your organization or only to people you invite.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • On the left, select a space.

  • At the top, click the space name Space settings .

  • Under the “Access” section, select a space access level:

    • Private: Users can’t find or join this space unless you add them.
    • Discoverable: Anyone in your organization can find the space.
    • Open: Anyone in your organization can find and join the space and preview messages.

  • If your space is private, discoverable, or open to a group of users that is smaller than your entire organization, you can choose whether users are allowed to request to join the space.

  • Click Save. If you have multiple target audiences:

  • Next to “Advanced access settings,” click Advanced .

  • Select who can join and who can find your space.

    • You can add only one audience in the “Who can join” field and multiple audiences in the “Who can find” field.

  • Turn Request to join on or off.

  • Click Done. Tip: If you already allow people outside your organization to join the space, you can’t make the space discoverable or open to others.

Update permissions for a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, select a space.
  • At the top, click the space name Space settings .
  • Under the “Permissions” section, select whether all members, managers and owners, or owners only, can:
    • Modify space board and details
    • Turn history on or off
    • Use @all
    • Manage apps
    • Manage webhooks
  • Click Save.

Manage view members permissions in Google Chat

The view members setting determines who accesses the member list in a space. Space owners and managers can manage this setting and can tailor visibility based on the space’s purpose and sensitivity. Restricting member visibility doesn’t limit the total member count displayed and doesn’t hide who sends messages in the space.

About view members settings

Options for the view members setting include:

  • Owners: Only space owners can access the member list.
  • Owners and managers: Both space owners and managers can access the member list.
  • All members: All members of the space can access the member list. This is the default setting for most spaces.
  • The entire organization: Anyone in your organization can access the member list. This applies even if they are not a space member.
    • Important: This option is available only if the space is discoverable to the entire organization. If shared with a different target audience, the maximum view members setting is “All members.”

Change view members permissions

Space owners and managers can adjust who can see the member list in Google Chat.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • Select the space where you want to change permissions.
  • At the top of the space, select the space name.
  • Scroll down and select Space settings.
  • Choose a view members setting Save.

Review view members restrictions

Review these details before adjusting the view members setting, as changing it can affect space functionality and member experience.

Important:

  • If you can’t view members, you can’t assign tasks to others; only to yourself.
  • If you can’t view members, any use of @mentions will show a “user can’t be added” error to ensure memberships stay private.
  • The “Manage members” permission cannot exceed the “View members” setting. If you reduce member visibility, manage member permissions adjust accordingly.
  • To protect privacy, system messages announcing new member additions are hidden if member visibility is restricted.

Related resources

  • Add or remove people from a space
  • Manage space settings

Search for a space

You can use search to find spaces in Google Chat you’re interested in or have been invited to.

Search for a space in Chat or Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Enter the name of the space that you want to find.
  • Click the space name or View.
    • If the space is open, click Join. You can also preview the messages.
    • If the space is private or discoverable and the space allows it, you can submit a request to join. Learn how to join a space in Google Chat.

Summarize chats in Google Chat

If you’re a Google Workspace user, conversation summaries are now automatically available by default in spaces with many read and unread messages. Some users can use Gemini to request summaries for read and unread conversations in Home.

Use Gemini summaries for read & unread conversations

Important:

  • This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace subscription. Learn about Gemini features and plans.

  • This feature is available in select supported languages. Learn about supported languages for summaries in home. You can use Gemini to show summaries for read and unread conversations that include 1:1 direct messages, group direct messages, spaces, and threads. Summaries aren’t available for:

  • Messages with apps

  • Conversations with history turned off Tip: To enable conversation and space summaries in Home, turn on smart features in Gmail.

Summarize read & unread conversations in Home

You can choose to summarize a specific read and unread conversation in Home.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Chat in Gmail.
  • Hover over the conversation you want to summarize in Home.
  • Click Summarize.
Summarize unread messages in a conversation
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat .
  • Choose a conversation with unread messages to summarize.
  • Click Summarize unread.
    • Under the “Recent discussions” section, you can find a summary list of your recent unread messages.
  • Click Close summary.

Give feedback about Gemini conversation summaries

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request. Because feedback may be human readable, please do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can submit feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

  • At the bottom of the generated output, click Good suggestion or Bad suggestion .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, including additional context and outputs. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
    • If you select Bad suggestion , select Next to select the issue you found and enter additional feedback.
  • Click Submit. To provide general feedback on this feature, at the top, go to Help Send feedback to Google. Learn more about sending feedback in Chat.

To report a legal issue, create a request.

  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.

Use threads in Chat

In addition to the main conversation in the space, you can reply to any message and create a separate thread. With a thread, you can track important discussions and prevent the main conversation from being cluttered.

Google Chat: In-line threading

Learn how threads work in Chat

To create a single, streamlined flow of conversation in Google Chat, use threads for conversation. In a thread, you can either:

  • Send a message to the entire group in the main conversation window.

  • Quote a previous message.

  • Reply to a single message to start a thread.

    • If you use threads to reply to a single message, your message branches into a separate conversation with up to 500 replies. A conversation with threads allows users to:

  • Follow specific threads and receive notifications for replies and mentions in the thread.

  • Find out who replies to a thread. Each thread shows avatars of users that reply to the thread. Find the number of unread thread updates:

  • For followed threads: Check the number on the Threads icon .

  • In the main conversation stream: The number of unread replies is underneath the initial message. Note: A special thread icon badge may also appear on bolded conversations when there is only followed thread activity in that conversation.

Reply in a thread

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Select a conversation.

  • Point to the message.

  • In the menu, click Reply in thread .

  • In the thread panel, to the right of the conversation, enter your message.

  • Click Send . Tips:

  • To open the thread panel for a thread with replies, click below the message where it says “X replies.”

  • To resize the thread panel, click and drag the bar on the left border of the panel.

Follow or unfollow a thread

  • At the top right corner of the conversation, click Threads .
    • Note: The icon may also show the number of unread followed threads.
  • In the thread panel, choose:
    • To follow a thread: Click Follow.
    • To unfollow a thread: Click Following. Tip: The Unread and Following filters apply automatically when the threads panel opens initially; if you update the filters, they will apply to all conversations on your device.

A thread is automatically followed if:

  • You’re the author of the main message that initiates the thread.
  • You reply via thread or were mentioned.
  • You set the notification setting of a specific conversation to notify for “All.”

Manage thread notifications

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • At the top of the conversation, click the conversation Notifications.
  • Select an option for notifications:
    • All: Notifications for all new messages and replies to threads.
      • If you select “All,” you automatically follow all new threads for that conversation.
      • To unfollow a thread, click Threads Following.
    • Main conversations: Notifications for all new main conversations, @mentions, and replies to threads you follow.
    • For you: Notifications for @mentions and replies to threads you follow.
    • None: No notifications, just an indicator for @mentions.
  • Optional: If you don’t want the conversation to be in bold and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”
  • Click Save. Tip: In your conversation list, you may see or a blue dot that indicates an unread message in a thread you follow.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

  • At the top right corner of the conversation, select Threads . Tips: When the threads panel opens, the Unread and Following filters apply automatically. You can also filter for threads where you are mentioned by clicking “Mentions me.”

Gemini in Chat

Collaborate with Gemini in Google Chat

Feature availability:

  • If you have access to Ask Gemini in Google Chat, you can access Gemini collaboration capabilities with Ask Gemini. Learn more about Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • If you have an eligible Google Workspace edition and have access to Ask Gemini, you can also access Gemini in Google Chat. Learn about Gemini features and plans. Note: If you have access to Ask Gemini in Chat, the side panel feature is removed.

Supported languages:

Learn about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.

Get started with Gemini in Chat

To summarize, generate action items, or answer questions about any space or conversation, use Gemini in Chat.

  • On your computer, go to chat.google.com.

    • Open the Chat standalone app or Chat in Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .

    • Learn more about things to ask Gemini in Chat. Select a suggestion

  • Select from the list of suggestions.

    • To get more options, select More suggestions.

  • At the bottom, in the prompt box, replace the example text with the information that you want.

  • Click Enter. Enter a prompt in Gemini

  • At the bottom, in the prompt box, enter a prompt.

  • Click Enter. Tips:

  • You can lose your conversation history when:

    • You refresh your browser.
    • You close and reopen Chat.
    • Your computer goes offline.

  • To remove your conversation history, click More options Clear history.

Things to ask Gemini in Chat

While using Gemini in Chat, you can use Gemini to summarize, list action items, or answer specific questions about a conversation. In the side panel, you can use a prompt to collaborate with Gemini in Chat.

Answer questions about any conversation

While using Gemini in Chat, you can ask Gemini to search through your entire chat history to answer questions about a conversation.

  • In the side panel, you can ask specific questions about conversations from your chat history and find citations.
    • Examples:
      • “What did [leader name] announce to the team yesterday?”
      • “What’s the decision on the project discussed in this conversation?” Summarize a conversation

While using Gemini in Chat, you can use Gemini to search through your entire chat history to summarize a conversation.

  • In the side panel, you can prompt to ask for a summary or to summarize action items from your chat history.​
    • Examples:
      • “Summarize my unread messages.”
      • “What are the key takeaways in this conversation?”
      • After an initial summary is generated, you can ask for a longer summary, “Give me a detailed summary of [topic] discussed in this space.” Summarize a file

You can use Gemini to summarize a file within a conversation if:

  • A message isn’t blocked.

  • File types shared as Drive links in Google Chat are:

    • Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides
    • .pdf
    • .csv
    • .txt
    • Zip files
    • Microsoft Office formats, like:
      • .docx (Word)
      • .xlsx (Excel)
      • .pptx (PowerPoint)

  • Download restrictions are off for the file. To summarize a file:

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Select a direct message or space with a file in the conversation.

  • Under the file, click Summarize this file. List action items

While using Gemini in Chat, you can use Gemini to list action items from any conversation.

  • In the side panel, you can prompt to ask for a list of action items.
    • Examples:
      • “What are the action items in this conversation?”
      • “Are there any action items for me?”
      • “Summarize [person’s] action items”

Download your conversation history

You can access and export your side panel chat history using Google Takeout, even if you don’t have access to side panel in Google Chat.

  • Go to takeout.google.com.
  • Sign in to your Google Account.
  • On the Google Takeout page, under “Select data to include,” select Gemini in Workspace.
    • Note: Chat side panel data is included in “Gemini in Workspace” data, not under “Chat.”
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete your export.
    • If you are unable to export your data, you may need to contact your administrator. Learn more about how to export your data. Important:
  • Your data from most Google products and services is included in the export by default. This includes your Gemini in Workspace data. Learn how to download your Workspace data using Takeout.
  • Downloading your Gemini in Workspace conversation history doesn’t delete it from Google’s servers.

Give feedback on generated output

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request. Because feedback may be human readable, please do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can submit feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

  • Below the generated output, select Good suggestion or Bad suggestion .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, including prompts, additional context, and outputs. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
    • If you select Bad suggestion , select Next to select the issue you found and enter additional feedback.
  • Select Submit. To provide general feedback about Gemini, at the top, click Help Send feedback to Google.

To report a legal issue, create a request.

Learn about Gemini feature suggestions

  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.
  • Your conversations with Gemini in Chat are not saved to Gemini Activity. When you delete your Gemini in Chat conversation history, it doesn’t delete any information that is saved to your Gemini Activity. Learn how to delete your Gemini Activity.

Customize Gemini in Workspace’s responses with your instructions

Important: Instructions for Gemini in Google Workspace are separate from and do not sync with instructions in Gemini Apps. Learn about instructions for Gemini Apps.

When you add instructions in your personalization settings, you can get tailored, relevant responses in:

  • Chat

  • Docs

  • Drive

  • Gmail

  • Slides For example, when you add instructions, Gemini can adapt its response to your:

  • Role: “When helping me write lesson plans, remember the class is high-school level.”

  • Preferred tone: “Remember to use a professional but enthusiastic tone for my document.”

  • Content: “Always include cost estimations when helping me write a proposal.”

  • Format: “Always summarize my files in bullet points.”

What you need

  • For personal Google Accounts:
    • You must have an eligible Google AI plan:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • You can also use personalization settings if your account is enrolled in Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts: You need an eligible Google Workspace plan. Learn more about Gemini features and plans.

How instructions work

  • Instructions are on by default in your personalization settings. You can turn them off at any time.
  • Instructions are shared across eligible Workspace products. For example, if you add instructions in Gemini in Gmail, it carries over to Gemini in Docs, Gemini in Slides, and others.
  • You can add up to 1,000 instructions.
  • To check if your instructions are used in a response:
    • Below the response, select Sources.
    • Under “Personalization settings,” find your instructions. Learn how to use sources with Google Workspace with Gemini.

Add instructions for Gemini

Add instructions when you chat with Gemini

When you use instructional phrases, Gemini automatically saves the instruction to your settings. For example, you can say:

  • “From now on, always use short sentences in your responses.”
  • “In the future, remember that I prefer summaries in a list format.” Add instructions in your personalization settings

  • Select Save.

Turn your instructions on or off

Get meeting recaps with Gemini in Google Chat

What you need

To receive meeting recaps with Gemini, turn on Google Workspace smart features. Learn about smart features & controls for Google products.

Get meeting recaps in Google Chat

You can use Gemini with meeting recaps in Google Chat to easily follow up with decisions and action items after meetings.

If “Take notes for me” is started during the meeting and there’s a chat message, you’ll get a recap that includes:

  • The meeting summary with highlights
  • Suggested next steps for after the meeting
  • Links to shared documents or files Tip: A recap won’t be posted if “Send notes to” in Meet is set to “Hosts and co-hosts only.”
Find your meeting recaps

Meeting recaps appear automatically in the meeting’s group chat once the meeting ends.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat .
  • Go to the meeting conversation.
  • At the end of the message history, you can find a card with the recap.
    • To delete the recap, at the top right, click More Delete . Tips:
  • Anyone can delete the recap.
  • If you delete the recap, the Gemini notes doc remains in Google Drive but the meeting summary in the chat is lost permanently.

Give feedback about Gemini meeting recaps

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can let us know by submitting feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

Because feedback may be human readable, do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

  • At the top right of the generated output, click Good summary or Bad summary .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, with additional context and output. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
    • If you select Bad summary : To select the issue and enter additional feedback, click Next.
  • Click Submit. To provide general feedback on this feature, at the top, click Help Send feedback to Google Chat. Learn how to send feedback in Google Chat.

Get started with Ask Gemini in Google Chat

Feature availability

  • This feature is currently only available in English and requires an eligible Google Workspace subscription. Learn about Gemini features and plans.
  • Learn about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.
  • You may not have access to some or all of the Ask Gemini features.
    • Note: Ask Gemini requires Gemini in Workspace in Chat and Workspace Intelligence to be turned on at the admin level for all apps. You can manage your day and find information more efficiently with Ask Gemini in Google Chat. This AI-powered assistant:
  • Finds quick answers from scattered information across your Google Workspace data
  • Summarizes updates on key topics across Chat spaces
  • Identifies daily priorities
  • Can share context or talk about a chat message you forwarded to it Important: To use these features, you must enroll in Workspace Smart Features. Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products.

In this article, learn how to:

  • Find Ask Gemini
  • Use Sessions in Ask Gemini
  • Use Ask Gemini to get daily briefs
  • Use Ask Gemini to answer specific questions
    • Search across the web or across Google Workspace data like Gmail, Google Drive, or Google Calendar.
  • Use Ask Gemini to prepare for your day
  • Use Ask Gemini to draft communications
  • Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Docs document
  • Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Slides presentation
  • Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Sheets spreadsheet
  • Use Ask Gemini to manage Drive files
  • Use Ask Gemini to manage tasks & show suggested to-dos
  • Use Ask Gemini to generate images
  • Use Ask Gemini to generate catch up summaries
  • Use Ask Gemini to schedule, manage, or find events
  • Use Ask Gemini to do deep research
  • Use Ask Gemini to invoke skills
  • Use Ask Gemini with third-party integrations

Find Ask Gemini

You can connect with Gemini in Chat in a few different ways.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Find Ask Gemini . Where to find Ask Gemini in Chat

Steps

Shortcuts or Conversation list

On the left, under “Shortcuts,” click Ask Gemini .

Keyboard shortcut

  • ChromeOS and Windows: Ctrl + g
  • macOS: Command + g Search bar

To the right of the search bar, click the Ask Gemini button.

Use Ask Gemini to start and use Sessions

You can manage your conversations with Ask Gemini by starting new sessions to keep discussions focused on single topics. Sessions help organize your interactions and improve the clarity of Gemini’s responses.

To start or open a session:

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • To start a new session:
    • In the message field, enter a new question or prompt.
    • Select one of the suggested topics displayed at the top of the chat interface.
  • To open a past session: Select the desired session from your recent conversations. When a session opens, all chats from that conversation will be displayed and stored together.

Use Ask Gemini to get daily briefs

You can get summaries of your day’s to-do items and things to follow up on from Ask Gemini that are sent to you automatically. This feature is on by default.

Tip: This feature is available through Gemini Alpha (for work accounts only, and enabled by your organization), and Google Workspace Experiments. The Google Workspace Experiments is a trusted tester program that users with personal accounts can use to try new AI features. Learn more about Google Workspace Experiments.

To access your daily brief:

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • Locate the most recent session called “Daily brief” from Ask Gemini. Your daily brief will appear with the date, a summary of your daily tasks and events, and links to related resources.
    • Note: You can access your daily brief from the Chat home screen, the Ask Gemini conversation thread, or the Ask Gemini home screen within Chat.
  • Optional: To unsubscribe from daily briefs, follow the prompt at the bottom of a brief.

Use Ask Gemini to answer specific questions

You can find information and get a unified knowledge base across the entire workspace or search the web with Ask Gemini. Since Gemini keeps your context across conversations, you don’t need to provide specific details every time you ask questions.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Find me the deck about [Project Name] that [Person’s Name] shared with me last week.”
    • “Give me the latest update on [Example Topic].”
    • “What did [Person’s Name] ask me last week about [Example Topic] and when am I meeting them next?”
  • Click Send . Tip: We include citations to note the source of the Ask Gemini’s information.

Use Ask Gemini to prepare for your day

You can ask Gemini for your action items at any time, and it’s based on the most recent information.

To ask for your action items:

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example, “What are my action items?”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to draft communications

You can use Ask Gemini to draft email or chat responses.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Draft an email to [Person’s Name] summarizing our progress on [Topic Name].”
    • “Refine the following chat message I am sending to [Person’s Name]: [Paste your draft here]. Make sure it’s professional and concise.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Docs document

You can use Ask Gemini to create a Google Docs document.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Create a meeting notes agenda.”
    • “Generate a draft with a response to this email.”
    • “Create a quick project coordination doc with a 30/60/90 plan section.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Slides presentation

You can use Ask Gemini to create a fully editable presentation in Google Slides with a single prompt.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, describe the presentation you want to create. For example: “Create a slide on quantum computing for a general audience with a modern design.”
  • Optional: To give your presentation the same style as an existing slide deck, you can use @<presentation name> to reference it. For example: “Create a presentation based on @old_project.”
  • Click Send .
    • Tip: Keep the tab open until Gemini generates your presentation; this may take up to several minutes. You can switch to other tabs or windows but do not close the existing tab.
  • To refine your presentation plan, you can answer Gemini’s follow-up questions. You may also find recommended sources that you can add for Gemini to use as it generates your presentation.
  • Click Next.
    • Keep the tab open until Gemini generates your presentation, which may take up to several minutes. You can switch to other tabs or windows, but do not close the existing tab.
    • Once the presentation is generated, you can open it in Google Slides to view and edit. Learn how to generate presentations with Gemini in Google Slides.

Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Sheets spreadsheet

You can use Ask Gemini to create a Google Sheets spreadsheet.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, describe the spreadsheet you want to build. For example:
    • “Create a sheet to track my monthly expenses with columns for date, category, amount, and notes.”
    • “Create a table for a project tracker in Google Sheets with columns for task, assignee, deadline, and status.”
    • “Create a 10-day itinerary for a first-time visitor covering Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka.”
    • “Create a visual dashboard in Sheets of this sales data.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to manage tasks & show suggested to-dos

You can use Ask Gemini to create and manage tasks and ask questions about your tasks. This includes suggested to-dos from chats and emails that need your attention.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “What tasks do I need to do today?”
    • “Add a task to complete the project proposal today.”
    • “Change the date of that task to tomorrow instead.”
    • “Mark the Friday workout task as complete.”
    • “Delete that last task.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate images

You can use Ask Gemini to create an image from within Chat. The image can have any specific style, setting, or subject.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Generate an image of a futuristic workspace in an ultra-realistic style.”
    • “Create an image showing the team welcoming our new sales lead.”
    • “Create a colorful icon for [Project Name].”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate catch up summaries

You can use Ask Gemini to help you catch up on specific topics, unread messages, and emails.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “What did I miss on [date or topic]?”
    • “Summarize some of the latest updates in [Space Name].”
    • “Catch me up on unread messages.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to schedule, manage, or find events

You can use Ask Gemini to schedule events, reschedule or delete existing events, find open time slots, or check calendars for availability.

Important: You can only create events on your primary calendar.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Create a 30 minute meeting with [Person’s Name] this week.”
    • “Schedule 1 hour of focus time for me this week.”
    • “Reschedule meeting with [Person’s Name] to next week.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini with third-party integrations

Important: Before you begin, you may need to ask your administrator to install the third-party integrations from the Google Workspace Marketplace.

You can use Ask Gemini to connect with third-party apps to manage tasks, find information, and automate workflows across Google Workspace and external tools.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .

    • Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • In the message field, type @ followed by the third-party integration name. For example, “@HubSpot,” “@Asana,” “@Salesforce.”

    • Or, you can enter the full name of the app in your prompt without the use of @.

  • Enter your prompt. For example:

    • “Summarize my Asana tickets.”
    • “@Salesforce find customer information for [Customer Name].”
    • “@Hubspot create a new lead for [Lead details].” or “Create a new lead for [Lead details] in Hubspot.”

  • Click Send . Tips:

  • Ask Gemini only connects to the third-party integrations you have successfully connected in the Google Workspace Marketplace. If you encounter an authorization error, you must authorize the app through the Google Workspace Marketplace.

  • When you use Ask Gemini, it cites the third-party app as a source for the information it provides. It often includes a link to the source in the app.

Use Ask Gemini to invoke skills

Important: Before you can use a skill in Chat, you must create the skill and turn it on in Workspace Studio.

To analyze chat conversations, use skills in Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
    • Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, type @ followed by the skill name. For example, “@Project Summary.”
  • Enter your prompt.
  • Click Send . Key use case: To analyze recent chat conversations within a particular chat space and generate a structured status update, use a “Project Summary” skill.

Use Ask Gemini to use Deep Research

You can use Ask Gemini to run complex, multi-step research tasks about any topic. Gemini synthesizes information from the web and any sources you include to create comprehensive research reports with cited sources. Learn more about Deep Research in Gemini.

Start a Deep Research report

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. Explain what you want to research. For example, “Deep research: Research current renewable energy trends and compare them with my project drafts in Google Drive.”
  • Click Send . Add sources and review your research plan

After you submit your prompt, a “Deep research sources” card shows in your chat. Ask Gemini uses these sources to base its research.

  • In the “Deep research sources” card, select one or more options:

    • Drive: Analyze files and folders in your Google Drive.
    • Gmail: Include info from your emails.
    • Chat: Include info from your chat messages.
    • Web: Search the public web for the latest info.

  • Optional: To choose specific sources for your research, click Add sources and select files from your Google Drive.

  • Click Next.

    • Ask Gemini creates a research plan for your topic with the questions the report aims to answer.
    • To update the research plan before you create a report, click Customize.

  • Click Start research. Track your research

  • While you work, Ask Gemini researches your topic based on the plan.

  • It can take some time to generate your report. You can close Ask Gemini, start a new chat, or switch to a different Google Workspace document. The research task continues in the background.

  • When the research is complete:

    • Ask Gemini generates the report in a Google Docs document.
    • You get an email about your plan’s completion. Open your report

  • In your conversation with Ask Gemini, click Open doc.

    • A new Google Docs document opens in a new tab.
    • It includes the findings, citations, and an organized summary of the data found.
    • The report automatically saves to your Google Drive.

  • In the document, you can ask follow-up questions about the report.

    • You can also use Ask Gemini to refine specific sections.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can let us know by submitting feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

Because feedback may be human readable, do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

  • Below the generated output, select Good suggestion or Bad suggestion .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, which includes prompts, additional context, and outputs. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
  • Select Submit. To provide general feedback about Google Chat, at the top, click Help Send feedback to Google.

To report a legal issue, create a request.
