  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • To start a new session:
    • In the message field, enter a new question or prompt.
    • Select one of the suggested topics displayed at the top of the chat interface.
  • To open a past session: Select the desired session from your recent conversations. When a session opens, all chats from that conversation will be displayed and stored together.

Use Ask Gemini to get daily briefs

You can get summaries of your day’s to-do items and things to follow up on from Ask Gemini that are sent to you automatically. This feature is on by default.

Tip: This feature is available through Gemini Alpha (for work accounts only, and enabled by your organization), and Google Workspace Experiments. The Google Workspace Experiments is a trusted tester program that users with personal accounts can use to try new AI features. Learn more about Google Workspace Experiments.

To access your daily brief:

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • Locate the most recent session called “Daily brief” from Ask Gemini. Your daily brief will appear with the date, a summary of your daily tasks and events, and links to related resources.
    • Note: You can access your daily brief from the Chat home screen, the Ask Gemini conversation thread, or the Ask Gemini home screen within Chat.
  • Optional: To unsubscribe from daily briefs, follow the prompt at the bottom of a brief.

Use Ask Gemini to answer specific questions

You can find information and get a unified knowledge base across the entire workspace or search the web with Ask Gemini. Since Gemini keeps your context across conversations, you don’t need to provide specific details every time you ask questions.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Find me the deck about [Project Name] that [Person’s Name] shared with me last week.”
    • “Give me the latest update on [Example Topic].”
    • “What did [Person’s Name] ask me last week about [Example Topic] and when am I meeting them next?”
  • Click Send . Tip: We include citations to note the source of the Ask Gemini’s information.

Use Ask Gemini to prepare for your day

You can ask Gemini for your action items at any time, and it’s based on the most recent information.

To ask for your action items:

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example, “What are my action items?”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to draft communications

You can use Ask Gemini to draft email or chat responses.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Draft an email to [Person’s Name] summarizing our progress on [Topic Name].”
    • “Refine the following chat message I am sending to [Person’s Name]: [Paste your draft here]. Make sure it’s professional and concise.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Docs document

You can use Ask Gemini to create a Google Docs document.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Create a meeting notes agenda.”
    • “Generate a draft with a response to this email.”
    • “Create a quick project coordination doc with a 30/60/90 plan section.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Slides presentation

You can use Ask Gemini to create a fully editable presentation in Google Slides with a single prompt.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, describe the presentation you want to create. For example: “Create a slide on quantum computing for a general audience with a modern design.”
  • Optional: To give your presentation the same style as an existing slide deck, you can use @<presentation name> to reference it. For example: “Create a presentation based on @old_project.”
  • Click Send .
    • Tip: Keep the tab open until Gemini generates your presentation; this may take up to several minutes. You can switch to other tabs or windows but do not close the existing tab.
  • To refine your presentation plan, you can answer Gemini’s follow-up questions. You may also find recommended sources that you can add for Gemini to use as it generates your presentation.
  • Click Next.
    • Keep the tab open until Gemini generates your presentation, which may take up to several minutes. You can switch to other tabs or windows, but do not close the existing tab.
    • Once the presentation is generated, you can open it in Google Slides to view and edit. Learn how to generate presentations with Gemini in Google Slides.

Use Ask Gemini to generate a Google Sheets spreadsheet

You can use Ask Gemini to create a Google Sheets spreadsheet.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, describe the spreadsheet you want to build. For example:
    • “Create a sheet to track my monthly expenses with columns for date, category, amount, and notes.”
    • “Create a table for a project tracker in Google Sheets with columns for task, assignee, deadline, and status.”
    • “Create a 10-day itinerary for a first-time visitor covering Tokyo, Kyoto, and Osaka.”
    • “Create a visual dashboard in Sheets of this sales data.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to manage tasks & show suggested to-dos

You can use Ask Gemini to create and manage tasks and ask questions about your tasks. This includes suggested to-dos from chats and emails that need your attention.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “What tasks do I need to do today?”
    • “Add a task to complete the project proposal today.”
    • “Change the date of that task to tomorrow instead.”
    • “Mark the Friday workout task as complete.”
    • “Delete that last task.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate images

You can use Ask Gemini to create an image from within Chat. The image can have any specific style, setting, or subject.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Generate an image of a futuristic workspace in an ultra-realistic style.”
    • “Create an image showing the team welcoming our new sales lead.”
    • “Create a colorful icon for [Project Name].”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to generate catch up summaries

You can use Ask Gemini to help you catch up on specific topics, unread messages, and emails.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “What did I miss on [date or topic]?”
    • “Summarize some of the latest updates in [Space Name].”
    • “Catch me up on unread messages.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini to schedule, manage, or find events

You can use Ask Gemini to schedule events, reschedule or delete existing events, find open time slots, or check calendars for availability.

Important: You can only create events on your primary calendar.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. For example:
    • “Create a 30 minute meeting with [Person’s Name] this week.”
    • “Schedule 1 hour of focus time for me this week.”
    • “Reschedule meeting with [Person’s Name] to next week.”
  • Click Send .

Use Ask Gemini with third-party integrations

Important: Before you begin, you may need to ask your administrator to install the third-party integrations from the Google Workspace Marketplace.

You can use Ask Gemini to connect with third-party apps to manage tasks, find information, and automate workflows across Google Workspace and external tools.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .

    • Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • In the message field, type @ followed by the third-party integration name. For example, “@HubSpot,” “@Asana,” “@Salesforce.”

    • Or, you can enter the full name of the app in your prompt without the use of @.

  • Enter your prompt. For example:

    • “Summarize my Asana tickets.”
    • “@Salesforce find customer information for [Customer Name].”
    • “@Hubspot create a new lead for [Lead details].” or “Create a new lead for [Lead details] in Hubspot.”

  • Click Send . Tips:

  • Ask Gemini only connects to the third-party integrations you have successfully connected in the Google Workspace Marketplace. If you encounter an authorization error, you must authorize the app through the Google Workspace Marketplace.

  • When you use Ask Gemini, it cites the third-party app as a source for the information it provides. It often includes a link to the source in the app.

Use Ask Gemini to invoke skills

Important: Before you can use a skill in Chat, you must create the skill and turn it on in Workspace Studio.

To analyze chat conversations, use skills in Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
    • Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, type @ followed by the skill name. For example, “@Project Summary.”
  • Enter your prompt.
  • Click Send . Key use case: To analyze recent chat conversations within a particular chat space and generate a structured status update, use a “Project Summary” skill.

Use Ask Gemini to use Deep Research

You can use Ask Gemini to run complex, multi-step research tasks about any topic. Gemini synthesizes information from the web and any sources you include to create comprehensive research reports with cited sources. Learn more about Deep Research in Gemini.

Start a Deep Research report

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
  • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • In the message field, enter a prompt. Explain what you want to research. For example, “Deep research: Research current renewable energy trends and compare them with my project drafts in Google Drive.”
  • Click Send . Add sources and review your research plan

After you submit your prompt, a “Deep research sources” card shows in your chat. Ask Gemini uses these sources to base its research.

  • In the “Deep research sources” card, select one or more options:

    • Drive: Analyze files and folders in your Google Drive.
    • Gmail: Include info from your emails.
    • Chat: Include info from your chat messages.
    • Web: Search the public web for the latest info.

  • Optional: To choose specific sources for your research, click Add sources and select files from your Google Drive.

  • Click Next.

    • Ask Gemini creates a research plan for your topic with the questions the report aims to answer.
    • To update the research plan before you create a report, click Customize.

  • Click Start research. Track your research

  • While you work, Ask Gemini researches your topic based on the plan.

  • It can take some time to generate your report. You can close Ask Gemini, start a new chat, or switch to a different Google Workspace document. The research task continues in the background.

  • When the research is complete:

    • Ask Gemini generates the report in a Google Docs document.
    • You get an email about your plan’s completion. Open your report

  • In your conversation with Ask Gemini, click Open doc.

    • A new Google Docs document opens in a new tab.
    • It includes the findings, citations, and an organized summary of the data found.
    • The report automatically saves to your Google Drive.

  • In the document, you can ask follow-up questions about the report.

    • You can also use Ask Gemini to refine specific sections.

Give feedback about Ask Gemini

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can let us know by submitting feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

Because feedback may be human readable, do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

  • Below the generated output, select Good suggestion or Bad suggestion .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, which includes prompts, additional context, and outputs. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
  • Select Submit. To provide general feedback about Google Chat, at the top, click Help Send feedback to Google.

To report a legal issue, create a request.

Learn about Gemini feature suggestions

  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.

What you need to use Google Workspace with Gemini

  • Be 18 or over.
  • An eligible Google Account:
    • If you have a work or school Google Account, you can get access to AI-powered features with an eligible Google Workspace plan.
    • If you have a personal Google Account, you can get access to AI-powered features with:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra Additional requirements
  • Some AI features may not be available in your language. If you can’t use a feature in your language, you can switch to a supported language in your Google Account. Learn more about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini.
  • If you have a personal Google Account, you can use these Gemini in Gmail features at no charge in the US:
    • Help me write
    • AI Overviews for email threads
    • Suggested Replies

Feature

Description

AI Inbox

Review top priorities and topics to catch up on from your inbox.

Generate a concise summary or answer from your emails directly above search results when you ask a natural language question.

Gmail Live

Use your voice to search and ask questions about your emails in the Gmail app.

Help me schedule

Propose times to meet in an email to someone else.

Help me write

Draft new emails or refine existing text based on a prompt.

Proofread

Get writing suggestions beyond spelling and grammar for conciseness, tone, and style.

Suggested replies

Gemini Apps

Frequently asked questions

How does Google protect my data?

The addition of these AI features includes the same robust data protection and security standards that come with all Google Workspace services:

  • Users get enterprise-grade data protections when they use the Gemini app. Submissions aren’t reviewed by humans or otherwise used to train models.
  • Your interactions with Gemini in Google Workspace apps stay within your organization. Prompts and content you generate with these features is stored alongside your Workspace content and is never shared outside your organization.
  • Your existing Google Workspace protections are automatically applied. These AI features bring the same enterprise-grade security as the rest of Google Workspace, automatically applying your organization’s existing controls and data handling practices, such as data-regions policies and Data Loss Prevention.
  • Your content is not used for any other customers. None of your content is used for model training outside of your domain without permission. Learn how Google Workspace keeps your data secure and prioritizes privacy.

If you have a Google AI plan, learn how Gemini protects your data.

Can I control access to these AI features?

You have the option to turn off some AI features. Learn how to turn Google Workspace smart features on or off.

In addition, if you have a work or school account, your administrator can also:

  • Turn off access to the Gemini App.
  • Turn off Gemini Notebook as an additional service.
  • Stop users from letting Google AI take notes in meetings. Your existing Google Workspace data protections are automatically applied to AI features.

If you have a Google AI plan, learn how Gemini protects your data.

Are there tips for using Gemini effectively?

You can help improve your success with Gemini with these basic best practices:

  • Learn how to write good prompts for Gemini.
  • Use this cheat sheet for an overview of Gemini features.

Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Vids & Pics protects your data

Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance.

Our privacy commitments to all Workspace users

Generative AI does not change our foundational privacy protections for giving users choice and control over their data. To that end, here are key facts about how Workspace data is handled.

  • Your data is your data. The content that you put into Google Workspace services (emails, documents, etc.) is yours. We never sell your data, and you can delete your content or export it.
  • Your data stays in Workspace by default. We do not use your Workspace data to train or improve the underlying generative AI and large language models that power Gemini, Search, and other systems outside of Workspace without permission.
  • Your privacy is protected. Interactions with intelligent Workspace features, such as accepting or rejecting spelling suggestions, or reporting spam, are anonymized and/or aggregated and may be used to improve or develop helpful Workspace features like spam protection, spell check, and autocomplete. These Workspace features are developed with strict privacy protections that keep users in control.
  • Your content is not used for ads targeting in Google Workspace. Google Workspace does not collect, scan, or use your content for advertising purposes. Important: If you’re a Workspace user with a personal account and you choose to share data, including your Workspace data, with Gemini Apps or Search services for Personal Intelligence, or through screen actions (including screenshots), this data will be processed according to their respective terms and policies, and may be used for model training and improvement. Learn more in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub or the Search services Frequently Asked Questions.

These are the privacy commitments that Workspace extends to all of its users. But they aren’t just words. To ensure we continually meet these high standards, independent auditors validate our practices against international standards and best practices.

Specific commitments for Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids & Pics

For users with Google AI plans, when using Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics, your data is yours and under your control. Whether you ask Gemini to summarize an email or document, write a blog post, or add a unique image to your slide:

  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics uses your content in Google Workspace to provide more useful responses to your prompts and doesn’t use your content to train or improve Gemini or other generative AI models.
  • Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics doesn’t store your prompt or the generated output without your permission. Note: For users enrolled in the Google Workspace Experiments program, use of Gemini in Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Slides, Sheets, Meet, Vids, and Pics is covered by the Google Workspace Experiments Privacy Notice & Terms for Personal Accounts.

Learn how to use Smart Actions in Google Chat

Feature availability

  • These features are available as part of the Gemini Beta.
  • Your administrator controls access to the Gemini Beta. If you can’t find these features, your administrator may not have Beta features enabled for your organization.
  • This feature is also available as part of our early access testing program, Google Workspace Experiments. Important: To use Gemini’s Smart Actions, you must have “Google Workspace smart features” turned on. Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products.

Use inline meeting intent & schedule meetings

If someone in a conversation asks for a time to meet, Gemini suggests a possible meeting time and can schedule on your behalf.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Hover over the underlined section of the message.
  • To confirm your suggested meeting:
    • To schedule the proposed meeting time and send an invite, click Send.
    • To edit the name, participants, or time in the Calendar Companion app, click Edit .
    • To view more suggested meeting times, click Help me schedule.

Turn off Smart Actions in Chat

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • In the “Message & Media” tab, turn off Smart Actions.
  • Click Save Changes.

Give feedback about Gemini in Chat for meetings

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can let us know by submitting feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

Because feedback may be human readable, do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

  • At the top right of the generated output, select Good summary or Bad summary .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, with additional context and output. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
    • If you select Bad summary : To select the issue and enter additional feedback, select Next.
  • Select Submit. To provide general feedback on this feature, select Help Send feedback to Google. Learn how to send feedback in Google Chat.

To report a legal issue, create a request.

Learn about Gemini feature suggestions

  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.

Use an AI Overview in Google Chat

Feature availability:

  • This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace subscription. Learn about Gemini features and plans.

  • This feature is only available in English. Learn about supported languages for Google Workspace with Gemini. To quickly find info from your Chat conversations, you can ask questions or enter keywords in the Chat search bar. Based on this, Chat generates an AI Overview that can:

  • Locate specific information or messages across your full Workspace profile.

  • Understand past discussions or outcomes mentioned.

  • Find attachments without extensive search.

Search your Google Chat conversations

Important:

  • If you use search operators, like is:unread or from:, you won’t get an AI Overview.

  • Search within any conversation or space doesn’t provide an AI Overview. To get an AI Overview in Google Chat:

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • In the search bar, enter keywords or a query. For example:

    • “What was the deadline for project X?”
    • “Find messages from Alice about the Q3 review.”
    • “Show me attachments from the design sprint space.”

  • Click Search .

    • Or, you can press Enter.

  • At the top of your search results, review the AI Overview. Tip: For the best AI Overview, provide as much detail as you can in your search description.

Expand or collapse an AI Overview

When you get a summary, you can expand or collapse the AI Overview.

  • To get the full summary, click Show more.
  • To collapse the overview, click Collapse .

Give feedback about an AI Overview in Google Chat

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can let us know by submitting feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

Because feedback may be human readable, do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

  • At the top right of the generated output, select Good summary or Bad summary .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, with additional context and output. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
    • If you select Bad summary : To select the issue and enter additional feedback, select Next.
  • Select Submit. To provide general feedback on this feature, select Help Send feedback to Google. Learn how to send feedback in Google Chat.

To report a legal issue, create a request.

  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.

  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.

Use Automatic Translation in Chat

Important: This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Learn about Gemini features and plans.

You can easily understand messages sent to you in Google Chat through Automatic Translation, which automatically converts messages to your preferred language set in your Google account settings. Learn how to change your language settings.

Tip: If you change your preferred language, it can take up to 24 hours for the feature to update.

Learn more about supported languages

You can use Automatic Translation in all languages available for the Neural Machine Translation model.

Turn on Automatic Translation in Chat or Chat in Gmail

After you turn on Automatic Translation, messages are automatically translated. To find the original untranslated content, click the toggle below the message. Translated messages are only visible to you.

In Google Chat:

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Message & Media .

  • Under “Automatic Translation,” check the box.

  • Click Done. In Gmail:

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab.

  • Go to Gmail settings

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Automatic Translation,” check the box.

  • Click Done. Tips:

  • On mobile: Unless you reinstall the app, the setting affects new messages but not the ones that already exist.

  • On the Web: Upon refresh, the setting affects messages that already exist.

  • If the message is short or the source language is unclear, Automatic Translation might not work.

Give feedback about a translation

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request.

If the generated translation is inaccurate or looks unsafe, you can let us know by submitting feedback:

  • At the top right, click Support Send feedback to Google. Learn how to send feedback in Chat.
  • To report a legal issue, create a request.

Use Deep Research in Gemini in Workspace apps

Important: You can also use Deep Research in Gemini Apps, though certain features may vary from Gemini in Workspace apps. Learn how to use Deep Research in Gemini Apps.

You can conduct in-depth and real-time research on most subjects with Deep Research in Gemini in Workspace. You can change or add other sources, like your personal Gmail or Drive, for your research.

You can use Deep Research for Gemini in:

  • Chat
  • Docs
  • Drive
  • Gmail
  • Sheets
  • Slides

What you need

  • For personal Google Accounts:
    • You need an eligible Google AI plan:
      • Google AI Plus
      • Google AI Pro
      • Google AI Ultra
    • You can also access Deep Research if your account is enrolled in Google Workspace Experiments, which is a trusted tester program to try new AI features. Learn how to get started with Google Workspace Experiments.
  • For work or school accounts: You need an eligible Google Workspace plan. Learn more about Gemini features and plans.

Start a Deep Research report

Start a Deep Research report in Chat

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .

    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • At the bottom, in the text box, enter a question or prompt that explains what you want to research. For example:

    • “Use Deep Research to examine current renewable energy trends and compare them with my project drafts in Drive.”
    • “Use Deep Research to recommend restaurants, attractions, and activities for my upcoming 7-day trip to Oslo, Norway.”

  • Click Send message . Start a Deep Research report in Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets, or Slides

  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.

  • On the right, click Ask Gemini .

  • At the bottom, click Tools Deep Research.

  • In the text box, enter a question or prompt that explains what you want to research. For example:

    • “Research current renewable energy trends and compare them with my project drafts in Drive.”
    • “Find recommended restaurants, attractions, and activities for my upcoming 7-day trip to Oslo, Norway.”

  • Click Submit .

Set up the Deep Report report

Step 1: Add sources & review your research plan

After you submit your prompt, you can choose sources to help inform your research.

  • In the sources card, select one or more options:

    • Drive: Analyze files and folders in your Google Drive.
    • Gmail: Include info from your emails.
    • Chat: Include info from your chat messages.
    • Web: Search the public web for the latest info.

  • Optional for Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets, and Slides: To choose specific sources for your research, click Add sources and select files from your Drive.

  • Click Next.

    • Gemini creates a research plan for your topic.
    • To update the research plan before you create a report, click Customize.

  • Click Start research. Step 2: Track your research

  • While you work, Gemini researches your topic based on the plan.

  • It can take some time to generate your report since Gemini analyzes many sources.

  • You can close Gemini, start a new chat, or switch to a different Workspace document. The research task continues to run in the background.

  • When the research is complete:

    • Gemini generates the report in a Google Doc.
    • You get an email about your plan’s completion. Step 3: Open your report

  • In your conversation with Gemini, click Open Doc.

    • A new Google Doc opens in a new tab.
    • It includes the findings, citations, and an organized summary of the data found.
    • The report automatically saves to your Drive.

  • In the document, ask Gemini follow-up questions about the report.

    • You can also ask Gemini to refine specific sections.

Find your Deep Research reports

Find your Deep Research reports in Chat

  • In Google Chat, open Ask Gemini .
    • Tip: Learn where to find Ask Gemini in Google Chat.
  • Under “Recent,” select your research conversation.
    • To find more conversations, click Show more. Find your Deep Research reports in Docs, Drive, Gmail, Sheets, or Slides
  • On your computer, open a Google Workspace app, like Gmail or Docs.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • At the top left, click More options .
  • Under “History,” find your research conversation.
    • To find more conversations, click View all. Tips:
  • Your conversations are organized by date, with the most recent at the top.
  • You can also find your research reports at drive.google.com.

Get started with Google Chat

Accessibility in Google Chat

Overview

You can use Google Chat with platform accessibility features and technologies, such as screen readers. It has several built-in accessibility features, like:

  • Keyboard shortcuts

  • Suggested replies

  • Spelling and grammar correction For best results, use the latest version of:

  • Chat

  • Browser

  • Operating system

  • Assistive technology

Vision

To interact with Chat with spoken feedback or Braille, use a screen reader to:

  • Describe Chat elements and content as you navigate.

  • Perform actions.

  • Inform you about alerts and notifications. Additionally, Chat has shortcuts to:

  • Navigate.

  • Search.

  • Reply to messages.

  • Announce recent messages in a conversation. For more information:

  • Learn how to use Google Chat with a screen reader.

  • Learn how to use Google Chat keyboard shortcuts. To customize the appearance of Chat, you have multiple options.

  • Learn how to update appearance in Google Chat.

  • Learn how to create & organize sections in Google Chat. For more information on low vision assistance available on your platform, refer to your platform’s related resources. Features include:

  • Screen reader

  • Screen magnification

  • Text scaling

  • Improve visibility of focus and cursor

  • Screen resolution

  • Color filter and contrast customization

  • Reading mode

  • Select to speak In addition to the platform features listed above, Chat also works with the latest version of these third-party assistive technologies for vision:

  • JAWS

  • NVDA

  • ZoomText

Hearing

While most chat conversations don’t include audio, it’s possible to start a video meeting or call someone. If you’re in a video meeting or a call, to follow the conversation, turn on captions.

  • In a video or audio call, click More options Settings.
  • Select Captions Live captions.
    • Or, to send text instead of speaking, select In call messages. Tips:
  • If all meeting participants understand sign language, there’s no need for captions or in call messages.
  • If someone sends a voice message instead of text, in the message, you can view a transcript. Learn how to send a voice message or view a transcript. For more information on routing platform audio to hearing aids, refer to your platform’s related resources.

Alternative input

You can use several powerful and useful shortcuts in Chat to:

  • Open a conversation.
  • Reply to a conversation.
  • Navigate to the sections for direct messages, spaces, and threads. For a list of shortcuts, visit Use Google Chat keyboard shortcuts.

If you want to reduce your keyboard input, you can:

  • Send a voice message.

  • Send a video message.

  • Start a video meeting or call someone. These optional smart features can improve the efficiency of all Chat users and help those who need to minimize mouse or keyboard input:

  • Smart Compose

  • Smart Reply

  • Auto-correct Chat supports platform features that can be helpful for those with motor disabilities or dexterity impairments:

  • Sticky keys, Filter keys, and Bounce keys

  • An on-screen keyboard, optionally with a switch device

  • Mouse keys

  • Eye or face tracking for mouse input

  • Voice input for:

    • Command
    • Control
    • Dictation For more information on these features, refer to your platform’s related resources.

Voice

While most Chat conversations don’t include audio, it’s possible to start a video meeting or call someone. If that happens, you can participate when you send:

  • Reactions
  • “In call messages”
    • To send, click More options In call messages. If you use an electrolarynx, we recommend you turn off the noise cancellation.
  • In a video or audio call, click More options Settings .
  • Turn off Noise cancellation.

Cognition

Some people with processing disorders, distraction issues, or other cognitive challenges, need or want extensive hints, more information density, and attention grabbing UI to keep them on task. Others require a less complex UI with minimal distractions. Which is why Google Chat provides settings and features to address these issues with toggles to turn individual features on or off. Examples include:

  • UI density adjustment

  • Create & organize sections

  • Animation on/off/use system settings

  • Optional autocorrect

  • Optional Smart compose that can learn from you

  • Conversation summaries

  • Configure desktop notifications Additional features that can be useful include:

  • Animation toggle

  • Notification timeout and appearance

  • Select to speak To explore these features, refer to your platform’s related resources.

Explore accessibility in our products on the Google Accessibility site.

  • Google Accessibility Help Center
  • Google Accessibility Conformance Reports

  • Create a space
  • Accessibility on Chrome
  • Making Chromebooks accessible
  • Turn on Chromebook accessibility features

While most chat conversations don’t include audio, it’s possible to start a video meeting or call someone. If you’re in a video meeting or a call, to follow the conversation, turn on captions.

  • In a video or audio call, click More options Settings.
  • Select Captions Live captions.
    • Or, to send text instead of speaking, select In call messages. Tips:
  • If all meeting participants understand sign language, there’s no need for captions or in call messages.
  • If someone sends a voice message instead of text, in the message, you can view a transcript. Learn how to send a voice message or view a transcript. For more information on routing platform audio to hearing aids, refer to your platform’s related resources.

Alternative input

You can use several powerful and useful shortcuts in Chat to:

  • Open a conversation.
  • Reply to a conversation.
  • Navigate to the sections for direct messages, spaces, and threads. For a list of shortcuts, visit Use Google Chat keyboard shortcuts.

If you want to reduce your keyboard input, you can:

  • Send a voice message.

  • Send a video message.

  • Start a video meeting or call someone. These optional smart features can improve the efficiency of all Chat users and help those who need to minimize mouse or keyboard input:

  • Smart Compose

  • Smart Reply

  • Auto-correct Chat supports platform features that can be helpful for those with motor disabilities or dexterity impairments:

  • Sticky keys, Filter keys, and Bounce keys

  • An on-screen keyboard, optionally with a switch device

  • Mouse keys

  • Eye or face tracking for mouse input

  • Voice input for:

    • Command
    • Control
    • Dictation For more information on these features, refer to your platform’s related resources.

Voice

While most Chat conversations don’t include audio, it’s possible to start a video meeting or call someone. If that happens, you can participate when you send:

  • Reactions
  • “In call messages”
    • To send, click More options In call messages. If you use an electrolarynx, we recommend you turn off the noise cancellation.
  • In a video or audio call, click More options Settings .
  • Turn off Noise cancellation.

Cognition

Some people with processing disorders, distraction issues, or other cognitive challenges, need or want extensive hints, more information density, and attention grabbing UI to keep them on task. Others require a less complex UI with minimal distractions. Which is why Google Chat provides settings and features to address these issues with toggles to turn individual features on or off. Examples include:

  • UI density adjustment

  • Create & organize sections

  • Animation on/off/use system settings

  • Optional autocorrect

  • Optional Smart compose that can learn from you

  • Conversation summaries

  • Configure desktop notifications Additional features that can be useful include:

  • Animation toggle

  • Notification timeout and appearance

  • Select to speak To explore these features, refer to your platform’s related resources.

Explore accessibility in our products on the Google Accessibility site.

Overview

You can use Google Chat with platform accessibility features and technologies, such as screen readers. It has several built-in accessibility features, like:

  • Keyboard shortcuts

  • Suggested replies

  • Spelling and grammar correction For best results, use the latest version of:

  • Chat

  • Browser

  • Operating system

  • Assistive technology

Vision

To interact with your device with touch and spoken feedback, turn on the VoiceOver screen reader. As you perform actions, VoiceOver describes Chat elements and content. It also informs you about alerts and notifications.

To customize the appearance of Chat, you have multiple options.

  • Learn how to update appearance in Google Chat.

  • Learn how to create & organize sections in Google Chat. If you need to adjust colors, you can use iPhone features like:

  • Dark mode

  • Color adjustments For more information on other low vision assistance, refer to Accessibility features on iPhone. Features include:

  • Screen magnification

  • Text scaling

  • Screen resolution

  • Select to speak

Hearing

While most chat conversations don’t include audio, it’s possible to start a video meeting or call someone. If you’re in a video meeting or a call, to follow the conversation, turn on captions.

  • In a video or audio call, tap More options Settings.
  • Select Captions Live captions.
  • Select Show captions.
    • Or, to send text instead of speaking, tap In call messages. Tip: If all meeting participants understand sign language, there’s no need for captions or in call messages.

Some accounts allow you to:

  • Send a voice message.
  • View a transcript of the message. For more information on how to route platform audio to hearing aids, refer to Accessibility features on iPhone.

Alternative input

If you want to reduce your keyboard input, you can:

  • Smart Compose

  • Smart Reply

  • Auto-correct These iPhone features for interaction and dexterity may be useful:

  • To navigate and interact with the Chat user interface, add a switch device.

  • To navigate without touch, use Eye Tracking.

  • To navigate and interact by voice, configure iPhone Voice Control.

  • Add a Touchpad and cursor to the Assistant menu.

  • Configure:

    • AssistiveTouch
    • Touch sensitivity
    • Duration settings

  • Add a physical keyboard with:

    • Sticky keys

    • Repeat keys For more information on platform settings for interaction or dexterity, refer to the accessibility features for mobility.

While most chat conversations don’t include audio, it’s possible to start a video meeting or call someone. If that happens you, you can participate when you send:

  • Reactions.
  • “In call messages”
    • To send, tap More options In call messages. If you use an electrolarynx, we recommend you turn off noise cancellation.
  • In a video or audio call, tap More options Settings .
  • Turn off Noise cancellation.

Cognition

Some people with processing disorders, distraction issues, or other cognitive challenges, need or want extensive hints, more information density, and attention grabbing UI to keep them on task. Others require a less complex UI with minimal distractions. Which is why Google Chat provides settings and features to address these issues with toggles to turn individual features on or off. Create & organize sections in Google Chat

To easily track your conversations, you can organize your direct messages and spaces into sections in Google Chat.

Create new sections

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Click and hold a conversation in the Chat navigation panel.
  • Drag and drop to the top of the conversation list .
  • Type the section name.
  • Click confirm . Tip: You can also hover over any section header, such as Direct messages or any custom section you created, click More Create new section.

Move a direct message or space to a section

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • In the navigation panel, click and hold a direct message or space drag to a new section. Tip: You can also drag and drop spaces or direct messages into sections.

Change display preferences

In sections, you can customize your display to:

  • Show all messages or unread messages only.
  • Adjust the number of spaces you can find in each section.
  • Resize the chat navigation panel horizontally.
Show all messages or unread messages only

For each custom section, you can turn sections on or off to Show all messages or Show unread messages .

Adjust section heights & placement
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • To adjust sizing for:
    • Section height: Drag a section.
      • Hover over the bottom of the section until a resize cursor appears.
      • Drag the resize cursor up or down.
    • Section placement: Click and hold a section name, then drag to its new location.
Sort alphabetically or by most recent
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Next to a section header, click More .
  • Select Sort by most recent or Sort alphabetically.
Resize the chat navigation panel
  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
    • If the navigation panel is hidden, at the top left, click Menu .
  • To adjust the chat roster horizontally, drag the bar left and right. Tip: This feature is only available in Google Chat on the web.

Create, send & reply to messages in Google Chat

You can send a direct message to a person or group of people in Google Chat.

Create a direct message

To send a new message:

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • At the top left, click New chat .
  • Enter the person’s name you want to message.
    • To create a group direct message, enter multiple names.
  • Click Start chat.

Send & reply to messages

To send or reply to a message, you can use the message field in Chat. There are multiple ways to reply.

When you reply, you can:

Send a message

Send the message you wrote in the message field.

Share files and more

Share Google Drive files, set up a Calendar invite, or add apps to a message.

Start a meeting

Start a video call with Google Meet.

Add a video meeting

Add a Google Meet link to a video meeting.

Edit a message

Edit a sent message.

Delete a message

Delete a sent message.

Format messages

Bold or italicize text, use bullet points, or add color.

React to messages

Add an emoji.

Upload a file

Share a file from your computer.

Share a GIF

React with an animated GIF.

Quote a message

To directly respond, quote a previous message in Chat.

Start a thread

In a space, create a new thread based on a message.

Troubleshoot permissions

Contact the Workspace administrator if you:

  • Can’t create a new conversation
  • Can’t add members to a space
  • Get a permission error like “You don’t have permission to start a new conversation” Learn how to manage space settings.

Schedule messages

You can write a message, then schedule it to be sent later.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Select a Space or Chat.
  • Type your message.
  • To the right of the “Send” arrow, click the Down arrow .
  • A pop-up appears with suggested send times, which includes the recipient’s time zone.
  • Select a suggested time or click Pick a custom time.
Confirm a scheduled message

After you schedule your message delivery, at the bottom of your chat, a banner appears. This confirms the message’s scheduled delivery time and recipient.

To find and manage all your scheduled messages, click See all scheduled messages.

Manage your scheduled messages

On the left navigation panel, in the “Drafts” tab, you can access and manage all your scheduled messages.

In “Drafts,” you can:

  • Find all your pending scheduled messages.
  • Get the send time in your time zone.
  • Get the send time in the receiver’s time zone.
  • Perform different actions on scheduled messages.
Perform actions on scheduled messages

In “Drafts,” you have full control over your scheduled messages. For each scheduled message, you can:

  • Edit message: Modify the content of a scheduled message.
  • Reschedule: Change the scheduled delivery time of a message.
  • Send immediately: Bypass the scheduled time and send the message immediately.
  • Delete: Remove a scheduled message.
Identify conversations with scheduled messages

A draft icon next to a conversation indicates that it contains either a draft or scheduled message.

Fix Google Chat errors

Important: If you can’t sign in to Gmail or Google Chat, go to Can’t sign in to your Google Account.

To resolve Google Chat errors, including those listed below, follow the troubleshooting steps in this page.

  • “Unable to load chat.”

  • “Trying to connect to chat.”

  • “Can’t connect to chat.”

  • “Can’t load the list of spaces. Try again in a minute.” If you can’t access or sign in to Google Chat, you can:

  • Check your network

  • Refresh Google Chat or Gmail

  • Check your browser

  • Uninstall browser extensions & apps

  • Check blocked domains & site permissions

Check your network

Make sure you have an active internet connection.

Refresh Google Chat

To refresh a tab or window, reload chat.google.com.

Check your browser

Make sure you use a supported browser. Chat in Gmail isn’t supported in mobile browsers or in Internet Explorer. You can download apps for:

  • Google Chat on iOS
  • Google Chat on Android

Uninstall browser extensions & apps

Some extensions and apps might block Google Chat from loading. To fix this issue, you can:

  • Uninstall active extensions.

  • Uninstall active apps.

  • Browse privately to avoid the use of extensions. Tips:

  • If you use a browser other than Chrome, check its support page for help.

  • Anti-virus software may prevent Google Chat from loading.

Check blocked domains & site permissions

Tips:

  • For work or school accounts, make sure your network administrator doesn’t block the browsers above. Learn how to change site settings permissions on Chrome.
  • If you use a browser other than Chrome, check its support page for help.

  • Learn how to manage space settings
  • Learn why you’re not getting Google Chat notifications
  • Learn why you can’t chat with someone

Install the Google Chat standalone app

For a simple way to use Google Chat, install the Google Chat standalone app in your Chrome Browser. This provides a streamlined Chat experience and is a Progressive Web Application (PWA) that you can open from your desktop.

Important: There’s no Google Chat Chrome extension. For a similar experience, install the app.

Check system requirements

To install the Chat standalone app, make sure:

  • Your device is running Google Chrome 73 or up.
    • Chrome doesn’t need to be your default browser, but it does need to be open to use the Chat standalone app.
  • You can install Chrome extensions and apps on your computer.
    • If you can’t complete the installation and you use a work or school account, contact your Google Workspace administrator.

Install the standalone app on your computer

  • Sign in to chat.google.com.
  • To install the app on your computer, try one of these methods:
    • At the top right of Google Chrome, in the URL bar, click Install Install.
    • At the top right of Google Chrome, click More Install Google Chat. Tip:
  • If you already created a Google Chrome shortcut to chat.google.com, the app automatically installs. You won’t have the option to manually install the app.

Open the standalone app

Once installed, you can open the standalone app from your desktop:

  • In ChromeOS, go to the Launcher Chat.
  • In Windows, click Start Chat.
  • In MacOS, go to the Applications folder Chat.
  • In a Chrome browser, in the address bar, enter chrome://apps and click Google Chat.

Open the standalone app automatically at startup

Important: These steps don’t work on Chrome OS.

  • On your computer, open Chrome.
  • In the address bar, enter chrome://apps.
  • Right-click on the Chat standalone app .
  • Select Launch at startup.

Uninstall the Chat standalone app

Uninstall the standalone app on Mac, Windows, or Linux

  • On your computer, open Chrome.

  • In the address bar, enter chrome://apps.

  • Right-click on the Chat standalone app .

  • Select Uninstall Remove. Uninstall the standalone app on Chrome OS

  • On your computer, open Launcher .

  • In the search bar, search for Google Chat.

  • In the search results, right-click on the Chat standalone app .

  • Click Remove from Chrome Remove.

Use the chat navigation panel to:

  • Send direct messages to one person or group direct messages
  • Create virtual spaces for team projects
  • Find direct messages and spaces

Navigate around Chat

In the navigation panel, you can:

Start a new chat

To open a direct message (DM) or a space to collaborate on projects, click New chat .

Catch up on your conversations

Find all your spaces and messages in Home . At the top right of Home, you can customize settings.

  • To find threads on your home screen, click Thread .
  • To find all unread messages on your home screen, turn on Unread .
  • To open selected DMs or spaces in a new panel on your home screen, at the top right, toggle Split pane mode . Find all messages in which you’re tagged

Under “Shortcuts,” click Mentions .

Find messages that you starred

Under “Shortcuts,” click Starred .

Below the shortcuts, you can find all your direct messages (DMs) and spaces. In the left-hand menu, you can choose from:

Shortcuts

Get quick access to:

- Find all of your conversations:
    - Toggle between all or unread conversations.
    - Select to display all conversations or threads.
- To open selected DMs or spaces in a new panel without leaving "Home," toggle Split pane mode.
  • Mentions: Find all messages where someone directly mentions you.
  • Starred: Track important messages that you’ve starred. Direct messages

Find all DMs between you and others. You can send a DM to one or more people.

Sections

Find all of your:

  • Spaces and apps organized by section.
  • DMs that you moved into a custom section.

Related resources

  • Send a message in Google Chat
  • Reply to a chat message in Google Chat
  • Create a space
  • Search for Google Chat messages

Personalize your Google Chat display settings (Computer)

To personalize your experience in Google Chat, you can select your color, mode, and density settings.

Change the appearance of Chat

Important: These appearance settings apply for chat.google.com and the Chat standalone app. These settings don’t apply to Chat in Gmail. Learn more about Chat in Gmail.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings .
  • In the side panel, click Appearance .
  • Select an option:
    • Under “Color,” select the color palette you want.
    • Under “Mode,” select: System, Light, or Dark.
      • Tip: The “System” option is based on your OS or browser setting.
    • Under “Density,” select Comfortable or Compact. Learn more about density settings for Chat in Gmail.
      • Tip: Use Compact mode to find more information at a glance in Chat. Comfortable (Default)

Compact

  • Sender and recipient message bubbles are on opposite sides.
  • Narrower message bubbles.
  • More space in the left bar, conversation list, and Home.
  • Sender and recipient message bubbles are on the same side.
  • Wider message bubbles.
  • Less space in the left bar, conversation list, and Home.
  • Click Close . Tip: Appearance settings in Chat comply with accessibility guidelines. Learn more about Accessibility in Google Chat.

Adjust density settings for Chat in Gmail

When you adjust the density settings in Gmail, your changes apply to both Gmail and Chat in Gmail.

Important: These changes don’t apply to Chat when you access it through:

  • chat.google.com

  • Chat standalone app To change the density settings:

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings .

  • In the settings side panel, under “Density,” select:

    • Default
    • Comfortable
    • Compact Tip: In Chat in Gmail, the “Default” and “Comfortable” options use the same Chat density layout.

Send feedback in Google Chat

You can send feedback in Google Chat to:

  • Give feature requests and suggestions.
  • Report something that doesn’t work, such as errors or product bugs. Your comments can help us improve your experience.

Give feedback in Google Chat

Important: To help us understand your feedback, include details and a screenshot. The more info you include in your feedback, the more helpful it is for us.

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Help Send feedback to Google.
  • Click Report an issue or Suggest an idea.
  • Describe your issue or suggestion.
  • Optional: To add a screenshot, click Capture screenshot.
    • To highlight or hide parts of the screenshot, click Highlight or Hide Info.
    • If you don’t want to include the screenshot, click Remove screenshot .
  • Click Send.

Related resources

  • Get started with Google Chat
  • Google Chat training and help

Sign in & access Google Chat (Computer)

On your computer, you can sign in to use Chat in Gmail or access Chat directly at chat.google.com. You can also sign in to the Google Chat standalone app.

On your phone or tablet, you can sign in to the Chat app for Android or iPhone or iPad , or use Chat in Gmail or in a browser.

Google Chat: Open a Google Chat

Sign in to Google Chat

Important: To use Chat, you need a Google Account. Learn how to create a Google Account.

  • In your browser, open Google Chat.
  • Tip: You can also:
    • Use Chat in Gmail
    • Install the Google Chat standalone app
  • If prompted, sign in. Tip: Chat displays the name and profile photo from your Google Account. Learn how to change personal info in your Google Account.

Use Chat in Gmail

You can access Chat in Gmail on your computer. Learn how to use Chat in Gmail.

If you can’t find Chat in Gmail, you need to turn it on in Gmail settings.

Go to Gmail settings

Access Chat from the web

To message people on the web, open Chat in your browser.

Open Chat

Tip: You can also install the standalone app for Google Chrome. Learn how to install the Chat standalone app.

Use Chat at work or school

If you have a work or school account that’s part of Google Workspace, you can use Chat to communicate in large spaces, small groups, or with another person.

Before you use Chat, your organization needs to set up Chat. If you don’t see Chat, reach out to your administrator. Learn how to find your administrator.

Sign out of Google Chat

You can sign out of, remove, or switch between different Google Chat accounts from any device.

Sign out on your computer

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • At the top right, click your profile picture.
  • Click Sign out or Sign out of all accounts.

Sign out from another computer

If you forgot to sign out of Google Chat on another computer, you can remotely sign out of your account. Sign out on a device you no longer use.

Switch accounts & stay signed in

If you have more than one Google Account, you can sign in to multiple accounts at the same time. You can also switch between your accounts and stay signed in to both.

Learn how to sign in to multiple accounts.

Sign out of Google Chat (iPhone and iPad)

You can sign out of, remove, or switch between different Google Chat accounts from any device.

Remove your Google Account from your device

Important:

  • To sign out of the Google Chat app, you must remove your account from your phone or tablet.
  • When you remove an account, it’s deleted from all apps on your device. When your account is removed, you won’t be signed in to Google products, like Maps or YouTube.
  • Open the Chat app or Gmail app .
  • At the top right, tap your profile picture.
  • Tap Manage accounts on this device.
  • Choose an option:
    • To disable an account on Google Chat temporarily, next to the account, tap Toggle .
    • To remove an account from your device completely, tap Remove from this device Remove. Tip: If you remove the account from your phone or tablet, you can still use Google Chat on a computer.

Switch accounts & stay signed in

Important: If you add multiple accounts to the Chat app, you can switch between them. Messages on the Chat app stay separate for each account.

  • Open the Chat app or Gmail app .
  • At the top right, tap your profile picture.
  • Tap the account you want to use with Google Chat.

Use Google Chat in Gmail

To manage your communication, stay connected, and collaborate in one place, add Google Chat to your Gmail inbox. If you use a work or school account, your organization determines if this option is available.

Important: Your child can use Chat in the Gmail app, or in the web version of Gmail, even if the Chat app is blocked. Learn how to manage your child’s Google Account.

Turn Chat on or off in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • Go to Gmail settings
  • At the top, click Chat and Meet.
  • Next to “Chat,” to turn Chat on or off in Gmail, select Google Chat or Off.
  • Click Save Changes.

How is Chat in Gmail different from Chat?

You get the same features in Chat and Chat in Gmail, but the integrated Gmail experience provides a central location to communicate with friends, family, or coworkers between emails.

  • Chat: Use when you prefer a dedicated chat experience and don’t mind switching between different apps.
  • Gmail: Use when you like to multi-task and prefer to get all of your communications in one place. Learn more about the new integrated Gmail layout.
