Notifications and shortcuts

Change your availability status in Google Chat

To let others know when you’re available, you can change your Google Chat status.

Status icon

Status text

Status meaning

Active

Gmail or Google Chat is open.

Do not disturb

Google Chat notifications are muted.

For Google Workspace accounts, your status is visible at the domain level only.

Away

You aren’t connected to the internet.

You’ve been idle for more than 10 minutes.

You’re in “Set as away” status.

Idle

You’ve been inactive in Gmail or Google Chat for the last 5 minutes.

This only shows on desktop.

Tips:

  • Only people you share a space with, someone you accept a chat invite from, or people who aren’t blocked have visibility of your status.
  • If your status is “Do not disturb”:
    • You temporarily mute notifications on all your devices from Chat or Gmail until you change your status to “Active.”
    • People can tell how long you paused notifications so they don’t expect an immediate response.

Change your status

  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, next to your status indicator, click the Down arrow .
  • Choose: Automatic, Do not disturb, or Set as away.

Set a custom status

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • From your status indicator at the top, click the Down arrow .
  • Click Add a status.
  • Follow the prompt to choose an emoji, write a status message, or end or clear a status.
  • Click Done.

Delete a custom status

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • From your status indicator at the top, click the Down arrow .
  • Click the status to delete.
  • Click X.
  • Click Done.

Turn off Calendar status for Workspace accounts

For Workspace accounts, your Chat status automatically updates based on your Calendar status. For example, your status updates when you’re in a meeting or when you’re out of office.

  • When someone sends you a direct message, they’ll see your Calendar status next to your name at the top.

  • Group conversations and spaces don’t show a Calendar status. Your administrator controls:

  • Status availability options in Chat, such as “Out of office” or “In focus time.”

  • Whether or not Calendar status is automatically displayed in Chat. If you don’t want to share your Calendar status, you can turn it off.

  • Go to Google Calendar.

  • At the top right, click the Settings menu Settings.

  • On the left, under “Settings for my calendar,” select your calendar.

  • Under “Access permissions for events,” check the box next to “Show calendar info in other Google apps, limited by access permissions.” Tip: Your changes are automatically saved.

Temporarily stop notifications in Google Chat or Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • At the top, click your status.
  • Select Do not disturb.
  • To set your preferred duration, select a duration from the list or click “Until a specific time.”
  • Click Set. Tip: Notifications automatically turn back on after the mute duration expires. To end mute sooner, click your status Do not disturb Turn off Do not disturb.

Schedule time for paused notifications in Google Chat or Gmail

  • Go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • At the top, click your status.
  • Select Do not disturb Set a do not disturb schedule.
  • Under “Do not disturb schedules,” click Create new.
  • Enter details of the times that you want to pause notifications, then click Save.
  • Optional: To match your time zone to your do not disturb schedule:
    • Open the Settings menu .
    • Check the box and click Save. Tip: You can create multiple schedules and notifications will be paused for each of the schedules.

Related resources

  • Turn Google Chat notifications on or off
  • Mute conversations in Google Chat

I’m not getting Google Chat notifications

If you don’t get notifications, you may need to update your device settings or check your Google Chat notification settings.

Understand app notifications

Some Google Chat applications can adjust notification settings, to send updates, including::

  • @notify messages: These messages are for critical or time-sensitive information. They work like @all messages to get immediate attention and ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status, muted conversations, or notification settings.
  • @silent messages: These messages are for low-priority updates. They minimize disruption by working like system messages. Tip: Only applications or bots can send @silent or @notify messages. You can’t send these message types.

Troubleshoot Chat notifications

This article explains how to troubleshoot these situations:

  • I don’t get any notifications
  • I get notifications sometimes
  • I don’t get notifications for a specific space
  • I don’t get notifications for a specific 1:1 or group direct message How to fix Google Chat notifications not working on your computer

I don’t get any notifications

If you don’t get notifications, turn on notifications in your computer’s operating system and browser.

Allow notifications in your computer’s operating system
  • Each computer operating system has different steps to turn on notifications. For more info, check your operating system’s online help.
    • Mac
    • Chrome
    • Windows
  • Some computer operating systems have settings that mute notifications. If you don’t get Google Chat notifications, check your operating system’s online help and make sure notifications aren’t muted. Tip: Older Windows versions may have different notification settings.
Turn on Chat notifications from the web

To make sure you receive Chat notifications, you may need to enable them from your Google Chat or Gmail settings on the web. This process involves granting both browser notification and idle detection permissions through a single prompt.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail .
  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .
    • In Gmail, click Settings See all settings Chat and Meet Manage chat settings.
  • Under “Desktop notifications,” you will find the “Allow chat notifications” toggle.
    • If this toggle is off, turn it on.
    • If this toggle is already on, but you are not receiving notifications, you may see a Turn on button. Click this button.
  • In the browser permission dialog that appears, click Allow to grant both browser-level notifications and idle detection permissions for Google Chat.
Understand and manage idle detection for notifications

Idle detection permission helps Google Chat ensure notifications are sent to your correct active device, reducing duplicate notifications across multiple devices.

To grant idle detection permission when browser notifications are already active:

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail .
  • At the top right, click Settings Manage Chat settings.
  • Under “Desktop notifications,” if prompted to turn on idle detection separately, click Turn on.
  • Follow the prompts from your browser to grant idle detection permission.
Allow Google Chat notifications in Google Chrome
  • On your computer, open Chrome .
  • At the top right, click More Settings .
  • On the left, click Privacy and security Site Settings .
  • Scroll to Permissions select Notifications .
  • Find “chat.google.com:443” and “mail.google.com:443.”
  • Follow the steps listed in the table below under “Steps to turn on notification permissions for both of these URLs.” Tip: To make sure notifications are allowed on your browser, under “Allowed to send notifications,” add both “chat.google.com:443” and “mail.google.com:443.” Follow the steps in the table for each of the URLs.

Location of Google Chat and Gmail entries (https://chat.google.com:443 and mail.google.com:443)

Steps to turn on notification permissions

Not listed under “Customized Behaviors”

  1. Next to “Allowed to send notifications,” click Add.

  2. In the “Site” field, enter: https://chat.google.com:443

  3. Click Add.

  4. If it’s not listed, follow the same steps for https://mail.google.com:443.

Listed under “Not allowed to send notifications”

  1. Turn on permission to send notifications.

  2. On the right, click More actions .

  3. Click Allow.

Listed under “Allowed to send notifications”

Notification permissions are turned on already.

Tip: By default, browsers disable auto-playing audio. To change the settings to allow audio:

  • Under “Customized behaviors,” click chat.google.com:443.
  • Under “Permissions,” next to Sound , click the dropdown box.
  • Select Allow.
  • Follow the same steps for “mail.google.com:443.”
Allow Google Chat notifications in other browsers

Each browser has different steps to turn on notifications. For more info, check your browser’s online help.

I get notifications sometimes

If you occasionally miss Google Chat notifications on your computer, follow these steps.

Close the mobile app

Close the Google Chat or Gmail mobile app. When an app is open, notifications show up there and don’t show up when you’re:

  • Online at chat.google.com.
  • In the Chat desktop app.
  • In Chat in Gmail.
Find out where you get notifications

Check where you receive notifications.

If you’re using chat.google.com:

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” check if the “Show an example” option shows.

    • If you can find “Show an example,” you get Google Chat web notifications at chat.google.com.
    • If you can’t find “Show an example,” you get Google Chat notifications in another browser tab or in the Chat app itself. If you’re using Gmail:

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Chat and Meet settings

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” check if the “Show an example” option shows.

    • If you can find “Show an example,” you get Google Chat web notifications in Gmail.
    • If you can’t find “Show an example,” you get Google Chat notifications in another browser tab or in the Chat app itself.

I don’t get notifications for a specific space

Make sure notifications are turned on for spaces. Learn how to manage thread notifications.

Tip: Notification settings for spaces and group direct messages are the same on the web and your mobile device. If you change notification settings for a space or group direct message on the web, the same settings apply on your mobile app.

I don’t get notifications for a specific 1:1 or group direct message

Make sure notifications are turned on for the direct message. Learn how to Turn Google Chat notifications on or off.

Tip: Notification settings for direct messages are the same in the web and mobile versions of Google Chat. If you change notification settings for a direct message on the web, the same settings apply on your mobile app.

  • Turn Google Chat notifications on or off
  • Change your availability status in Google Chat
  • Mute conversations in Google Chat

  • @silent messages: These messages are for low-priority updates. They minimize disruption by working like system messages. Tip: Only applications or bots can send @silent or @notify messages. You can’t send these message types.

Troubleshoot Chat notifications

This article explains how to troubleshoot these situations:

  • I don’t get any notifications
  • I get notifications sometimes
  • I don’t get notifications for a specific space
  • I don’t get notifications for a specific 1:1 or group direct message How to fix Google Chat notifications not working on your mobile device

I don’t get any notifications

If you don’t get notifications, check the notification settings on your mobile device.

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open “Settings” on your device.
  • Tap Notifications Chat.
  • Make sure app notifications are turned on.
  • Check if Google Chat app notifications are also turned on. Tip: The settings menu on your device might have a different name for “Notifications.” For more info on how to access app notification settings, check your mobile device’s online help.

I get notifications sometimes

On your computer, close active Gmail and Google Chat browser tabs. When you’re in a browser, notifications show up there instead of the mobile app. If you’re not active in Google Chat, notifications show up on all devices signed in to your Google Account.

I don’t get notifications for a specific space

Make sure notifications are turned on for spaces. Learn how to manage thread notifications.

Tip: Notification settings for spaces and group direct messages are the same on the web and your mobile device. If you change notification settings for a space or group direct message on the web, the same settings apply on your mobile app.

I don’t get notifications for a specific 1:1 or group direct message

Make sure notifications are turned on for the direct message. Learn how to turn on notifications for a direct message.

Tip: Notification settings for direct messages are the same in the web and mobile versions of Google Chat. If you change notification settings for a direct message on the web, the same settings apply on your mobile app.

Related resources

  • Turn Google Chat notifications on or off
  • Change your availability status in Google Chat
  • Mute conversations in Google Chat

Mute conversations in Google Chat

If you don’t want to get notifications for a specific conversation in Chat, you can mute it. When you mute a conversation, the conversation isn’t:

  • Highlighted in your list of conversations
  • Moved to the top of your list of conversations
  • Shown in Home
    • Tip: When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. A badge still shows next to conversations where someone mentions you. Learn more about mentions in Chat.

Mute or unmute a conversation

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • In your conversation list, on the right of a conversation, click More options Mute or Unmute.

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off (Computer)

Notifications appear on the devices you used most recently. If you’re not active in Chat, notifications appear on all devices signed in to your Google Account.

By default, you receive notifications when:

  • Someone @ mentions you
  • Someone reacts or responds to your message If you mute a specific conversation or set your Chat status to “Do not disturb,” you won’t receive notifications.

In this article, learn how to:

  • Turn notifications on or off.

  • Customize notifications for specific conversations & spaces.

  • Customize notification sounds.

  • Get notifications in the Chat mobile app.

  • Update device or browser notification settings for Chat on a computer. Tips:

  • If email notifications are on, you get email reminders for Chat messages you haven’t read for more than 12 hours.

  • If you have multiple Google Accounts, you can set different notification settings for each account.

  • Some Google Chat apps can ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status or notification settings, to send updates, including:

    • @notify messages: These messages are for critical or time-sensitive information. They work like @all messages to get immediate attention and ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status, muted conversations, or notification settings.
    • @silent messages: These messages are for low-priority updates. They minimize disruption by working like system messages.

Google Chat: Manage your settings

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Turn on notifications

Turn on notifications in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • To turn on notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • If you don’t get Google Chat notifications after you turn it on, allow Google Chat notifications in your operating system and browser.

  • To turn email notifications for unread messages on or off, under “Email notifications,” select Only @mentions & direct messages or Off.

Manage combined notification permissions

Web users can grant browser notifications and idle detection permissions through a single flow. This occurs in two ways:

  • Enabled but blocked: If “Allow chat notifications” is enabled but the browser blocks notifications, a “Turn on” button appears. Click it to trigger permission dialogs.
  • Disabled toggle: If “Allow chat notifications” is disabled, turning on the toggle triggers permission dialogs.
Check if notifications are on
  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .
  • Under “Desktop notifications,” click Show an example.
  • If an example notification doesn’t appear:
    • Your notifications may be muted because of your availability status.
    • Turn on notifications for the device and browser you use with Google Chat.
Turn on notifications in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • To turn on notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Allow chat notifications.”

Check if notifications are on

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat notifications settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” click Show an example.

  • If an example notification doesn’t appear:

    • Your notifications may be muted because of your availability status.
    • Turn on notifications for the device and browser you use with Gmail. Turn off notifications
Turn off notifications in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • To turn off notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.” Learn how to change your availability status in Google Chat.

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn off Google Chat notifications in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • To turn off notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.” Learn how to change your availability status in Google Chat.

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn Google Chat reaction notifications on or off

Turn on reaction notifications

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Reaction notifications.” Tips:

  • For reaction notifications to work, turn on Allow chat notifications.

  • The existing notification settings apply to the reaction notifications of a conversation.

  • You can’t get reaction notifications in Announcement Spaces. Turn off reaction notifications

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Reaction notifications.”

    • This also turns off reaction notifications on mobile.

Customize Google Chat notifications for spaces & direct messages

Customize notifications for a space with in-line threading

By default, only threads you follow are bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list. To control how thread updates show in Chat, customize your notification settings.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Next to the space name, click More options Notifications.

  • Select an option for notifications:

    • All: Notifications for all new messages and replies to threads.
      • Tip: If you select “All,” it automatically follows all new threads for that space. To unfollow a thread, click Active Threads Following.
    • Main conversations: Notifications for all new main conversations, @mentions, and replies to threads you follow.
    • For you: Notifications for @mentions and replies to threads you follow.
    • None: No notifications, just an indicator for @mentions.

  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

  • Click Save. Turn notifications on or off for a direct message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

  • Next to the direct message or group DM, click More options Notifications.

    • For group DMs, you can select to get notifications for:
      • All: All new messages
      • For you: Only @mentions
      • None

  • Select All or None.

  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

Customize Google Chat notification sounds

Customize notification sounds in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Notifications sounds,” select the sound to use for notifications. Customize Google Chat notification sounds in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Notifications sounds,” select the sound to use for notifications.

Grant idle detection permissions

Idle detection delivers notifications to your active device. Granting this permission helps reliably send notifications and pauses mobile alerts when you are active on desktop.

If you are idle on Gmail or Google Chat on your computer, notifications go to your mobile device. You are considered idle if you’re inactive for over 30 seconds, even if you still have a web browser open.

For Chrome users, you can adjust settings to receive chat notifications on mobile only when you’re inactive on Chrome.

Respond to the permission prompt

When you enable Chat notifications, a dialog may appear. This dialog asks you to “Pause mobile notifications when you are active on this device.” Click Continue to grant idle detection permission.

Adjust Chrome settings manually

If the permission dialog doesn’t appear, you can manually enable idle detection in your Chrome settings.

  • Go to chrome://settings/content/idleDetection.
  • Check the box for “Sites can ask to know when you’re actively using your device.”
  • Under “Customized behaviors,” add mail.google.com or chat.google.com to the allowed sites list.
  • To add a site, click Add.

Update device or browser notification settings

Update device notifications

Each computer operating system has different steps to turn on notifications. For more info, go to your operating system’s online help.

Some computer operating systems have settings that mute notifications. If you don’t get the notifications, make sure notifications aren’t muted.

Update browser notifications

To turn notifications on or off, you might need to update your browser notification settings. Learn how to allow Google Chat notifications.

Customize Google Chat notifications for spaces & direct messages

Customize notifications for a space with in-line threading

By default, only threads you follow are bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list. To control how thread updates show in Chat, customize your notification settings.

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • Tap and hold a space Notification settings.
  • Select an option for notifications:
    • All: Notifications for all new messages and replies to threads.
      • Tip: If you select “All,” it automatically follows all new threads for that space. To unfollow a thread, tap Active Threads Following.
    • Main conversations: Notifications for all new main conversations, @mentions, and replies to threads you follow.
    • For you: Notifications for @mentions and replies to threads you follow.
    • None: No notifications, just an indicator for @mentions.
  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, turn on Mute conversation. Tip: When you follow a thread in a space, you’re notified with a blue dot whenever there’s activity in that thread unless that space is muted.

Turn notifications on or off for a specific direct message

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app .
  • Tap and hold a direct message.
  • Tap Notification settings.
  • Select All or None.
  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, turn on Mute conversation.

Customize Google Chat notification sounds

Customize notification sounds in Google Chat app

  • Open the Chat app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .

  • Under “Notifications,” tap Notification sounds.

  • Select the notification sound you want to use.

  • To turn off notification sounds, tap None.

  • Tap Done. Customize Google Chat notification sounds in Gmail

  • Open the Gmail app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings .

  • Under “Notifications,” tap Chat notifications Notification sounds.

  • Select the notification sound you want to use.

  • To turn off notification sounds, tap None.

  • Tap Done.

Troubleshoot issues with Google Chat notifications

Prevent multiple notifications

To avoid duplicate mobile notifications from the Gmail and Chat apps, in your device’s settings, turn off Google Chat app notifications.

  • On your device, open the Settings app.
  • Tap Notifications Chat.
  • Turn “Allow notifications” off. Tip: For more info, visit stop extra chat notifications.

Not getting notifications

If you don’t get notifications, visit I’m not getting Google Chat notifications.

Get notifications in the Google Chat mobile app

When the Google Chat mobile app is open, you get notifications in the app.

You won’t get notifications:

  • Online at chat.google.com
  • In the Chat desktop app
  • In Chat in Gmail When the Chat app is open, you get the message “You’re receiving Chat notifications here.” Learn more about the Chat standalone app.

Important: When iPhone or iPad users get messages from you, your profile picture could also appear on the notifications. Learn how to change your profile picture.

Use keyboard shortcuts to navigate around Chat

Navigate around chat

  • To go to a conversation or space, use the Up and Down arrows. To open a conversation or space, press Enter.

  • By default, the focus is on the message or conversation box. To read messages in a 1:1 conversation or space, press Esc to exit the box, then to go through the messages, use the Up arrow. Legacy Spaces always have 2 levels:

  • Level one is the list of conversations.

  • Level 2 is messages within a conversation. Current Spaces can have 2 levels:

  • Level one is the main conversation.

  • Any message in the main conversation can start a thread at the second level. Tips:

  • To move through the level, use the Up and Down arrows.

  • To change the level, use the Left and Right arrows.

    • This may start a thread if one doesn’t already exist. Start a conversation

  • Select an option:

    • On Chrome OS and Microsoft Windows, press Ctrl + Shift + k or ‘q’ when not editing.
    • On macOS, press Command + Shift + k or ‘q’ when not editing.

  • To move through the suggestions:

    • Enter the username.
    • Use the Up and Down arrows, then press Enter.

  • Enter your message.

  • To send your message, press Enter. Create or find a space

  • Select an option:

    • On Chrome OS and Windows, press Ctrl + o.
    • On macOS, press Command + o.

  • To create a space, enter the name.

  • Press Tab Enter.

  • To find and join a space:

    • To move through the list of spaces, use the Up and Down arrows.
    • Press Tab to highlight or “Preview” Enter. Start a new conversation or message in a space

  • Select an option:

    • On Chrome OS and Windows, press Ctrl + s.
    • On macOS, press Command + s.

  • Focus moves to the main reply box.

    • In a legacy Space, this is a new topic.

  • Enter your message.

  • Press Enter.

Privacy, data, and policies

Export your data from Google Chat

If you have a Google account, you can download your data from Chat. You can create an archive to keep for your records or use the data in another service. Learn how to download your data.

Your download includes your:

  • User profile information
  • Memberships in direct messages, group messages, and spaces
  • Messages along with attachments from direct messages, group messages, and spaces Tip: Group messages and spaces created by users with a work or school account won’t export as part of your Chat history.

If you need to export data and you use a work or school account, please contact your administrator. Learn who your administrator is.

If you’re a super administrator of your Google domain, you can download your organization’s data. Group messages and spaces created by users from outside your domain will not be available in the export. Learn how to export your organization’s Google Workspace data.

Final update: Google Currents shutdown

As an admin, we are sharing this update to help you transition to Google Chat following the completion of the Google Currents shutdown. You can refer to this article for help with any questions you may have in the future.

Currents shutdown timeline

  • In February 2021, we announced the migration of Google Currents to spaces in Chat. For more information, go to Google Workspace Updates.
  • Customers could opt-in to the data migration until December 31, 2022. For customers who opted-in to the migration, Google migrated most data by July 2023.
  • After customer migrations completed in July 2023, we began deleting all remaining Currents data on August 8, 2023.
  • All remaining support resources for Currents, including help center content, will be deleted by December 31, 2023.

Impact on other Workspace products & features

Expand section | Collapse all

Google+

Following the consumer Google+ shutdown in 2019, enterprise user data was transitioned to Currents. Following the Currents shutdown, we began deleting all remaining data migrated from Google+ on August 8, 2023. For details, go to Frequently asked questions about the Google+ shutdown.

Currents content embedded in Google Sites

Effective July 5, 2023, Currents communities embedded in Google Sites are no longer available.

Editing About Me data

With Currents enabled, some profile fields in the About Me section of myaccount.google.com were available to users for editing, including:

  • Email
  • Address
  • Phone
  • Occupation
  • Organization (Work and Education History)
  • Website (Profile and Contributor Links)
  • IM (Chat username)
  • Location (Places) Once the Currents shutdown is complete, users who have previously edited these fields will no longer be able to update this information, and these fields will be removed from the user profile and deleted.

We plan to relaunch these fields with additional controls for admins in the future.

Frequently asked questions about the Google+ shutdown

About the Google+ shutdown

  • On April 2, 2019, we shut down the consumer (personal) version of Google+, a social network by Google.
  • Google+ content from consumer Google+ accounts and Google+ pages has been deleted.
  • If you have a Google Workspace account, as part of your work or school, you can continue to use Google+ within your organization.
  • No other Google products (such as Gmail, Google Photos, Google Drive, YouTube) were or will be removed as part of the consumer Google+ shutdown. The Google Account you use to sign in to these services will remain.

General questions

Why shut down Google+ for consumers?

Given the challenges in creating and maintaining a successful Google+ that meets our consumer users’ expectations, we decided to sunset the consumer version of Google+. We’re committed to focusing on our enterprise efforts, and will be launching new features purpose-built for businesses. Read the announcement.

Will other Google services be shutdown when my Google+ content is deleted?

No other Google products (such as Gmail, Google Photos, Google Drive, YouTube) were or will be shut down as part of the consumer Google+ shutdown, and the Google Account you use to sign in to these services will remain. Your brand account will continue to exist without Google+, so you can continue to use it with other Google products, such as YouTube channels.

What happened to my Google+ content?

Google+ content from consumer Google+ accounts and Google+ pages has been deleted.

Are there any cases where Google+ content was not deleted from consumer Google+ accounts?

Certain Google+ content may not have been deleted from consumer Google+ and/or Album Archive if it was needed in order to meet any applicable law, regulation, legal process, legal obligation (including legal preservation obligations), or governmental request.

What happened to my Google+ vanity URLs?

Google+ vanity URL names are no longer supported and were deleted as part of the shutdown. Any links that use Google+ vanity URLs, including Album Archive, will no longer work.

How do I delete the Google+ app if it came with my Android device?

You can delete or disable the Google+ app by following the steps here.

Will my photos and videos from Google+ continue to exist in Album Archive?

No, photos and videos from consumer Google+ accounts and Google+ pages in Album Archive were deleted.

Photos and videos backed up in Google Photos were not deleted as part of the consumer Google+ shutdown. Note that some photos and videos uploaded from Google+ may remain available in Google Photos. Namely,

  • Photos and videos uploaded to Google+ before Google Photos launched in 2015
  • Photos and videos backed up at any time using older versions of Google+ mobile apps (from 2015 or earlier)
  • Photos and videos that were associated with Google+ Events These photos and videos remain in Google Photos after the Google+ shutdown.

Google Workspace and Google+

What is a Google Workspace account?

Google Workspace is an integrated suite of collaboration and productivity apps for businesses that includes Gmail, Docs, Drive, Calendar, Hangouts Meet, and more. To learn more about Google Workspace, see Google Workspace editions.

Google Workspace users include businesses who pay for its services and educational institutions and other organizations that use Google Workspace at no cost.

How do I know if I have a Google Workspace or consumer (personal) Google+ account?

If you use Google+ for work or school, you probably have a Google Workspace account. You can check to see if you have a Google Workspace account by asking your administrator. If you do not know who your administrator is, read Who is my administrator?

How will Google Workspace accounts be impacted?

Google Workspace customers may see some upcoming changes to Google+ features related to the consumer shutdown. If you’re a Google Workspace customer, you can find more details here or you can talk to your administrator to learn more.

Will Google+ continue to be available to Google Workspace for Education users?

Organizations using Google Workspace for Education Plus will have the same access as other Google Workspace customers. If you participate in Google+ communities, please note that some Google+ communities may be impacted as part of the shutdown. For more information about the effect of the shutdown on communities, read Important changes to Google+ for Google Workspace due to the consumer shutdown.

Are Google+ pages part of Google Workspace?

Google+ pages are not part of Google Workspace and have been removed with the rest of the consumer Google+ platform. The associated brand accounts will continue to exist without Google+, so you can continue to use them with other Google products, such as YouTube channels.

How the Google+ shutdown affects other applications

What happened to the Google+ APIs?

Google+ APIs were shut down on March 7, 2019, including Google+ Sign-In. Developers should migrate to the more comprehensive Google Sign-In authentication system. In advance of the shutdown, we made some changes to mitigate the impact of the Google+ API shutdown. For more information, see our Google+ API shutdown page.

Will the API shutdown affect external sites?

Google+ integrations for web and mobile apps stopped functioning on March 7, 2019. The Google+ Sign-In feature was also shut down on March 7, 2019. Developers should migrate to the more comprehensive Google Sign-In authentication system. In advance of the shutdown, we made some changes to mitigate the impact of the Google+ API shutdown. For more information, see our Google+ API shutdown page.

What will happen to Google+ comments on Blogger and other sites?

Blogger and other sites may have used Google+ for their commenting system. Comments on blogs may also exist as posts or comments on Google+. This feature has been removed from Blogger and other sites. All your Google+ comments on all sites will be deleted starting April 2, 2019. Learn more about how the Google+ shutdown impacted Blogger.

Will the Google+ Sign-In button continue to work on other sites?

While we strongly encourage developers to migrate to the more comprehensive Google Sign-In authentication system, legacy applications can continue to use Google+ Sign-In until they can migrate. For more information, see our Google+ API shutdown page.

Will the photos from Local Guides uploaded to Google Maps be impacted by the shutdown of Google+?

No, photos uploaded by Local Guides to Google Maps will not be impacted.

How will the Google+ shutdown impact YouTube?

Most YouTube users won’t be impacted. However, some YouTube functionality that was built with Google+ may be impacted including channel art and channel icon editing on mobile, private video sharing to Google+ Circles, links to Google+ profiles on YouTube channel pages, Google+ custom URLs for channel pages, and commenting with outdated versions of the YouTube mobile app.

How will the Google+ shutdown impact Google Calendar?

All events created in Google+ have been removed from Google Calendar and birthdays of people in your Google+ Circles will no longer be displayed (birthdays from your Contacts will not be affected) as early as March 11, 2019. Events created from Google Calendar were not impacted.

What will happen to my data for Google+ +1s on external websites after the shutdown?

All +1s made on external websites have been deleted.

What will happen to the phone number I’ve set for Google+ use?

Phone numbers that were only used for Google+ notifications have been deleted. Phone numbers used with other Google services on your Google Account were not deleted. You can check the status of your phone number here.

Will my Google My Business account be impacted by the Google+ shutdown?

The consumer Google+ shutdown should not affect your Google My Business listing. These are 2 separate products with different accounts. Learn more

Google Chat Acceptable Use Policy

Last updated: September 11, 2025

These policies apply to Google Chat (“Chat”). When applying these policies, we may make exceptions based on educational, documentary, scientific, or artistic considerations, or where there are other substantial benefits to the users of the service. Be sure to check back from time to time, as these policies may change. Learn how to block users in Chat. Please also refer to Google’s Terms of Service for more information.

Child Safety

Do not create, upload, or distribute content that exploits or abuses children. This includes all child sexual abuse materials. To report content on a Google product that may exploit a child, click “Report abuse.” If you find content elsewhere on the internet, please contact the appropriate agency in your country.

More broadly, Google prohibits the use of our products to endanger children. This includes, but is not limited to, predatory behavior towards children, such as:

  • Child grooming: For example, befriending a child online to facilitate, either online or offline, sexual contact and/or exchanging sexual imagery with that child
  • Sextortion: For example, threatening or blackmailing a child by using real or alleged access to a child’s intimate images
  • Sexualization of a minor: For example, imagery that depicts, encourages, or promotes the sexual abuse of children or the portrayal of children in a manner that could result in the sexual exploitation of children
  • Trafficking of a child: For example, advertising or soliciting a child for commercial sexual exploitation If we become aware of such content, we will remove such content and take appropriate action, which may include reporting to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, limiting access to product features, and disabling accounts. If you believe a child is in danger of or has been subject to abuse, exploitation, or trafficking, contact the police immediately. If you have already made a report to the police and still need help, or you have concerns a child is being or was being endangered on our products, you can report the behavior to Google.

Dangerous & Illegal Activities

Do not use Chat to engage in illegal activities, or to promote activities, goods, services, or information that cause serious and immediate harm to people or animals. While we permit general information for educational, documentary, scientific, or artistic purposes about this content, we draw the line when the content directly facilitates harm or encourages illegal activity. We will take appropriate action if we are notified of unlawful activities, which may include reporting you to the relevant authorities, removing access to some of our products, or disabling your Google Account.

Deceptive Practices, Fraud & Scams

Do not deceive, mislead, or confuse users for financial gain or personal harm. This includes providing instructions on, recruiting for, or facilitating scams and fraud. Deceptive content includes, but is not limited to, fake reviews, “get rich quick” schemes, advance fee, romance, sweepstakes, and investment scams.

Harassment, Bullying & Threats

Do not harass, bully, or threaten others. We also don’t allow this product to be used to engage or incite others in these activities. This includes singling someone out for malicious abuse, threatening someone with serious harm, sexualizing someone in an unwanted way, exposing private information of someone else that could be used to carry out threats, disparaging or belittling targets of violence or tragedy, inciting others to carry out these activities, or harassing someone in other ways. Keep in mind that online harassment is illegal in many places and can have serious offline consequences for both the harasser and the target. We may take appropriate action if we are notified of threats of harm or other dangerous situations, which may include reporting you to the relevant authorities, removing access to some of our products, or disabling your Google Account.

Hate Speech

Do not engage in hate speech. Hate speech is content that promotes or condones violence against or has the primary purpose of inciting hatred against an individual or group on the basis of their race or ethnic origin, religion, disability, age, nationality, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, or any other characteristic that is associated with systemic discrimination or marginalization.

Impersonation & Misrepresentation of Identity

Do not impersonate a person or organization or misrepresent yourself. This includes impersonating any person or organizations you don’t represent; or providing misleading information about a user/site’s identity, qualifications, ownership, purpose, products, services, or business.

This also includes content or accounts misrepresenting or concealing their ownership or primary purpose such as misrepresenting or intentionally concealing your country of origin or other material details about yourself when directing content about politics, social issues, or matters of public concern to users in a country other than your own.

Malware & Similar Malicious Content

Do not transmit malware or any content that harms or interferes with the operation of the networks, servers, end-user devices, or other infrastructure. This includes the direct hosting, embedding, or transmission of malware, viruses, destructive code, or other harmful or unwanted software or similar content. This also includes content that transmits viruses, causes pop-ups, attempts to install software without the user’s consent, or otherwise impacts users with malicious code. See our Safe Browsing Policies for more information.

Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery & Sextortion

Do not store or distribute private nude, sexually explicit, or intimate images or videos without the subject’s consent. If someone has sent a private nude, sexually explicit, or intimate image or video of you, please report it to us here.

Do not coerce (using power, influence, or pressure), encourage, or solicit financial gain or other sexual content from an individual through the threat of disseminating their explicit, intimate, or embarrassing content of a sexual nature.

Personal & Confidential Information

Do not share or distribute other people’s personal or confidential information without their authorization. ​This includes the use of sensitive information, such as US Social Security numbers, bank account numbers, credit card numbers, images of signatures, and personal health documents. In most cases where this information is broadly available elsewhere on the internet or in public records, like national ID numbers listed on a government website, we generally don’t take action.

Phishing

Do not use this product for phishing. This includes soliciting or collecting sensitive data such as passwords, financial details, and social security numbers.

Spam

Do not spam. This may include unwanted promotional or commercial content, unwanted content that is created by an automated program, unwanted repetitive content, nonsensical content, or anything that appears to be a mass solicitation.

Violent Organizations & Movements

Known violent non-state organizations and movements aren’t permitted to use this product for any purpose. Do not distribute content that facilitates or promotes the activities of these groups, such as recruiting, coordinating online or offline activities, sharing manuals or other materials that could facilitate harm, promoting ideologies of violent non-state organizations, promoting terrorist acts, inciting violence, or celebrating attacks by violent non-state organizations. Depending upon the content, we may also take action against the user.

Policy enforcement

Google may disable accounts that are found to be in violation of these policies. If your account is disabled, and you believe it was a mistake, learn how to ask us to restore your account.

How Google Workspace with Gemini helps protect users from malicious content and prompt injection

Learn how Google Workspace with Gemini helps protect users from malicious content and prompt injection attacks.

Malicious content and prompt injection in generative AI

Similar to email and content threats like malware and phishing attacks, security threats can target generative AI tools. Prompt injection is an attempt to elicit an unintended or harmful response from generative AI tools. Attackers may commit prompt injection not only by directly submitting queries, but also by sharing malicious content with a user, who then unintentionally references this malicious content in prompts in generative AI tools like Gemini Apps or Google Workspace with Gemini.

To help protect Gemini users, Google uses advanced security measures to identify risky and suspicious content.

How Google detects malicious content and prompt injection

To help protect you from malicious content and prompt injection, Gemini in Workspace may filter or block some responses if malicious activity is detected.

When Gemini identifies activity related to a prompt that may be malicious
  • Gemini in Workspace warns you that the content has security risks.
  • Sometimes, none of your content can be used to generate a response.
  • Sometimes, only some of your content is used to generate a response, with the malicious content excluded by Gemini. For example, if you ask Gemini in Gmail to summarize email messages, and one of those messages has malicious content, Gemini may not respond to your prompt for safety reasons.

Help avoid unsafe content

Pay attention when interacting with content from someone you don’t know
  • Take notice of warnings from Google on content you receive in other tools like Gmail.
  • Avoid clicking links from untrustworthy sources.
  • Use caution when interacting with shared content from unknown senders, like files in Drive.
Report malicious messages in Gmail

If you get a deceptive message or URL in Gmail, you can report it as phishing. Phishing is an attempt to steal personal information using deceptive emails, messages, ads, or websites that appear legitimate. For example, a phishing email might look like it’s from your bank and request private information about your bank account. Learn how to report phishing in Gmail.

Report malicious documents in Docs Editors

If you get malicious documents, files, images, and other content in Docs Editors, you can report them. Learn how to report abusive content.

Report malicious behavior in Gemini in Workspace apps

If you get a response that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can give feedback on that response to let us know. Learn how to report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps.

Related resources

  • Avoid and report phishing emails
  • Report a violation
  • Report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps

Learn about message history for conversations

From May 1, 2025, the message history in some 1:1 direct messages may change if all of the following apply:

  • You have a 1:1 direct message with someone who uses Google Chat for school or work.
  • The person who started the 1:1 direct message belongs to an organization that has a rule to delete messages after a certain time period. This change applies to previous and newly created 1:1 direct messages.

Learn how to determine retention policies

If you have a work or school account, your organization sets the retention policies for all users in direct messages, group messages, and spaces you create.

After May 1, 2025, if you’re in a conversation started by someone from a different organization (for example, someone messaging from an external work or school account), their admin sets the retention policy which determines how long message history is available for all users in the conversation.

All conversations will show text that indicates who started the conversation. If the person that started the conversation is messaging from an external work or school account, their account’s policy applies to the conversation.

To download old messages, export your data from Google Chat.

If you’re a Google Workspace administrator, learn more about retention policies.

Automatic deletion of inactive spaces

Google Chat automatically deletes inactive spaces to declutter your chat list. This feature is active for spaces in Google Chat, including those in continuous meeting chats. You can’t recover deleted spaces.

Spaces are permanently deleted if:

  • No user messages: The space contains no user-sent messages. System messages, such as ‘User X joined,’ don’t count as user activity.
  • No recent activity: There has been no other activity, such as membership or setting changes, in the space for 30 consecutive days.
  • No pinned resources or tasks: The space contains no resources, like documents or media, that have been pinned in the space. Tip: To prevent your space from being deleted, send a message in the space.

  • Use search operators in Google Chat

Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products

To give you more granular control over your data, we’ve updated our smart feature settings for Google Workspace. This update turns the existing control into two distinct settings that govern different product experiences. These updates also give you more choice and control over your data, and do not alter our underlying data handling practices or our robust privacy commitments.

In Calendar, Chat, Drive, Gmail, Meet, and Voice, you can manage smart feature settings. Depending on your smart feature settings, you can do things like:

  • Use Gemini in Google Workspace to reference Drive files from Gmail.
  • Automatically add events such as flights from Gmail to Calendar.
  • Compile loyalty cards and tickets from your inbox into Google Wallet.

Smart features in Gmail, Chat & Meet

When you turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, you agree to let Gmail, Chat and Meet use your content and activity in these products to personalize your experience in those apps.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in Gmail, Chat and Meet that include:

  • Automatic email filtering / categorization (Primary/Social/Promotions)
  • Smart Compose (suggested text) in email
  • Smart Reply (suggested quick replies) in email
  • Summary cards above emails (travel, package tracking, and more) The setting controls app-level smart features which personalize your experience within Gmail, Chat, or Meet. Changes to this setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Google Workspace setting.

When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Gmail, Chat, and Meet. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Even if you turn off smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, some smart features with individual on and off settings are still available. Some examples include:

  • Conversation summaries in Chat
  • Smart Reply in Chat Smart features in Google Workspace

When you turn on smart features in Google Workspace, you agree to let Google Workspace use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience across Workspace. Workspace includes apps for businesses and schools, such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more. To learn more, visit the Workspace website.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences across Workspace that include:

  • Show events from Gmail in Calendar (such as flight itineraries and invitations).
  • Personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results) in products like Drive.
  • Ask Gemini to summarize content, create drafts, and find key information, along with other Google Workspace with Gemini features.
  • Personalized recommendations on features to use across Google Workspace services. When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Google Workspace products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Changes to the smart features in Google Workspace setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet setting described above.

Smart features in other Google products

When you turn on smart features in other Google products, you agree to let Google use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience in other Google products.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in other Google products that include:

  • Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)
  • Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in Search services (personal accounts only) When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in other Google products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

In addition, data sharing and personalization in other Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).

Even when the setting for smart features in other Google products is turned off, if you choose to share your Workspace data through screen actions (including screenshots), some smart features in other Google products will still be available. An example is when you use screen actions to chat with Gemini Apps.

Change smart feature settings

Learn how to change your smart feature settings in different Google Workspace products. You can change smart feature settings on your computer or in the Gmail app for Android, iPhone, or iPad.

Change smart feature settings for Gmail, Chat & Meet

Important: Changes to smart feature settings apply across all devices and apps where you’re signed in.

  • If you’re on the mobile Gmail app but don’t get a notification about the changes, update your app.
  • Some changes made on your computer don’t reflect in the mobile app.
  • On your computer, go to Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • In the “General” tab, scroll to “Smart features.”
  • Next to “Turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet,” check or uncheck the box.

  • Under the “General” tab, scroll to “Google Workspace smart features.”
  • Click Manage Workspace smart feature settings.
  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  • At the bottom right, click Save.

Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings

If you have a personal Google Account, this notice and our Privacy Policy describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

If you have a work or school Google Account, this notice and the Google Cloud Privacy Notice describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

What are Google’s legal bases of processing for users in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland?

For users based in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland, Google processes your information for the purposes, and on the legal grounds, described below.

When we refer to “your Workspace Content & Activity” below, we mean content from Workspace apps such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more, and related data about how you use Workspace products.

Google’s legal bases are:

  • Your consent. We rely on your consent for Google to use your Workspace Content & Activity, when you turn on any of the smart features settings for Google Workspace, for the following purposes:
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat and Meet. For example, when you turn the smart features in Gmail, Chat and Meet setting on, you can get experiences that include Gmail Smart Compose (suggested text in email).
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience across Google Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in Google Workspace setting on, you can get experiences that include personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results). This setting does not affect your control over the smart features setting that personalizes your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet.
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in other Google products outside of Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in other Google products setting on, you can get experiences that include restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps. Data sharing and personalization in certain products may be subject to additional controls such Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).
  • You can revoke your consent to any of these purposes at any time by turning off the relevant setting as described in the “Change smart feature settings” section above.
  • Google and third parties’ legitimate interests with appropriate safeguards to protect your privacy.
    • To improve our services. If you have turned on any of the smart features settings, we may also process your Workspace Content & Activity to improve these features.
    • Processing information for this purpose is necessary for the legitimate interests of Google and our users in:
      • Providing, maintaining and improving services for our users (such as a flight confirmation email you receive being used to create a summary card that appears in your Gmail).
      • Developing new products and features that are useful for our customers and users (for example, processing aggregated Gmail data helped us develop and launch Smart Compose suggestions as you enter text in Gmail).
      • Performing research that benefits our users and the public (such as to conduct a user study that helped us develop and launch Smart Reply suggested responses in Gmail).
    • Learn more about how we’re protecting your Google Workspace data in the era of generative AI. How long is your Workspace Content & Activity used to provide smart features and to improve these features?

Your Workspace Content & Activity is used to provide you with smart features as long as the relevant smart feature setting is turned on. Turning off a smart feature setting or deleting your Workspace Content & Activity stops that data from being used to provide relevant smart features to you in the future.

Turning off a smart feature setting means your Workspace Content & Activity will no longer be used to improve the relevant smart features moving forward. The learnings developed from this improvement process may persist even after you turn off a smart feature setting or delete your Workspace Content & Activity from your Google Account. However, turning off a smart feature setting means that your Workspace Content & Activity would no longer be actively processed to improve the relevant smart features after you have turned the setting off.

Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products (Computer)

To give you more granular control over your data, we’ve updated our smart feature settings for Google Workspace. This update turns the existing control into two distinct settings that govern different product experiences. These updates also give you more choice and control over your data, and do not alter our underlying data handling practices or our robust privacy commitments.

In Calendar, Chat, Drive, Gmail, Meet, and Voice, you can manage smart feature settings. Depending on your smart feature settings, you can do things like:

  • Use Gemini in Google Workspace to reference Drive files from Gmail.
  • Automatically add events such as flights from Gmail to Calendar.
  • Compile loyalty cards and tickets from your inbox into Google Wallet.
  • Track an upcoming order using summary cards in Gmail.
  • Record, transcribe, and summarize notes in Meet and Voice.

  • Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  • At the top right, tap Done.

Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings

If you have a personal Google Account, this notice and our Privacy Policy describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

If you have a work or school Google Account, this notice and the Google Cloud Privacy Notice describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

What are Google’s legal bases of processing for users in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland?

For users based in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland, Google processes your information for the purposes, and on the legal grounds, described below.

When we refer to “your Workspace Content & Activity” below, we mean content from Workspace apps such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more, and related data about how you use Workspace products.

Google’s legal bases are:

  • Your consent. We rely on your consent for Google to use your Workspace Content & Activity, when you turn on any of the smart features settings for Google Workspace, for the following purposes:
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat and Meet. For example, when you turn the smart features in Gmail, Chat and Meet setting on, you can get experiences that include Gmail Smart Compose (suggested text in email).
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience across Google Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in Google Workspace setting on, you can get experiences that include personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results). This setting does not affect your control over the smart features setting that personalizes your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet.
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in other Google products outside of Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in other Google products setting on, you can get experiences that include restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps. Data sharing and personalization in certain products may be subject to additional controls such Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).
  • You can revoke your consent to any of these purposes at any time by turning off the relevant setting as described in the “Change smart feature settings” section above.
  • Google and third parties’ legitimate interests with appropriate safeguards to protect your privacy.
    • To improve our services. If you have turned on any of the smart features settings, we may also process your Workspace Content & Activity to improve these features.
    • Processing information for this purpose is necessary for the legitimate interests of Google and our users in:
      • Providing, maintaining and improving services for our users (such as a flight confirmation email you receive being used to create a summary card that appears in your Gmail).
      • Developing new products and features that are useful for our customers and users (for example, processing aggregated Gmail data helped us develop and launch Smart Compose suggestions as you enter text in Gmail).
      • Performing research that benefits our users and the public (such as to conduct a user study that helped us develop and launch Smart Reply suggested responses in Gmail).
    • Learn more about how we’re protecting your Google Workspace data in the era of generative AI. How long is your Workspace Content & Activity used to provide smart features and to improve these features?

Your Workspace Content & Activity is used to provide you with smart features as long as the relevant smart feature setting is turned on. Turning off a smart feature setting or deleting your Workspace Content & Activity stops that data from being used to provide relevant smart features to you in the future.

Turning off a smart feature setting means your Workspace Content & Activity will no longer be used to improve the relevant smart features moving forward. The learnings developed from this improvement process may persist even after you turn off a smart feature setting or delete your Workspace Content & Activity from your Google Account. However, turning off a smart feature setting means that your Workspace Content & Activity would no longer be actively processed to improve the relevant smart features after you have turned the setting off.

Learn how Google Chat protects you

Google Chat scans files and messages to help protect you from spam, phishing, and malware.

Types of files & messages scanned

An antivirus scan is automatically done on files uploaded in Google Chat. If Google Chat finds malware, or the file type isn’t allowed for attachments:

  • Google Chat warns you.
  • Google Chat prevents downloads of the file. Learn more about file types blocked in Google Chat.

Learn how Google detects & reports online child sex abuse

Google Chat detects online child sexual abuse under the Regulation (EU) 2021/1232, which provides for a derogation from the confidentiality of communications under Articles 5(1) and 6(1) of the Directive 2002/58/EC for the purpose of combating online child sexual abuse.

Google does not allow the use of our services to create, upload, or distribute content that exploits or abuses children. To keep our service safe we use technology (i.e. hash matching) to detect such content. If we find such content, we will take appropriate action, which may include removing the content and disabling accounts. Users whose accounts are disabled are provided with information on available redress avenues if the user disagrees with our decision. Users within the European Union can also lodge a complaint to their country’s relevant data protection authority and they have the right to seek a judicial remedy as laid out in the Regulation 2021/1232.

Relevant information, which may include personal information and the violative content, is reported to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC), which in turn forwards reports to law enforcement authorities around the world, as appropriate.

Restrict message requests for personal accounts

For personal accounts, you can choose to restrict messages from unknown senders in Chat.

Report Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery

If you find intimate images or videos shared without an individual’s consent, you can report it to Google Chat.

After you submit a report, our teams review the content. If our team confirms the content is NCII, they remove it.

To prevent NCII from being uploaded or shared again in Google Chat, our system also scans for content we previously identified as NCII.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open the conversation with the message you want to report.
  • Hover over the message with the image or video attachment.
  • Click More actions Copy message link.
  • From the conversation menu, select Blocking & reporting.
  • In the pop-up, click Report non-consensual intimate imagery.
  • Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the report. If prompted, include the copied link.

Report abuse in Gemini in Workspace apps

Important: This article only applies for reporting abuse about Gemini responses. For general feedback about Gemini responses, use Good suggestion or Bad suggestion . The terms in the feedback flow will apply when you submit general feedback.

If you get inaccurate or unsafe responses in Gemini in Workspace apps, you have the option to report them to us. Your feedback helps make Gemini in Workspace apps more helpful, accurate, and safe.

When you report a response, such as spam, fraud, or illegal content, your conversation with Gemini is added to your report, including:

  • Prompts

  • Context documents, emails, and other content

  • The response from Gemini To report abuse in Gemini in a Workspace app:

  • Next to a response, select the Report abuse option.

    • If you can’t find Report abuse, select More options .

  • Select the reason you wish to report content.

  • Click Report. Tip: You can also report a legal issue here.

Restrict messages from unknown senders in Chat

To increase security and reduce the number of unwanted messages, which includes spam, you can restrict Chat message requests from unknown senders in 1:1 conversations and spaces.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings .
  • To choose who can message you in:
    • 1:1 conversations: Under “Who can message you?,” select:
      • Anyone: You can receive invitations from anyone.
      • Known senders only: For increased security, you can receive invitations only if the sender is in your contacts or if you’ve interacted with them before. Other invitations go to the spam folder.
    • Spaces: Under “Who can invite you to spaces?,” select:
      • Anyone: You can receive invitations from anyone.
      • Known senders only: For increased security, you can receive invitations only if the sender is in your contacts or if you’ve interacted with them before. Other invitations go to the spam folder.

Add formatting to your Google Chat messages

To change the appearance of your Chat messages, you can use the format menu, use markdown formatting, or add block quotes.

Format Google Chat messages

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Go to a conversation.
  • Enter a message.
  • Highlight the text you want to format.
  • Click Format or select one of the formatting options on the floating toolbar.
  • Select an option:
    • To strikethrough: Click Strikethrough .
    • To bold: Click Bold .
    • To italicize: Click Italic .
    • To underline: Click Underline .
    • To change the text color: Click Text color .
    • To add a bullet point before the text: Click Bulleted list .
    • To add a “1.” before the text: Click Numbered list .
    • To highlight a text or citation: Click Block quote .
    • To insert a link:
      • Click Insert link .
      • Enter the link.
    • To add inline code: Click Code .
    • To add multi-line code block: Click Code block .
  • Tip: You can also use markdown formatting to add styling to your messages. Learn more about how to use markdown formatting in Google Chat.
  • Click Send . Tip: To remove a text format, highlight the text and repeat steps 5 and 6.

Use markdown formatting in Google Chat

You can use markdown formatting to add styling to your messages using special characters.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • As you type your message, add characters to update the formatting of your text: Format option

  • You can choose to have live markdown on or off. If you turn off live markdown, after you send the message, the text converts to the format. Turn live markdown on or off in Google Chat

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click Chat and Meet Manage chat settings.

  • On the left, click Message & Media.

  • Turn Live Markdown on or off. Turn live markdown on or off in Chat for Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings .

  • On the left, click Message & Media.

  • Turn Live Markdown on or off.

  • If you turn off this setting, you can include special characters in the text. After you send the message, the text converts to the format.

Add block quotes

To highlight key text or citations in your Chat messages, use block quotes.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Go to a conversation.
  • Enter a message.
  • To format the text, highlight it.
  • To use a block quote, click Formatting options Block quote enter a message.
    • Or, you can:
      • Enter a message.
      • Highlight the text you want to format.
      • Click Formatting options Block quote .
  • Click Send .

Create nested and mixed lists

Note: You can only compose nested and mixed lists on the web. Mobile users can view these lists, but can’t create them.

  • Indent a list item: At the start of any bullet or number in a list (except the first item), press Tab to indent that line.
  • Nested bulleted lists: You can create up to 3 levels of nested bulleted lists with distinct symbols per level:
    • Level 1: Filled Circle
    • Level 2: Open Circle
    • Level 3: Square
  • Numbered lists: Numbered lists cycle symbols through levels and support automatic splitting and merging when lines are added or removed.
    • Level 1: 1.
    • Level 2: a.
    • Level 3: i.
  • Mixed lists: You can nest numbered lists inside bulleted lists and vice versa.
