Block & report someone

If you don’t want to chat with someone in Google Chat, you can block and report them. You can block direct messages, or block people in spaces and most group messages.

Learn what happens when you block someone

  • If you use a Google Workspace account and the person you blocked is in your organization, they can still tell when you’re online.

  • The person you blocked can’t send you messages. For them to send you a message, you need to unblock them.

  • The messages of a person you’ve blocked are hidden from you in spaces and group messages. You can unhide messages you want to find.

  • A person you’ve blocked can still read any messages sent to the space.

  • You and the person you blocked can’t edit any old messages to one another.

  • The person is also blocked in certain other Google services.

  • Links or attachments the person sent before you blocked them are still active.

  • If you report someone for abuse, a copy of the last 50 messages of your conversation is sent to Google for review.

  • You can download messages from a blocked user from your Google Account. Learn how to download your Google data. In Google Chat or Gmail, you can choose to:

  • Block someone

  • Unblock someone

  • Block & report a direct message

  • Block & unblock someone in a direct message or space

Block someone in Chat or Gmail

How to block & report someone in Chat

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • In your conversation list, next to someone’s name, click More options Block & Report.
    • If you have a work or school account and the person is in your organization, this option is Block.
  • Optional: To report someone for abuse, check the box next to “Report to Google.”
    • If you have a work or school account, you can only report people outside your organization.
  • To confirm, click Block.

Unblock someone in Chat or Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Choose an option:
    • In Chat, at the top, click Settings Manage blocked users.
    • In Gmail, at the top, click Settings See all settings Chat and Meet. Then click Manage chat settings Access Restrictions Manage blocked users. Manage blocked users
  • Select the person from the suggestions.
  • Click Unblock .

Block & report a direct message

You can choose to block a 1:1 direct message or a group direct message rather than block a person. You can also block and report a space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • In Chat, next to the conversation name, click More options Block & Report.
    • If you have a work or school account, this option is “Block this conversation.”
  • Optional: To report the conversation for abuse, check the box next to “Report this space as spam or abuse.”
    • If you have a work or school account, you can only report people outside your organization.
  • To confirm, click Block.

Block or unblock someone in a direct message or space

Important: You can block someone in the same conversation without messaging them directly.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • In Chat, open a conversation.
  • At the top, click the direct message or space name View members.
    • In spaces, click the space name Manage members.
  • Next to the person’s name, click More options Block or Unblock. Tip: To hide someone’s messages after you block them in a space, you may need to refresh your browser.

Block an app creator

If an app is spammy or abusive, you can block its creator. You’ll need their email address, which is available in the app’s warning badge.

Important: You can only block unverified, consumer-built chat apps that are not published to Google Workspace Marketplace.

Find the developer’s email address
  • In an app message in Google Chat, select the “Unverified app” warning badge.
  • Hover over the warning badge and you’ll see the creator’s email address in a popup message.
Use the email address to block

  1. Click the space name Manage members.

  2. On the “Space members” page, locate the email address of the app creator.

  3. Next to the app creator’s name, select Block.

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • In your conversation list, tap and hold a direct message Block & report.
    • If you have a work or school account and the person is in your organization, this option is Block.
  • Optional: To report the person for abuse, check the box next to “Also report.”
    • If you have a work or school account, you can only report people outside of your organization.
  • To confirm, tap Block.

Unblock someone in Chat or Gmail

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • In the top left, tap Menu Settings.
  • After opening Settings, select your email address.
  • Tap Manage blocked users Unblock .
    • In Gmail: Tap Manage blocked users Unblock . Manage blocked users

Block & report direct message

You can choose to block a 1:1 direct message or a group direct message rather than block a person. You can also block and report a space.

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • In your conversation list, tap and hold a direct message.
  • Tap Block & report.
    • If you have a work or school account, this option is “Block this conversation.”
  • Optional: To report the conversation for abuse, check the box next to “Report this space as spam or abuse.”
    • If you have a work or school account, you can only report people outside your organization.
  • To confirm, tap Block.

Block or unblock someone in a direct message or space

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • Select a direct message or space.
  • At the top, tap the conversation name Manage members.
  • Next to the person’s name, tap More options Block or Unblock.

Create a meeting in Google Chat

You can schedule a Google Calendar meeting and share a link to the meeting in Google Chat.

When you share the meeting, an event card appears in the message with the meeting title, date, and time.

Schedule & share a Calendar meeting

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • In Chat, open a message.

  • In the reply area, click Google Workspace tools Calendar invite.

    • You can also type /calendar in the reply area to create a meeting invite.

  • On the right, in the side panel, enter your meeting details.

  • Click Save & share Send. Tips:

  • If you have smart features turned on, you can schedule meetings using inline meeting intent. When someone asks to meet, Gemini suggests a possible meeting time and can schedule the meeting for you. Learn how to use Smart Actions in Google Chat.

  • If you remove someone from a meeting invitation, but they’re still in the chat, they can view the event card.

  • You can also share a link to a video meeting in Chat. Learn how to create a video meeting.

Related resources

  • Add or remove a video conference from your Calendar event
  • Start a video meeting

Edit or delete a message in Google Chat

Important: This page provides instructions on how to edit or delete messages in Google Chat. To learn how to do this in Google Messages, go to Update an RCS sent message in the Google Messages Help Center.

If you make a mistake or need to update a message, you can edit or delete the message.

When you edit a message:

  • You can’t go back to the previous edit or the original message.

  • Chat notifications may include the original message. When you delete a message:

  • The message is permanently removed from your Google Account and can’t be recovered.

  • You can’t undo the message deletion.

Edit a sent message

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.
  • Open a conversation, such as a direct message, group direct message, or space.
  • Hover over the message you want to edit.
  • Click Edit .
  • Make your changes.
  • Click Update.

Delete a sent message

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.
  • Open a conversation, such as a direct message, group direct message, or space.
  • Hover over the message you want to delete.
  • Click More Delete .
  • To confirm, click Delete.

Learn why you can’t edit or delete a message

  • You can delete messages from apps, but you can’t edit them.
  • If you use a personal account, you can’t delete messages when:
    • You’re in a space a different organization started.
    • You send a direct or group message to a Google Workspace account.

Related resources

  • Hide or delete a conversation
  • How to download your Google data

Forward a message from Chat to Gmail

You can forward a message from Google Chat to your Gmail inbox. The email includes the last 4 messages in the conversation thread. Later, if you turn chat history off, the messages stay in your inbox.

The email may take up to 2 minutes to appear in your inbox.

Tips:

  • If you forward messages that are more than 25 MB to your inbox, the attachments aren’t included.
  • Chat app messages in cards won’t forward to Gmail inbox.
  • Point to the message and click Forward to inbox .
  • Go to your Gmail inbox to find the forwarded messages.

Related resources

  • Turn history on or off in Google Chat
  • Pin a conversation

Forward a message in Google Chat

You can forward important messages in Google Chat to people, spaces, Chat apps, or AI agents like Ask Gemini. This allows you to:

  • Quickly relay information
  • Share updates without needing to add them to another chat
  • Bring a message to a new conversation and provide context to a connected app or agent without copying and pasting the original text

Forward a message

Some restrictions apply to forwarding, depending on the sender and receiver.

You can forward a message:

  • From people outside your organization into your internal conversations. You can’t forward a message:

  • From internal conversations to external conversations

  • From external conversations to other external conversations Note: When forwarding a message, you can’t select multiple apps at once, and you can’t combine app or agent selections with human contacts or spaces.

  • On your computer, go to Google Chatand select a direct message or space.

  • Hover over the message you want to share.

  • Select More Actions Forward message .

  • Search for and select where you want to forward the message. You can send to human contacts, spaces, Chat apps, or AI agents. Visual badges and attribution identify AI agents and Chat apps in the suggestions.

    • When you forward a message from a DM or group DM, a reminder about sensitive information appears.

  • Select Next.

    • Optional: You can add your own message before you share the forwarded message.

  • Select Send message . Tips:

  • To send any attachments or images included in the original message, forward the message.

  • To increase the message’s visibility, forward a message from a thread to the main stream of the same space.

Related resources

  • Create, send & reply to messages in Google Chat
  • Forward a message from Chat to Gmail
  • Pin messages, files & links in spaces & messages

Hide or delete a 1:1 direct message

You can hide or delete a conversation between you and another person in Google Chat and Chat in Gmail.

  • Hide a 1:1 direct message
    • Hides your copy of a conversation, but doesn’t remove the conversation for other participants.
    • If you hide a conversation with someone and then message them again, the conversation chat history shows up again.
  • Delete a 1:1 direct message
    • Permanently hides the conversation history from your view. The content remains visible to the other participant. You can also choose to edit or delete a specific message. If you edit or delete a sent message, it updates the message for you and other participants in the conversation.

Hide a conversation or space

You can hide a 1:1 direct message, a group direct message, or a space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Hover over the 1:1 or group direct message name.
  • Click Options Hide conversation.
Hide a space
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Hover over the Space name.
  • Click Options Hide Space.

Delete a 1:1 direct message

Important: You can’t delete a group direct message with more than 2 participants.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Hover over the person’s name.
  • Click More Delete conversation .
  • To confirm, click Delete. To delete a single message instead of a conversation, learn how to edit or delete a message in Google Chat.

  • Edit or delete a message in Google Chat
  • Block & report someone
  • Respond to a Google Chat message request

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .

  • In the bottom navigation menu, tap Direct messages .

Insert smart chips in Google Chat

In Chat, type “@” with a keyword to insert a smart chip:

  • To tag someone to get their attention, enter “@” and their name or email address. When the correct person is suggested, click their name.

  • To access and interact with installed apps, enter “@” and the name of the app. Click when the correct app is suggested.

  • To search for and share files relevant to the conversation, enter “@”and the name of your file. Click when the correct file is suggested.

  • To reference or link to a specific space, enter “@” and the name of the space. Click when the correct space is suggested. Important: When you mention a user in a smart chip, they don’t automatically get access to your document. To grant access to another user, you must share your document.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

    • Type “@,” then select from the suggestions or enter letters, numbers, or symbols.

Learn about custom emojis in Google Chat

Create and share custom emojis with your organization through Google Chat. Use your custom emojis to personalize messages and share your team’s culture.

Important:

  • Custom emojis are only available for work and school accounts.
  • Your administrator can turn custom emojis on or off. Find out who your administrator is.
  • You can’t share custom emojis with people outside your organization.

Create a custom emoji

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Open a chat conversation.
  • At the bottom right, click Add emoji .
  • Next to “Search emojis,” click Create Upload image Save.

Use custom emojis in Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Open a chat conversation.
  • At the bottom right, click Add emoji .
  • Click on Custom emojis to open all of your organization’s custom emojis. Tip: You can hover over a custom emoji to see its name.

Find your custom emojis

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Open a chat conversation.
  • At the bottom right, click Add emoji .
  • Click Custom emojis Manage. Tip: You can search for custom emojis by name.

Delete your custom emojis

Important:

  • When you delete a custom emoji, it’s removed for everyone in your organization. The emoji is replaced in messages or reactions.

  • You can only delete custom emojis you create.

  • Emoji managers can delete custom emojis created by anyone in the organization. To delete a custom emoji:

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or Gmail.

  • Open a chat conversation.

  • At the bottom right, click Add emoji .

  • Click Custom emojis Manage.

  • To the right of the emoji, click Delete Delete.

Find custom emojis in your organization

As an emoji manager, you can:

  • Find custom emojis people in your organization create.
  • Spot the emoji’s:
    • Image
    • Name
    • Creator’s name
    • Creation date To find a custom emoji:
  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Click Settings Manage custom emoji. Tip: You can search for emojis by name in the search bar.

Delete custom emojis in your organization

As an emoji manager, you can delete emojis that are problematic or don’t meet your organization’s guidelines.

Important: Deleted emojis are removed from messages and reactions. No one in the organization can share or use them.

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Click Settings Manage custom emoji.
  • To the right of the emoji you want to delete, click More actions Delete emoji Delete.

  • Click Settings Manage custom emoji. Tip: You can search for emojis by name in the search bar.

Delete custom emojis in your organization

As an emoji manager, you can delete emojis that are problematic or don’t meet your organization’s guidelines.

Important: Deleted emojis are removed from messages and reactions. No one in the organization can share or use them.

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Click Settings Manage custom emoji.
  • To the right of the emoji you want to delete, click More actions Delete emoji Delete.

Learn about custom emojis in Google Chat (iPhone and iPad)

Create and share custom emojis with your organization through Google Chat. Use your custom emojis to personalize messages and share your team’s culture.

Important:

  • Custom emojis are only available for work and school accounts.
  • Your administrator can turn custom emojis on or off. Find out who your administrator is.
  • You can’t share custom emojis with people outside your organization.

Use custom emojis in Chat

  • On your iPhone or iPad, go to the Google Chat app or to the Chat tab in the Gmail app .
  • Tap on a chat conversation.
  • At the bottom right, tap Add emoji .
  • Tap on Custom emojis to open all of your organization’s custom emojis.

Find your custom emojis

  • On your iPhone or iPad, go to the Google Chat app or to the Chat tab in the Gmail app .
  • Tap on a chat conversation.
  • At the bottom right, tap Add emoji .
  • Tap Custom emojis Manage. Tip: You can search for custom emojis by name.

Learn about huddles in Google Chat

Important: Only users with a work account can access huddles in Chat, which aren’t available for personal or school accounts.

  • You can start a huddle instantly as a voice chat from a 1:1 conversation, group conversation, or space in Google Chat without ringing.
  • You can share your screen or turn on your camera in a huddle.
  • You can also choose to start a video meeting or call someone directly from Chat or Gmail. Learn more about how to start a video meeting or call someone.

Start a huddle in Chat

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Open a direct message or space.

  • At the top right, click the dropdown click Huddles .

  • To end the call, click End call . Tips:

  • If participants are in a huddle, it remains active.

  • Someone can join a huddle anytime through a huddle invitation chip as long as the person who started the huddle is in it.

Join a huddle

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • You can join a huddle from your list of conversations or from a direct message or space:
    • To join from your list of conversations: click the huddle icon next to the name or space name.
    • To join from within a conversation:
      • Open a conversation.
      • At the top right, click Huddles . Turn cameras on or share your screen in a huddle

By default, the huddle opens as a voice chat.

  • To change the voice chat to a video chat, click Turn on camera .
    • Tip: If someone in the huddle turns on their camera, a video badge displays next to their profile picture.
  • To share your screen, click Present now . Resize your huddle window

To resize a huddle, at the bottom left, drag the handle .

Tip: The huddle window automatically resizes if someone turns on their camera or you click the presentation tile .

Switch from a Chat huddle to Google Meet

To switch from a Chat huddle to Google Meet, at the top right, click Open Meet in tab .

Change background effects

To use a background effect in a huddle, hover over your video, then click Apply visual effects .

Send an emoji reaction

To send an emoji reaction in a huddle, click More Send a reaction .

Related resources

  • Start a video meeting
  • Create a meeting in Google Chat

Start a huddle in Chat

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .

    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .

  • Open a direct message or space.

  • To start a huddle with the members of the chat or space:

    • In a 1:1 conversation: At the top right, tap Call Start a huddle .
    • In a group conversation or a space: At the top right, tap Send a Meet link Start a huddle .

  • To end the call, tap End call . Tips:

Mention someone or add someone to a message

To get someone’s attention in Google Chat or to add them to a message, enter “@” before their name. If the person is already in the conversation, they get a notification. If they aren’t, you can either mention and add them to the conversation, or choose to just “reference” them and not add them to the conversation.

Mention someone in a conversation

  • When writing a message, enter @.
  • Enter a person’s name.
  • If the person isn’t already in the conversation, you can:
    • Add member and send: Add the user to the conversation and send the message. The user gets a notification.
    • Send message only: Send the message, but don’t add them to the conversation. This option simply references them and doesn’t notify them. Tips:
  • To mention more than one person in the same message, enter each of their names.
  • To mention everyone in a message, enter @all.
  • If a new member is added to the conversation, they can access all previously posted content.
  • You can only add members to a conversation in group direct messages and spaces. In 1:1 conversations, when you mention someone, they are treated as a reference and not added directly.
  • If an app is mentioned in a conversation, it must be added to it and not just referenced.

Mention someone in a message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • Select a message you want to edit.
  • From the pop-up menu, click Edit .
  • Enter @.
  • Enter a person’s name, a file name, or a space name.
  • From the suggestion menu, select a person’s name, a file name, or a space name you want to mention.

Locate your mentions

When someone mentions you, your name is highlighted in their message.

To find all conversations where you’re mentioned, go to Mentions in Chat.

  • On the left, click Mentions.
  • Click a message where you’re mentioned.
Learn how newly mentioned users are notified

  • If you mention a new user in a threaded message, they start to follow the message topic.

  • If a newly mentioned user isn’t in the space, a confirmation dialog adds the user to the space.

  • Only newly mentioned users receive push notifications for an edited message. If a user already received a notification for the message before the edit, they don’t get another one. Existing notifications don’t update. Important: Some messages don’t show in Mentions, including:

  • Messages that mention @all.

  • Messages in spaces organized by conversation topics.

Related resources

  • Send a message in Google Chat
  • Reply to a chat message

Pin messages, files & links in spaces & messages

You can pin your important messages, files, links, images, and videos in spaces and in direct messages with an individual or group with the Board tab in Chat.

  • Pin what’s important: You can place important messages, files, links, images, and videos on the Board.
  • Access key items easily: To make sure that everything is neatly organized and easily curated, the Board is readily available at the right panel.
  • Save time: To save time, important messages and files are always easily accessible.
  • Use smart suggestions: To save time, use the suggestions feature to quickly find the best and most relevant files to pin.

Open a Chat board

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • Open any conversation or space.
  • At the top right, click Board .

Pin or unpin a message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • Open any conversation or space.
  • Click the message you want to pin More actions Pin to board .
    • To unpin, click Unpin .

Pin a file or link

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • In Chat, open any conversation or space.
  • At the top right, click Board Add resource .
  • To upload a file from Drive, select Upload or attach from Drive.
    • Select the file name.
    • Click Insert.
    • In the pop up, to give access, select Share with people.
    • Click Share.
  • To add a URL, select Link.
    • In the pop up, enter the link and the link title.
    • Click Add Link.

Reply to a message in Google Chat

There are several ways to reply to a message in Google Chat. You can:

  • Reply in the conversation.
  • Reply in a thread to a message in a conversation.
  • Quote a message in your reply.
  • Use a reply suggestion.
  • React to a message.

Respond to a message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a conversation.
  • In the reply area, enter your message.
  • Click Send .

Reply in a thread

Important: You can reply to any messages. Your reply creates a separate thread. Learn more about threads in Chat conversation.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Select a conversation.
  • Select a reply option through the:
    • Thread icon:
      • Hover over the message.
      • Click Reply in the Thread .
    • Reply button: At the bottom of a space message, click Reply.
      • You can find this option only in spaces, not in DMs.
      • Tip: If the thread has replies, under the main message, click the indicator that shows the number of replies.
  • In the Thread panel, enter your message.
  • Click Send . Tip: To find all threads in a group, at the top right, click Thread .

Quote a message in your reply

Important: When you quote a message, the quoted content displays the original message. If the original message is deleted or edited, the quoted content isn’t updated in your reply.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a conversation.
  • Point to the message.
  • From the available message actions, click Quote in reply .
  • Enter your message.
  • Click Send .

Get suggestions for quick replies

To respond to messages quickly, turn on Smart Reply. When Smart Reply is on, you can find suggestions above the reply area in Chat.

Turn on Smart Reply in Chat
  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings .
  • Under “Smart Reply,” click the box.
Turn on Smart Reply in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click Chat and Meet Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Smart Reply,” click the box. Tips:

  • To reply, select a suggestion below the message. You can edit the suggestion before you reply.

  • Before you can turn on Smart Reply, enable smart features and personalization in Gmail. Learn more about smart features & controls.

Auto-save & sync message drafts

Google Chat automatically saves your unsent messages as drafts across your computer and mobile devices in the conversation compose box and in a new Drafts shortcut. This allows you to start a message on one device and finish it on another.

This feature is available to all Google Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts.

Draft messages are automatically saved when you:

  • Pause typing for 5 seconds.

  • Switch to a different window or application where Google Chat is not in focus.

  • Navigate to another screen within Google Chat, such as your chat list or Home. Access and manage drafts:

  • In Chat, in the left sidebar, select Drafts to view and manage all active drafts.

  • Note: If you have no active drafts, this shortcut won’t be visible.

  • Select a draft. You can edit a draft, which opens the conversation with the draft pre-filled, or delete it.

  • Optional: You can access drafts from your chats. When you open a conversation, any saved draft for that conversation automatically appears in the compose box and a new draft icon appears next to conversations that have an unsent draft. This icon takes priority over other indicators like pinned conversations or meeting notifications. Important:

  • Google Chat can store up to 100 drafts. When this limit is reached, the oldest draft is removed to make space for new ones.

  • Drafts are kept for 30 days from the last time they were edited.

  • Mark a conversation as read or unread

To respond to messages quickly, turn on Smart Reply. When Smart Reply is on, you can find suggestions above the reply area in Chat.

Turn on Smart Reply in Chat
  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app .
  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings.
  • Next to “Smart reply,” tap the toggle.
Turn on Smart Reply in Gmail

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Gmail app .

  • At the top left, tap Menu Settings.

  • Tap Smart reply.

  • Next to “Smart reply in chat,” tap the box. Tips:

  • To reply, select a suggestion below the message. You can edit the suggestion before you reply.

  • Before you can turn on Smart Reply, enable smart features and personalization in Gmail. Learn more about smart features & controls.

Auto-save & sync message drafts

Google Chat automatically saves your unsent messages as drafts across your computer and mobile devices in the conversation compose box and in a new Drafts shortcut. This allows you to start a message on one device and finish it on another.

This feature is available to all Google Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts.

Draft messages are automatically saved when you:

  • Pause typing for 5 seconds.

  • Switch to a different window or application where Google Chat is not in focus.

  • Navigate to another screen within Google Chat, such as your chat list or Home. Access and manage drafts:

  • In Chat, in the left sidebar, select Drafts to view and manage all active drafts.

  • Note: If you have no active drafts, this shortcut won’t be visible.

  • Select a draft. You can edit a draft, which opens the conversation with the draft pre-filled, or delete it.

  • Optional: You can access drafts from your chats. When you open a conversation, any saved draft for that conversation automatically appears in the compose box and a new draft icon appears next to conversations that have an unsent draft. This icon takes priority over other indicators like pinned conversations or meeting notifications. Important:

  • Google Chat can store up to 100 drafts. When this limit is reached, the oldest draft is removed to make space for new ones.

  • Drafts are kept for 30 days from the last time they were edited.

Report messages in Google Chat

You can report messages that are inappropriate or that violate your organization’s guidelines in Google Chat. This feature is only available in:

  • Google Workspace for Education Standard

  • Google Workspace for Education Plus

  • Google Workspace Enterprise Plus Important:

  • Before you can report messages, your admin must turn on Chat content reporting for your organization.

  • Your admin sets up the types of messages that you can report in Chat. If you don’t see the option to report a message, you won’t be able to send the message to your admin for review.

  • You can only report messages sent in your organization. Chat history must be turned on in the conversation.

Report a specific message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a conversation.
  • Hover over the message.
  • From the available message actions, click More options Report.
  • Enter your feedback.
  • Click Submit report.
    • The report is sent to your admin to review.

Related resources

  • Manage content reporting for Chat
  • Block and report someone
  • Block or report a space in Google Chat & Gmail

Respond to a Google Chat message request

In Google Chat, you don’t have to chat with people you don’t know. The first time someone sends you a direct message, you get a request. If you use Google Chat with a Google Workspace account, you may get requests from people within your organization. You can accept requests or ignore them.

What happens when you accept or ignore a message

If you accept a message request
  • The requester can view your basic profile details (name, avatar, email address) and can tell if you’re online.
  • You can view all attachments that the person sends and reply to their messages.
  • The requestor can add you to chat spaces.
If you ignore a message request
  • The message goes away. To find the request again, search for the person in Google Chat. You may need to use their email address when you search.
  • The requestor can’t tell you ignored them.
  • You can block the requestor from sending you more requests. Learn how to block a person.

Spam message requests

Google Chat filters messages requests that appear to be spam into a separate section. You can accept or block messages that are marked spam.

Accept or ignore a chat message request in Chat or Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Click New chat Message requests.
  • Click the name. Their message appears with the request.
  • Click Accept or Ignore.
    • Optional: To stop additional message requests from a person, click Also block Ignore.

Related resources

  • Block and report someone

Search for Google Chat messages

In Google Chat, you can search:

  • In all your messages.

  • For messages that include specific people.

  • For messages that include certain types of content, such as images. Important:

  • To search for Chat messages in Gmail, turn on Chat in Gmail.

  • You can search for messages in conversations you joined or can join.

  • To filter your search results, you can also use search operators.

  • You can’t search for messages using the Gmail API.

  • Even if you’re invited to join, you can’t search for messages in conversations or spaces that someone from a different organization created.

Search for messages in Chat & Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • At the top, click the search box.
  • Enter search text.
    • For Gmail: You can also use the search operatorin:chats.
  • Select an option:
    • For Gmail: Under the search box, click Conversations.
    • Select a recent search.
  • To open a result, click it.

Search for messages in a space or conversation

  • In Chat, select the space or conversation you want to search.
  • At the top right, click Search in this chat .
  • Enter search text.
  • Select an option:
    • Press Enter.
    • Select a recent search.
  • To open a result, click it.

Filter & sort messages

  • In Chat, at the top, click the search box.
  • Enter search text.
    • As you enter text, suggestions appear below. Press “tab” to autofill the rest of a query.
  • Press Enter.
  • Select a filter to find the following types of messages:
    • From: Messages sent from specific people.
    • Said in: Messages said in a specific conversation or space.
    • Date: Messages sent during a specific date range.
    • Has file: Messages that include documents, spreadsheets, slides, and more.
    • Has link: Messages that include links.
    • Mentions me: Messages that mention you.
    • Only conversations I’m in: Messages from conversations that you’re a member of.
  • Optional: To sort messages, below the filters, click Sort menu.
    • Most relevant: Sort messages by how relevant they are to your search text.
    • Most recent: Sort messages by how recent they are.
  • To open a result, click it.
    • Results from spaces you haven’t joined may appear. To join, next to the message, click Join.

Delete suggested search results

When you enter text in the Chat search bar, suggestions may appear based on your search history. To find messages, you can select a suggestion.

  • Suggestions are stored for 90 days after use.
  • Search history for suggestions isn’t shared between Chat and Chat in Gmail.
  • You can delete your recent searches or your entire search history.
  • In Chat, click the Search bar.
  • Under “Recent searches,” you can:
    • Delete a recent search: Click a search Delete.
    • Delete all searches: Click Delete all.

Fix issues to find Google Chat messages

  • Check if history was turned off for the Chat conversation.
    • If Chat history was turned off, then the messages were permanently deleted.
  • For work or school accounts, and for anyone in a 1:1 direct message with a work or school account user: Messages may not be available after a certain time period. This depends on the retention policy of the organization of the person who started the direct message. Learn about message history for conversations with work or school accounts.

  • Optional: You can access drafts from your chats. When you open a conversation, any saved draft for that conversation automatically appears in the compose box and a new draft icon appears next to conversations that have an unsent draft. Send & share files in Google Chat messages

You can attach files up to 200 MB from your computer, mobile device, or Google Drive directly to Google Chat messages.

In spaces, you can view a list of files shared with the space, open files, and add them to Drive.

Supported image files:

  • BMP
  • GIF
  • JPEG
  • PNG
  • WBMP
  • HEIC You can’t send certain files. Read File types blocked in Chat below.

Send files in a chat message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Open a conversation.
  • If you’re in Gmail, on the side, click Chat.
  • Enter your message and choose an option:
  • Add an emoji
  • Click Emoji .
  • Send a GIF
  • Click GIF .
    • If you use Google Chat on a work or school account, you may not have the option to send a GIF.
  • Attach files from your computer
  • Click Upload file and drag files into the compose bar.
  • Tip: You can attach up to 20 images or videos at a time or one attachment of other file types.
  • Add a link to a video meeting
  • Click Add video meeting .
  • Attach a Drive file
  • Click Add Drive.
    • When you send the file, you’re notified if someone needs access.
    • If you have edit access, you have an option to grant access.
    • If you grant access to a conversation or space, people who join the space later also have access.
    • If people leave the space, they lose access to the file unless they’re given access individually or through a group.
  • Create a Google Calendar invite
  • Click Add Calendar invite .
  • Click Send . Insert files from Drive in a chat message

To add files from Drive in your message, add “@” followed by the name of your file.

  • In the reply area of the conversation, type “@.”
    • To search for more related files, you can enter the filename or related keywords after “@.”
  • Under “Files,” select from the list of suggestions.
  • Click Send .
    • When you send the file, you’re notified if someone needs access.
  • Select the type of access.
    • Optional: To share access to the file with others, refer to the section To attach a Drive file. Tip: You can find file suggestions you have access to from your Drive.

Manage files, links & media in conversations & spaces

In 1:1 conversations, group conversations, and spaces, you can find a list of shared files, links, and media. You can open a file and add a file to Drive.

  • If you delete a chat message with a shared file, it’s also deleted from the conversation or space.

  • If you delete a file in Drive, the file link remains in the conversation or space until you delete it from the chat message.

  • When you delete the file from the chat message, the file link is removed from the chat and the “Shared” tab of the conversation or space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail, on the left, click Chat.

  • Select a conversation or space.

  • At the top, click Shared .

    • Tip: In Gmail, you might have to expand the space to view the Shared tab.

  • To open the file, click the name of the file.

    • Google files: File opens in the chat window, next to the conversation, or opens in a new browser tab.
    • Other types of files: File opens as a preview in full screen. Files not in Drive will download, except PDF and video files, which open in a new browser tab.

  • Optional: To add the file to your Google Drive, next to the file, click More actions Add shortcut to Drive. Tips:

  • If you can’t add files to Drive and you use a Google Workspace account, contact your administrator.

  • To find all files and links in a conversation or space, click View all files or View all links.

Remove a file from a conversation or space

Important: To remove a file from a conversation or space, you must use a Google Workspace account.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail, on the left, click Chat.

  • Select a conversation or space.

  • At the top right, click Shared More actions View in conversation.

  • Hover over the message with the file.

  • Click More actions Delete Delete. Tips:

  • If you delete a file in Drive, the file link remains in the conversation or space until you delete it from the chat message.

    • If you don’t delete it from the chat, the file link will show a “File in Trash” message when you select it.
    • If you don’t delete it from the chat and Drive trash is emptied, you won’t be able to open the file from the file link.

  • When you delete the file from the chat message, the file link is removed from chat and your shared files.

Collaborate on Google Docs & Sheets

Important:

  • To work with comments or use other features from Docs or Sheets, open the file in a new tab.

  • If your chat window is not in full screen, click Open chat in full screen . You can collaborate on shared Google Docs and Sheets with people directly in a conversation or space. Next to the conversation, the document or spreadsheet opens in the chat window, where you can chat while you collaborate on the file together. You can edit, format, share, and rename the document or spreadsheet without leaving Gmail or Google Chat.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

  • In Chat, select a conversation or space.

    • To open an already shared document, point to it in the chat, then click Open in chat . The document opens to the right where you can make edits directly without changing tabs.
    • To create a shared document within a space, in the reply area of the “Chat” tab, click Action menu Google Docs .

  • At the top right, click Close .

  • Optional: To open the document in a new browser tab, at the top right of the conversation preview, click Open in a new tab . Tips:

  • If you can’t add documents and you use a Google Workspace account, contact your administrator.

  • You can collaborate on existing Google Docs and Sheets in 1:1 messages.

File types blocked in Google Chat

There are several reasons why you might get an upload error in Google Chat. Chat blocks files or links that might spread viruses, such as executable files. To keep up with harmful software, Chat regularly updates the file types that aren’t allowed.

You can’t attach certain types of files. These include:

  • ADE, ADP, APK, BAT, CAB, CHM, CMD, COM, CPL, DLL, DMG, EXE, HTA, INS, ISP, JAR, JS, JSE, LIB, LNK, MDE, MSC, MSI, MSP, MST, NSH, PIF, SCR, SCT, SHB, SYS, VB, VBE, VBS, VXD, WSC, WSF, and WSH.
  • This list includes any compressed form, such as GZ or BZ2 files, or files found in archives, such as ZIP or TGZ files.
  • Documents with malicious macros.
  • Password-protected archives whose content is an archive. If a blocked file isn’t listed above and you’re sure the blocked file is safe, upload the file to Drive and then send the file as a Drive attachment.

Send & share files in Google Chat messages (Computer)

You can attach files up to 200 MB from your computer, mobile device, or Google Drive directly to Google Chat messages.

In spaces, you can view a list of files shared with the space, open files, and add them to Drive.

Supported image files:

  • BMP
  • GIF
  • JPEG
  • PNG
  • WBMP
  • HEIC You can’t send certain files. Read File types blocked in Chat below.

Send files in a chat message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Open a conversation.
  • If you’re in Gmail, on the side, click Chat.
  • Enter your message and choose an option:
  • Add an emoji
  • Click Emoji .
  • Send a GIF
  • Click GIF .
    • If you use Google Chat on a work or school account, you may not have the option to send a GIF.
  • Attach files from your computer
  • Click Upload file and drag files into the compose bar.
  • Tip: You can attach up to 20 images or videos at a time or one attachment of other file types.
  • Add a link to a video meeting
  • Click Add video meeting .
  • Attach a Drive file
  • Click Add Drive.
    • When you send the file, you’re notified if someone needs access.
    • If you have edit access, you have an option to grant access.
    • If you grant access to a conversation or space, people who join the space later also have access.
    • If people leave the space, they lose access to the file unless they’re given access individually or through a group.
  • Create a Google Calendar invite
  • Click Add Calendar invite .
  • Click Send . Insert files from Drive in a chat message

To add files from Drive in your message, add “@” followed by the name of your file.

  • In the reply area of the conversation, type “@.”
    • To search for more related files, you can enter the filename or related keywords after “@.”
  • Under “Files,” select from the list of suggestions.
  • Click Send .
    • When you send the file, you’re notified if someone needs access.
  • Select the type of access.
    • Optional: To share access to the file with others, refer to the section To attach a Drive file. Tip: You can find file suggestions you have access to from your Drive.

Manage files, links & media in conversations & spaces

In 1:1 conversations, group conversations, and spaces, you can find a list of shared files, links, and media. You can open a file and add a file to Drive.

  • If you delete a chat message with a shared file, it’s also deleted from the conversation or space.

  • If you delete a file in Drive, the file link remains in the conversation or space until you delete it from the chat message.

  • When you delete the file from the chat message, the file link is removed from the chat and the “Shared” tab of the conversation or space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail, on the left, click Chat.

  • Select a conversation or space.

  • At the top, click Shared .

    • Tip: In Gmail, you might have to expand the space to view the Shared tab.

  • To open the file, click the name of the file.

    • Google files: File opens in the chat window, next to the conversation, or opens in a new browser tab.
    • Other types of files: File opens as a preview in full screen. Files not in Drive will download, except PDF and video files, which open in a new browser tab.

  • Optional: To add the file to your Google Drive, next to the file, click More actions Add shortcut to Drive. Tips:

  • If you can’t add files to Drive and you use a Google Workspace account, contact your administrator.

  • To find all files and links in a conversation or space, click View all files or View all links.

Remove a file from a conversation or space

Important: To remove a file from a conversation or space, you must use a Google Workspace account.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail, on the left, click Chat.

  • Select a conversation or space.

  • At the top right, click Shared More actions View in conversation.

  • Hover over the message with the file.

  • Click More actions Delete Delete. Tips:

  • If you delete a file in Drive, the file link remains in the conversation or space until you delete it from the chat message.

    • If you don’t delete it from the chat, the file link will show a “File in Trash” message when you select it.
    • If you don’t delete it from the chat and Drive trash is emptied, you won’t be able to open the file from the file link.

  • When you delete the file from the chat message, the file link is removed from chat and your shared files.

Collaborate on Google Docs & Sheets

Important:

  • To work with comments or use other features from Docs or Sheets, open the file in a new tab.

  • If your chat window is not in full screen, click Open chat in full screen . You can collaborate on shared Google Docs and Sheets with people directly in a conversation or space. Next to the conversation, the document or spreadsheet opens in the chat window, where you can chat while you collaborate on the file together. You can edit, format, share, and rename the document or spreadsheet without leaving Gmail or Google Chat.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

  • In Chat, select a conversation or space.

    • To open an already shared document, point to it in the chat, then click Open in chat . The document opens to the right where you can make edits directly without changing tabs.
    • To create a shared document within a space, in the reply area of the “Chat” tab, click Action menu Google Docs .

  • At the top right, click Close .

  • Optional: To open the document in a new browser tab, at the top right of the conversation preview, click Open in a new tab . Tips:

  • If you can’t add documents and you use a Google Workspace account, contact your administrator.

  • You can collaborate on existing Google Docs and Sheets in 1:1 messages.

Start a video meeting or call someone

You can start a video meeting or call someone from Google Chat or Chat in Gmail.

If you have a work account, you can start a huddle in Chat. Learn about huddles in Google Chat.

Important: If your organization allows external users to join rooms or group conversations, anyone in the room or group can join a video meeting without permission.

Tip: To make sure you don’t join a meeting with an expired code and to better plan for the future meetings you create, check when meeting codes expire. Learn about Google Meet meeting codes.

Start a video meeting from Chat or Gmail

How to start a Google Meet video from Chat

  • On your computer, open Google Chator Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Open a conversation.

  • In the reply area, click Add video meeting Send .

    • You can also type /calendar in the reply area to create an invite to a meeting.

  • To join a video meeting, click Join video meeting Join now. Tips

  • If you have smart features turned on, you can schedule meetings using inline meeting intent. When someone asks to meet, Gemini suggests a possible meeting time and can schedule the meeting for you. Learn how to use Smart Actions in Google Chat.

  • To learn more about Meet video meetings, go to the Meet Help Center.

Call someone directly from Chat or Gmail

Important: You can call someone directly from Chat or Gmail in Chrome. If you make a call to a non-Chrome user, they can receive and join the call but they won’t hear a ring.

You can start a voice or video meeting from Chat or Gmail. When the other person receives the call, they’ll hear a ring.

  • In Chat, open a direct message.

  • At the top, click Start video call . The call opens in a small window.

  • To end the call, click End call . Tip: If you want to adjust the call window:

  • To move the call to a new tab, click Move to a tab .

  • To move, click and hold the window.

Use search operators in Google Chat

To filter your Google Chat search results, you can use words or symbols called search operators. To filter your results in detail, you can combine operators.

Search operators you can use

What you can search for

Search operator & example

Search for messages from a specific sender.

from:

Examples:

from:me

from:john@xyz.com

Tip: When you use the from: operator, suggested contacts may autocomplete. To accept a suggestion, click the contact’s name.

Search for messages that have a Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides attachment.

has:doc

has:sheet

has:slide

Search for messages that have a file, link, video, or another attachment type.

has:file

has:url

has:video

has:pdf

has:image

Search for messages that mention a specific person.

at:

Examples:

at:me

at:rashad

at:fatima@xyz.com

Search for an exact word or phrase.

" "

Examples:

"happy birthday"

"anniversary"

Exclude specific messages from search results.

-

Examples:

from:issac -from:jenny

-birthday from:jenny

-has:file from:issac

Search for messages sent within a certain time period.

after:

before:

Examples:

after:2023/04/16

before:04/18/2023

With “d” (day), “m” (month), and “y” (year), you can search for messages older or newer than a particular time period.

older_than:

newer_than:

Examples:

newer_than:2d

older_than:1y

Specify a timezone for messages sent within a time period.

tz:GMT+hh:mm

tz:GMT-hh:mm

Examples:

after:2023/01/02 before:2023/12/20 tz:GMT-05:30

newer_than:3d older_than:2d tz:GMT+05:00

Narrow results to a direct message or a space.

Narrow results to a direct message

is:dm

is:chat

Narrow results to unread messages

is:unread

Tips:

  • This search operator only shows unread main messages from conversations or spaces.
  • For replies within an inline thread, is:unread only returns unread replies from followed threads. Narrow results to a space

is:room

Examples:

happy birthday is:dm

anniversary is:room

Search for messages in a specific space.

in:&lt;space>

Examples:

apple in:recipes

apple in:(mobile phones)

apple in:”mobile phones”

Related resources

  • Search for Google Chat messages
  • Add formatting to your Google Chat messages

Use Smart Compose in Google Chat

With Smart Compose, powered by machine learning, you can write messages faster. Smart Compose offers suggestions as you enter text.

Important:

  • Smart Compose is available in English, Spanish, French, Italian, and Portuguese. Smart Compose is not designed to provide answers and may not always predict factually correct information.
  • To use Smart Compose, you must turn on smart features and controls. Learn more about Smart features & controls in Google products.

Use Smart Compose in Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings .
  • Under “Smart Compose,” check the box next to “Enable predictive writing suggestions as you compose a message on web and desktop.”

Use Smart Compose in Chat for Gmail

  • On your computer, go to Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • At the top, click Chat and Meet Manage chat settings.
  • Under “Smart Compose,” check the box next to “Enable predictive writing suggestions as you compose a message on web and desktop.” Tip: To accept a suggestion, on your keyboard, press Tab.

Learn about machine learning

As language understanding models use billions of common phrases and sentences to automatically learn about the world, they can also reflect human cognitive biases.

Being aware of this is a good start, and the conversation around how to handle it is ongoing.

Google is committed to making products that work well for everyone, and are actively researching unintended bias and mitigation strategies.

  • Smart features & controls in Google products
  • Use Smart Compose

Send a direct message

Add or remove someone in a direct message

To add someone to a direct message (DM) with two or more people in Google Chat, add them to the member list or mention them in the message.

Add people to a DM

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Open a DM.

  • At the top, click the conversation name Start a new chat.

  • Enter a name or email address.

  • Click Create. Tips:

  • To quickly add a new person to a DM with 2 or more people, in the reply area, enter @ followed by the person’s name.

  • Or, next to conversation name, click the dropdown Add people.

Remove people from a DM

Important: When you remove someone from a DM, they can’t:

  • Participate in the conversation.
  • Check message history.
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a DM.
  • At the top, next to conversation name, click the dropdown View members.
  • Next to the person’s name, click More options Remove from conversation.

Manage members in a DM created from Calendar

With continuous meeting chat, you can send messages to meeting participants before, during and after a meeting in Google Chat from a computer or mobile device. Continuous meeting chat is available to all business and enterprise users. Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

You can use the dedicated conversations from your meetings to:

  • Remind or prepare attendees for the meeting.

  • Chat during the meeting.

  • Access the conversation through Chat after the meeting has ended. For users in the same organization as the meeting host, after the meeting has ended, you can access the conversation through Chat. When you create a DM from a Google Calendar invite, it links to the event’s invite list. This happens when you:

  • Select “Chat with Guests” from the Calendar invite.

  • Access the calendar reminder in the Chat roster.

  • Send the first message in Meet when continuous meeting chat is enabled. You can add or remove members during or after a meeting.

  • Before or during a meeting: To add or remove someone from a DM created from a Calendar event, update the Calendar invite. You can’t update the members through the DM in Chat.

  • After a meeting: You can add or remove members directly within the Chat DM. When you use the “Chat with Guests” option to create a DM from Calendar, third-party (3P) or external users aren’t included. When they join the meeting, they can find the messages sent after the time they joined. They have access to these messages only from within the meeting chat, and have no access once the meeting ends.

Tip: The host can turn off continuous meeting chat in the settings under “Chat Moderation.” Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

Add or remove someone in a direct message (Computer)

To add someone to a direct message (DM) with two or more people in Google Chat, add them to the member list or mention them in the message.

Add people to a DM

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Open a DM.

  • At the top, click the conversation name Start a new chat.

  • Enter a name or email address.

  • Click Create. Tips:

  • To quickly add a new person to a DM with 2 or more people, in the reply area, enter @ followed by the person’s name.

  • Or, next to conversation name, click the dropdown Add people.

Remove people from a DM

Important: When you remove someone from a DM, they can’t:

  • Participate in the conversation.
  • Check message history.
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a DM.
  • At the top, next to conversation name, click the dropdown View members.
  • Next to the person’s name, click More options Remove from conversation.

Manage members in a DM created from Calendar

With continuous meeting chat, you can send messages to meeting participants before, during and after a meeting in Google Chat from a computer or mobile device. Continuous meeting chat is available to all business and enterprise users. Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

You can use the dedicated conversations from your meetings to:

  • Remind or prepare attendees for the meeting.

  • Chat during the meeting.

  • Access the conversation through Chat after the meeting has ended. For users in the same organization as the meeting host, after the meeting has ended, you can access the conversation through Chat. When you create a DM from a Google Calendar invite, it links to the event’s invite list. This happens when you:

  • Select “Chat with Guests” from the Calendar invite.

  • Access the calendar reminder in the Chat roster.

  • Send the first message in Meet when continuous meeting chat is enabled. You can add or remove members during or after a meeting.

  • Before or during a meeting: To add or remove someone from a DM created from a Calendar event, update the Calendar invite. You can’t update the members through the DM in Chat.

  • After a meeting: You can add or remove members directly within the Chat DM. When you use the “Chat with Guests” option to create a DM from Calendar, third-party (3P) or external users aren’t included. When they join the meeting, they can find the messages sent after the time they joined. They have access to these messages only from within the meeting chat, and have no access once the meeting ends.

Tip: The host can turn off continuous meeting chat in the settings under “Chat Moderation.” Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

Create a guest account in Google Chat

You can join another organization’s Google Chat with a Google Workspace guest account. At no cost to you, collaboration and communication with other organizations is easy. To join, you must be invited.

Tip: If you’re part of a Workspace and want to invite a guest to your Chat, you can send an invitation.

What you can do with a guest account

Once you create an account, your invitation lets you chat directly with the person who invited you and join any approved spaces.

  • Google Chat: Use chats and spaces to coordinate and communicate.
  • Google Meet: Join huddles, Google Meet calls, or access Meet sessions that are shared through links.
  • Google Drive: Open and edit shared Google Drive files like Docs, Sheets, or Slides. Tip: Guest accounts can’t use chat in Gmail.

Create a new guest account

  • Open the invitation email.

    • For the best experience, use a computer web browser to create your account.
    • Tip: If there’s a sign-in conflict with a Chrome or Google Chat account that’s already logged in:
      • Copy the invitation link.
      • Paste it into a new incognito or private browsing window.

  • To accept the invitation, select Join the conversation.

  • To create your guest account, follow the on-screen instructions. Tips:

  • Save your guest account email ID and password for future use.

  • You can find the guest account email ID in the invitation email if you didn’t save it during setup.

Sign in to your guest account on another device

Sign in on web
  • Go to chat.google.com.
  • Sign in with your guest account email ID and password.
    • If you’re already signed into other Google Chat accounts:
      • Select your Profile picture Add another account.
      • Sign in with your guest account.

Related resources

  • Sign in & access Google Chat
  • Invite external guests in Google Chat

Improve your Chat messages with Refine

To improve the clarity and tone of your message before you send it, use Refine to edit your message in Google Chat.

Important: This feature requires an eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. Learn about Gemini features and plans.

You can use Refine in the following languages:

  • English
  • French
  • German
  • Italian
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish If your draft text isn’t in these languages, you receive an error message.

Refine your message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Enter a message in Chat.

  • To refine your message:

    • Click Formatting options .
    • Activate the Refine hint text:
      • Mac: Press Option + H.
      • Windows: Press Alt + H.
    • Highlight the text you want to refine.

  • Click Refine .

    • Above the Compose area, a refined version of your message displays.

  • To replace your original text with the refined version, click Replace. Tips:

  • To dismiss the Refine hint text and prevent it from appearing again throughout the current compose session, press Esc. The Refine hint text appears again after a page refresh.

  • To manage the Refine hint text suggestion, in the Chat settings, under “Message & Media,” turn Smart Compose on or off.

Turn Refine on or off

  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  • Under the “General” tab, in the “Google Workspace smart features” section, click Manage Workspace smart features settings.
  • Turn on Smart features in Google Workspace.
  • At the bottom, click Save.

Learn about Gemini feature suggestions

  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial, or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information. Learn how to use Google Workspace with Gemini & double-checking responses.

Invite external guests in Google Chat

With guest accounts, you can securely collaborate, coordinate, and communicate with external non-Workspace users and individuals outside your organization in Google Chat.

Tip: If you received an invitation to Chat as a non-Workspace user, learn how to create a guest account.

Learn how to invite guests

When you invite an external, non-Workspace user through a direct message (DM) or space, a guest account is provided for that external user within your Workspace domain.

A guest account is denoted by teal “External” label . This is similar to the yellow “External” label that indicates external Workspace users .

Send an invitation

To invite a guest to a direct message:

  • In Google Chat, click New chat.

  • In the search or recipient field, enter the guest’s email address.

  • To start the conversation and the invitation process, click Start chat.

    • After the invitation, the DM displays a teal “External” label .

  • Send your first message. To invite a guest to a space:

  • In Google Chat, open the space you want to invite the guest to.

  • At the top, click the space name Manage members Add.

  • Enter the guest’s email address.

  • To send the invitation, follow the prompts. Tips:

You can invite external, non-Workspace users to Google Chat as guests in a DM or space if:

  • The external user doesn’t have a Workspace or Gmail account.
  • Your admin allowlisted the invitee’s domain, if your organization uses a trusted domain to restrict external chatting.
  • Your admin allowlisted you to invite guests.
  • External members are allowed in the space.

Collaborate with external users

  • Google Meet: Guest users can join huddles, Meet calls, or access Google Meet sessions that are shared through links within a space.
  • Google Drive: Guest users can open and edit Google Drive files like Docs, Sheets, or Slides shared within the space. External users with a Drive Visitors account can still receive Guest Pass invites.

Review guest invitation failures

Error type 1: External chat failure

The external user displays a yellow “External” label . This error occurs with email addresses linked to existing Workspace accounts. These users aren’t eligible for guest invitations.

Error message

Error reason

This user doesn’t have Google Chat enabled.

Chat is disabled for this Workspace account. To allow this user to use Google Chat, the invitee’s administrator must enable Chat for the user.

You’ve blocked this user. Unblock them to send a message.

The invitee is blocked by the inviter.

This user’s account is still being set up. Please try again later.

New account restriction. There may be a short wait time before Chat activates.

Can’t start a direct message right now. Try again later.

A transient error occurred. Retry later.

This conversation can’t be created due to conflicting history retention or data location policies.

History retention or data location policies conflict between the inviter and the invitee accounts. To permit messaging, one or both administrators must resolve these conflicts.

  • You can’t send a message to them because their organization doesn’t allow it.

  • You can’t message the user(s) because of a policy set by their administrator. Your domain isn’t in the invitee organization’s allowlisted domains. Contact the invitee’s administrator for help.

  • Your organization doesn’t let you send direct message to this person.

  • You can’t message the user(s) because of a policy set by your administrator. The invitee’s domain is not in your organization’s allowlist.

Error type 2: Guest invitation failure

Error message

Error reason

  • Your organization doesn’t let you send a direct message to this person.
  • You can’t message the user(s) because of a policy set by your administrator. The invitee’s domain is not in your organization’s allowlist.

Can’t invite user. Org limit to add non-Workspace users met. Contact admin.

Your organization has exceeded the limit for the number of guests.

Can’t invite user. This type of external invite isn’t enabled by your administrator.

You aren’t allowed to invite guests. An administrator must enable guest invitation privilege for you.

Mark a conversation or thread as read or unread

In Google Chat, you can mark conversations as unread to return to them later. You can also mark a conversation as read without opening it.

When you mark a conversation as unread, a dot shows up next to it in your conversation list.

Change a conversation to read or unread

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • In the navigation panel or “Home,” next to the conversation or thread, click More options .

  • Click Mark as read or Mark as unread . Tips: Other ways to mark a conversation as read or unread include:

  • At the top of a DM or space, click the conversation name Mark as read or Mark as unread.

  • For individual messages in a conversation, point to the message click More actions Mark as unread. This adds an “Unread” line above the message in the conversation.

Locate your unread conversations

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, click Home.
  • At the top right, click Unread.

Send a direct message

You can send a direct message (DM) to a person or group in Google Chat.

Learn how DMs work

  • DMs can be from you to another person or include multiple people.
  • When one or more people read your message, their avatar displays next to their last read message.
  • To focus conversation around a topic, project, or shared interest with multiple people, create a space instead. Learn the differences between spaces and DMs.

Find your DMs

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, click Direct messages. Tip: To search for DMs, use the search bar at the top. Learn how to search for messages.

Send a DM

Important: If this is your first time sending a message to someone else, they need to accept your message request before you can chat with them.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Click New chat.

  • Enter a name or an email address.

  • Click Start chat.

    • When you enter a name or email address, you can get suggestions.
    • To start a group DM, add more names or email addresses.

  • In the reply area, enter a message.

  • Click Send . Tip: To start a new DM easily, next to a person’s name:

  • Click Start chat .

  • Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Enter / ⌘ + Enter. Message options

In the reply area, you can add more content to your message before you send it. You can:

  • Format your message .

  • Add an emoji .

  • Insert a GIF .

  • Upload a file or photo from your computer .

  • Insert a Google Meet link . For more options, click Google Workspace tools to:

  • Attach Drive files .

  • Schedule a meeting in Google Calendar .

  • Add Chat apps.

Turn a DM into a space

Important: If there are 2 or more people in the DM, you can turn a DM into a space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a DM.
  • At the top, click the conversation name.
  • Click Turn this chat into a space.

Start a new Meeting Conversation

Important: All Business and Enterprise users have access to continuous meeting chat.

You can create a continuous meeting chat when you:

  • Select “Chat with Guests” from a Calendar invite.

  • Access the group chat within your Chat list of conversations.

  • Send the first message with the embedded chat in Meet.

    • These messages sync to the Google Chat group direct message (GDM).

  • Click the calendar nudge in the Chat roster. Tips:

  • To find Meeting Conversations in your Chat conversations list, check under the “Direct messages” section.

  • To help you organize your chats, you can move your meeting conversations from direct messages to a dedicated “Meeting” section in Chat. Learn how to manage meeting conversations in Google Chat. Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

For every instance of recurring events in Calendar, it generates a separate Meeting Conversation.

The Meeting Conversation name combines the event name and date. For example:

  • “Sales Team Weekly - Nov 8”
  • “Sales Team Weekly - Nov 15” The date in the title uses the format and language of your current language settings in your account. Learn how to change your language on the web.

When you use a group chat from a Calendar invite:

  • The group chat automatically includes all guests within your workspace, regardless of their RSVP status.
  • The chat and event titles match.
Manage updates
  • If you add or remove guests or update the event title before the event, your changes are automatically reflected in the group chat.
  • If you reschedule a calendar event or change the roster, the group chat stays linked to the original calendar event.
  • Users within the workspace can access and send messages in the group after the meeting ends. Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

Tips:

  • When you invite external guests to a meeting through the “Chat with Guests” feature in Calendar, they aren’t automatically added to the Meeting Conversation.
  • If no one sends a message before or during the meeting, Calendar won’t create or display a new Meeting Conversation in your Chat conversations list.
  • The same retention policies apply to both Meeting Conversations and Google Chat spaces. Learn about message history for conversations with work or school accounts.
  • If you reuse an existing meeting code to create a meeting, users who aren’t part of the original meeting-code invite can’t participate in the previous meeting chat in Chat. Learn more about meeting codes in Calendar events.

Learn how DMs work in Google Workspace

If your work or school uses Google Chat, your administrator allows you to send messages to people in and out of your organization. When you add someone outside of your organization to a group direct message, they get an invite to join the chat.

  • You can send a direct message or create a group direct message with people outside of your organization if:
    • They use their personal Google Account.
    • Both organizations allow it.
  • An “External” badge displays next to:
    • The person’s name in direct messages with someone outside of your organization.
    • The group name in group direct messages with people outside of your organization.
  • You can’t add external participants to existing internal group direct messages. Instead, you must create a new group direct message.
  • Internal group direct messages can’t be converted into external group direct messages.
  • External group direct messages that have all external members removed will continue to be external.
  • When you add people to a direct message, you can find suggestions. Suggestions include everyone in your organization, even if they don’t have Google Chat.
  • For administrators: External group direct messages are controlled by the same admin settings that control external spaces (External Chatting & External Spaces).
