Send a direct message (Computer)

You can send a direct message (DM) to a person or group in Google Chat.

Learn how DMs work

  • DMs can be from you to another person or include multiple people.
  • When one or more people read your message, their avatar displays next to their last read message.
  • To focus conversation around a topic, project, or shared interest with multiple people, create a space instead. Learn the differences between spaces and DMs.

Find your DMs

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, click Direct messages. Tip: To search for DMs, use the search bar at the top. Learn how to search for messages.

Send a DM

Important: If this is your first time sending a message to someone else, they need to accept your message request before you can chat with them.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Click New chat.

  • Enter a name or an email address.

  • Click Start chat.

    • When you enter a name or email address, you can get suggestions.
    • To start a group DM, add more names or email addresses.

  • In the reply area, enter a message.

  • Click Send . Tip: To start a new DM easily, next to a person’s name:

  • Click Start chat .

  • Use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Enter / ⌘ + Enter. Message options

In the reply area, you can add more content to your message before you send it. You can:

  • Format your message .

  • Add an emoji .

  • Insert a GIF .

  • Upload a file or photo from your computer .

  • Insert a Google Meet link . For more options, click Google Workspace tools to:

  • Attach Drive files .

  • Schedule a meeting in Google Calendar .

  • Add Chat apps.

Turn a DM into a space

Important: If there are 2 or more people in the DM, you can turn a DM into a space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a DM.
  • At the top, click the conversation name.
  • Click Turn this chat into a space.

Start a new Meeting Conversation

Important: All Business and Enterprise users have access to continuous meeting chat.

You can create a continuous meeting chat when you:

  • Select “Chat with Guests” from a Calendar invite.

  • Access the group chat within your Chat list of conversations.

  • Send the first message with the embedded chat in Meet.

    • These messages sync to the Google Chat group direct message (GDM).

  • Click the calendar nudge in the Chat roster. Tips:

  • To find Meeting Conversations in your Chat conversations list, check under the “Direct messages” section.

  • To help you organize your chats, you can move your meeting conversations from direct messages to a dedicated “Meeting” section in Chat. Learn how to manage meeting conversations in Google Chat. Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

For every instance of recurring events in Calendar, it generates a separate Meeting Conversation.

The Meeting Conversation name combines the event name and date. For example:

  • “Sales Team Weekly - Nov 8”
  • “Sales Team Weekly - Nov 15” The date in the title uses the format and language of your current language settings in your account. Learn how to change your language on the web.

When you use a group chat from a Calendar invite:

  • The group chat automatically includes all guests within your workspace, regardless of their RSVP status.
  • The chat and event titles match.
Manage updates
  • If you add or remove guests or update the event title before the event, your changes are automatically reflected in the group chat.
  • If you reschedule a calendar event or change the roster, the group chat stays linked to the original calendar event.
  • Users within the workspace can access and send messages in the group after the meeting ends. Learn how to use Chat with Google Meet.

Tips:

  • When you invite external guests to a meeting through the “Chat with Guests” feature in Calendar, they aren’t automatically added to the Meeting Conversation.
  • If no one sends a message before or during the meeting, Calendar won’t create or display a new Meeting Conversation in your Chat conversations list.
  • The same retention policies apply to both Meeting Conversations and Google Chat spaces. Learn about message history for conversations with work or school accounts.
  • If you reuse an existing meeting code to create a meeting, users who aren’t part of the original meeting-code invite can’t participate in the previous meeting chat in Chat. Learn more about meeting codes in Calendar events.

Send a voice message in Google Chat

You can send a voice message to a person or group in Google Chat and transcribe these voice messages into text.

Send a voice message

Important:

  • If this is the first time you send a message to a particular person, they must accept your message request before you can chat with them.
  • This feature isn’t available on Chrome OS.
  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Click New chat.
  • Enter a name or an email address.
  • Click Start chat.
    • When you enter a name or email address, you can get suggestions.
    • To start a group DM, add more names or email addresses.
  • In the reply area, click the mic .
  • In the popup, to record and stop the recording, select the red circle . Tip: After recording, you can find options to either restart or send the voice message.

View or hide voice message transcription

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Click a conversation, direct message, or space.
  • To view the voice message transcript:
    • Sender: Click below the voice message Show more.
    • Receiver: Click below the voice message View transcript.
  • To hide the transcript, click Hide transcript.

Share in Chat from Gmail

Users with a work or school account can quickly share an email in a Chat message to keep the email context and avoid long email threads.

Important:

  • Users with a personal account don’t have access to this feature.
  • To share an email in Chat, you must turn on Chat in Gmail.

Share an email in Chat

  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • Open an email.
  • At the bottom of the email, select Share in chat .
    • Tip: To share a specific email in a multiple-email thread, next to the email, click More Share in chat .
  • To add recipients, you can:
    • Click Add everyone from the email.
    • Search or select from listed suggestions.
  • Optional: To remove a recipient, next to the name or space, click Remove .
  • Click Next.
  • Enter your message.
  • Click Send .
    • The recipient gets a link to the email in Chat.
    • Gmail adds an automated reply to the email thread that links to the Chat message.

Learn why you’re unable to share an email in Chat

You can’t share an email in Chat if:

  • You use a personal account.
  • The admin for your work account turned off Chat.
  • You haven’t turned on Chat within Gmail on your computer.
  • The email is spam, phishing, scheduled, in trash, in drafts, or in confidential mode.
  • You open the email in another email app, like Apple Mail or Microsoft Outlook.
  • The email is encrypted with Client-side encryption. Learn about Gmail Client-side encryption.
  • You try to share an email in Chat to more than 50 recipients or to a Google Group.

  • Edit or delete a message in Google Chat
  • Search for Google Chat messages

Turn history on or off in Google Chat

When you message a person or group in Google Chat, you can choose to save your conversation or have it automatically deleted after 24 hours.

When anyone in the chat turns history on or off:

  • A note appears in the message stream that says history was turned on or off.
  • A prompt appears in the compose box that says “History is on” or “History is off.”

Learn who can control conversation history

  • If you use Google Chat with a work or school account: Your organization determines if you can use the history setting to save your chats.
  • If you use Google Chat with a personal account: You can choose whether to turn history on or off.

Manage conversation history

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Open a conversation.
  • At the top, click the conversation name Turn on history or Turn off history.

About history in spaces

When history is on
  • History is always on in spaces grouped by topic.
  • History is on by default in spaces with in-line threading. If you have a workspace account, your administrator may change the default history setting.
  • When history is on, people added to a space can view past messages from before they joined the space.
When history is off
  • When history is off in spaces with in-line threading, messages remain in your email if you forward them to your Gmail inbox.
  • When history is off in a space, shared files won’t appear in that space’s “Files” section. For people to view shared files, turn on space history and then share files. Learn how to manage your files in spaces.
  • Even with history off, Google Chat may scan messages for spam, phishing, and malware.
  • Even with history off, if you use Google Chat with a work or school account, your organization may scan messages for sensitive data.

Why can’t I chat with someone?

When you try to send someone a message in Google Chat, you might get a banner that says you can’t message them. This problem happens if you have incompatible settings.

Reasons you can’t chat with someone

  • Settings that block you in Google Chat or another product. Learn more about blocked accounts.
  • Settings that don’t allow the other person to chat outside their organization.
    • If they use a Google Workspace account and their administrator disabled chats with external people, you can’t send each other messages. Learn how to turn Chat history on or off.
  • History settings aren’t compatible.
    • Important: If you have a work or school account, your administrator may set your history settings and may not allow users to change their history settings.
    • You might be able to fix this problem if you update your history settings to be compatible with the other person’s. For example, if your chat history is on, and you send a message to someone who doesn’t have their history on, you may be able to chat by updating those settings to match. Learn how to turn Chat history on or off.
      • Tip: If both of you can turn off history, it automatically turns off when you chat with someone in a different data region.
  • Your Workspace administrator may have configured policies that limit certain capabilities. For example, you can send messages in existing conversations but can’t start new ones.
    • Contact your Workspace administrator if this happens.

Use apps

Access Workspace Studio from Gmail & Chat

You can use Workspace Studio inside Google Chat and Gmail to automate everyday tasks without leaving your conversation or inbox.

Access Workspace Studio

  • Open the side panel: The Workspace Studio side panel helps you discover and manage your flows without leaving your conversation or your inbox. On the top right of Gmail or Google Chat, click the Workspace Studio icon to open it.
  • Discover: Browse recommended flows for your current app. The simplest way to create your first flow is to pick a pre-built template from the Discover tab.
  • My Flows: You can use this tab to quickly check which flows are active or turn them off. If a flow has an error, a red badge appears to notify you of the issue. Click Show me to investigate.
  • Tip: If a flow requires your approval to proceed, a red badge displays on the Workspace Studio icon. To evaluate and approve or reject the request, click Review.
  • Activity: Check ”Activity” to confirm your flows ran successfully. You can also investigate any errors here.
  • Do more in Studio: To build more powerful flows from scratch or manage advanced settings, click Do more in Studio to open the full editor at studio.workspace.google.com.

Use skills in Ask Gemini

Important: Before you can use a skill in Gmail or Google Chat, you must create the skill and turn it on in Workspace Studio.

Use skills in Gmail

To analyze emails or draft responses with custom instructions, use skills in Ask Gemini in Gmail.

  • On your computer, open Gmail.
  • At the top right, click Ask Gemini .
  • In the Ask Gemini side panel, type: @.
  • Select the desired skill from the autocomplete list.
  • Enter your prompt.
  • Click Submit .
Use skills in Google Chat

To analyze chat conversations, use skills in Ask Gemini in Google Chat.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • On the left, under “Shortcuts,” click Ask Gemini .
  • In the message field, type @ followed by the skill name. For example, “@Project Summary.”
  • Enter your prompt.
  • Click Send .

Learn about Google Chat app permissions

Google Chat apps can perform actions that are similar to user actions in Google Chat. You can find more information about the permissions that a specific app can request in the app’s listing in the Google Workspace Marketplace.

Tip: If you have a work or school account and you want to know what permissions an app is granted, contact your admin.

Understand permissions for apps added to spaces

Apps added to spaces can:

  • Post messages
  • Manage space members membership
  • Update space metadata
  • Read:
    • Messages that invoke the app
    • Membership information
    • Space metadata, such as a space name, description, and on or off history

Understand permissions for app-created spaces

  • App-created spaces may not have human space managers.
  • The app can perform management actions typically limited to space managers in app-created spaces, like:
    • Manage space managers membership
    • Update space permissions
  • For work or school accounts, you can:
    • Remove the app, if the space permission settings allow.
    • Leave the space.
    • Contact your admin.
      • If needed, admins can revoke app permissions and appoint a human space manager.

Understand advanced app permissions

  • Learn about how to set up app authorization for Chat.
  • You can find permissions the app can request in the app’s listing in the Google Workspace Marketplace.

Learn the differences between app permissions & space permissions

Generally, space permissions don’t apply to apps. Instead, they’re based on the app’s membership in your space. They may also require your admin’s consent. Even if permissions only allow space managers to perform an action, an application may still have permission to perform that action if it’s a member of the space and has the appropriate consent. Learn more about space permissions here.

Actions that only require the app to be a space member include:

  • Use @all.

  • Post in announcement spaces.

  • Reply in announcement spaces. Actions that require admin consent include:

  • Change space details.

  • Turn history on or off.

  • Manage members and groups. Actions normally limited to space managers can generally be performed by applications in spaces the app created with admin consent. With permission, an app can:

  • Manage space managers, which includes promotions, demotions, and deleting membership.

  • Manage space permissions.

  • Delete the space.

  • Use apps in Google Chat
  • Chat apps built by Google

Meet app for Google Chat Turndown

The Meet app for Google Chat shut down in summer 2024. To modify or reschedule meetings or to look up your schedule, go to Calendar on calendar.google.com or use the Google Calendar Android or iOS app.

Use apps in Google Chat

Apps are special accounts you can message that connect you to services in Chat, so you can:

  • Look up information.
  • Schedule a meeting.
  • Do tasks.

Learn how apps work in Google Chat

When you interact with an app in Chat, the app can see your:

  • Email address
  • Avatar
  • Basic information (such as your name) The app can see others’ basic information in a chat, but it can’t see their email address or avatar unless they interact directly with the app.

Google creates and maintains some apps, such as the Google Drive and Poll apps.

Third-party software vendors create and maintain other apps. If you use one, review the vendor’s Terms of Service and privacy policy for more information on the third-party use of your data.

Important:

  • On your work or school accounts, your admin can install apps for you. Afterwards, the apps can send you direct messages. You can’t uninstall the apps but you can turn off notifications for conversations with the app.

  • If you’re an external member of a Google Chat space created by a work or school account, you can’t add, remove, or interact with any apps. Tips:

  • Learn how to create custom apps for your organization.

  • For your organization’s guidelines on app creation, contact your Google Workspace administrator.

Learn about unverified & personal apps in Google Chat spaces

Developers with personal Gmail accounts can create and add personal apps to Google Chat spaces, group direct messages (DMs), and DMs they join. Any member of the space can then interact with these apps.

Important: Developers must explicitly provide consent in their app’s configuration to enable apps to join spaces and group conversations. This allows their email to be visible to other members.

Google Chat displays an “Unverified app” warning badge next to messages sent by these apps to ensure transparency. When you hover over or click this badge, it reveals the creator’s email address. For example, “Unverified—built by [developer_email].” This badge appears on all app interaction surfaces, such as messages, link previews, slash/quick commands, message actions, and system messages.

If a personal app’s creator leaves or is removed from a space, the app is automatically removed from that conversation to help prevent spam and abuse. Learn more about how to block an app creator.

Find & install a Chat app

Important: If you have a work or school account, your organization controls which apps are available to you.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Select an option:
    • Click New chat Find apps.
    • In the Chat sidebar, click Get Add-ons .
  • Search or browse for an app.
  • Select an app.
  • To create a dedicated 1:1 direct message with the app and allow you to interact with the app’s features individually, click Install.
    • Or, to add an app to a space and allow all space members to use the app’s features, click Add to Space. Tips:
  • You can find and install an app in the Marketplace.
  • To perform tasks on your behalf, the app sends you a prompt to get your permission to access your Google Account. To grant permission, go to the prompt and click Allow. Learn how to remove third-party app access to your account.
  • To uninstall an app in a direct message, at the top, click the app name Uninstall. For work or school accounts, you can’t uninstall apps that your admin installed.

Add apps to a conversation or space

Your installed apps can be used in your conversations and spaces. When you add an app to a space, you grant the app the ability to:

  • Fetch basic information about the space.

  • Create messages in the space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

  • Select a conversation or space.

  • At the top, click the space name or conversation participants.

  • Click Apps & integration Add apps.

  • Enter the app name.

  • Select one or more apps.

  • Click Add. Tips:

  • When you add an app to a space, it grants the app access to messages that triggered the app, not to read all the messages in the space.

    • Apps that require access to the full message context can only do so with explicit permission.

  • When you add an app to a space, the app gets installed in your Apps section.

    • Now the app is available in every other space you’re in and may be available in other Workspace products.

  • Do not manually add the app to the conversation. To use the app in a different conversation or space, add the app in the space with:

    • An @mention or /mention
    • A command
    • A relevant link preview

  • When you add an app to space, it grants the app access to manage cards that it owns in the space, including cards attached to human user messages.

Remove apps from a conversation or space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

  • Select a conversation or space.

  • At the top, click the space name or conversation participants.

  • Click Apps & integrations.

  • To remove an app, click More options Remove from space. Tips:

  • When you remove an app from a conversation or space, it’s only removed from that conversation or space, not from your Apps section.

  • You can uninstall the app from the Apps section. This also uninstalls the app from other Workspace products.

Uninstall an app

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • On the left sidebar, under “Apps,” open an app.
  • At the top, click the app’s name Uninstall.

Use app commands

Use app commands in Google Chat to communicate quickly with apps. You don’t have to remember the commands. Instead, you can enter a forward slash / or click Add .

The app commands you use in a conversation are private. The app’s responses appear in the conversation.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Select a conversation or space.
  • In the reply area, enter a forward slash /.
    • Or, at the left of the reply area, click Add .
  • Start typing and select the option from the list that matches what you’re trying to do.
    • If the command requires more information, type your input in the reply area and press Enter to activate.
    • If the command does not require more information, click the command to activate it. Tips:
  • If the app isn’t already in the conversation or space, the app is added when you message it.
  • To perform a custom behavior, add an argument. An argument is an additional input that you provide to a command.

Get help with apps

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Open the conversation with the app.
  • At the top, click About.

Use the Asana app in Google Chat

Use the Asana app in Chat to get notifications about updates to Asana tasks.

Before you begin

  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • You need an Asana account.

Set up the Asana app in Chat

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • To sign in to your Asana account, tap Sign Into Asana.
    • The configuration window opens.
  • Under Choose Workspace, to use the workspace, tap the Down arrow .
    • Select the Asana workspace.
  • Under Choose Project, to get notifications, tap the Down arrow .
    • Select the Asana project.
  • Under Thread messages by menu, choose an option:
    • No threads
    • Threaded by project
    • Threaded by task
  • To get the notifications of the items in Chat, check the boxes next to the items.
  • Click Save.
  • Optional: To add another project, click Add. Tip: You need to set up notifications in each space where you add the app. The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member.

Change app settings

In spaces, only the person who added the app can change the settings.

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Enter settings.
    • In spaces, enter @Asana settings or /Asana settings.
    • The current settings for the app opens.
  • Click Edit Settings.
    • The settings page opens.
  • Click Edit .
  • Change the settings as needed.
  • Click Save. Once the app is removed from a space, the app settings get deleted.

    • The current settings for the app opens.
  • Tap Edit Settings.
    • The settings page opens.
  • Tap Edit .
  • Change the settings as needed.
  • Tap Save. Once the app is removed from a space, the app settings get deleted.

Use the Bitbucket app in Google Chat

Use the Bitbucket app in Chat to:

  • Receive messages when events occur in Bitbucket.
  • Perform quick actions, such as to view and approve pull requests.
  • View and reply to comments on your pull requests.

Learn what you need before you begin

  • Permission from your Google Workspace administrator to install apps.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • Use your Bitbucket administrator privileges to install the Bitbucket for Google Chat plugin in the Bitbucket workspace from the Bitbucket Marketplace.
    • Once an administrator installs the app, all users with access to the workspace can add the Bitbucket for Google Chat and work with that workspace.

Set up the Bitbucket app in Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • Select an option:
    • Open a direct message with the app.
    • Go to a space with the app.
  • Click Connect.
    • The configuration window opens.
  • Enter the Bitbucket workspace URL.
    • Example URL: bitbucket.org
  • Click Next Step.
    • If the required plugin is already installed, go to step 6.
    • Otherwise, follow the instructions on the page to install the plugin, then click Run App.
  • Click Connect Configure Access.
  • To provide the app access to your Google and Bitbucket accounts, follow the steps during setup.
    • If successful, you should receive a message that the app is now connected to your chosen Bitbucket account.

Manage repository notifications

Change workspace
  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • Select an option:
    • Open a direct message with the app.
    • Go to a space with the app.
  • Click Settings.
    • Alternatively, enter /bitbucket_settings.
  • At the top right, click Change.
  • Select a workspace.
  • Click Change workspace.
Add notification for a repository

Add the repositories that you want to receive notifications for.

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • Select an option:
    • Open a direct message with the app.
    • Go to a space with the app.
  • Click Settings.
    • Alternatively, enter /bitbucket_settings.
  • At the bottom right, click Add repository.
  • Choose a repository from the list.
  • Click Select.
  • Select an option:
    • Check the boxes that you want to receive notifications for.
    • Check Select all.

Change app settings

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • Select an option:
    • Open a direct message with the app.
    • Go to a space with the app.
  • Enter /bitbucket_settings.
  • Update your settings.
  • Click Save.

Uninstall the Bitbucket app

Important: If you uninstall the app from a space, the Bitbucket workspace is removed from the space and all the notifications you set up are lost. However, your login information remains.

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat or your Gmail account.
  • Select an option:
    • Open a direct message with the app.
    • Go to a space with the app.
  • At the top, click the Down arrow .
  • Select an option:
    • For Chat: Click Uninstall.
    • For Spaces: Click Apps & integrations More Remove from space.

Use the Bulk Member Manager app in Google Chat

To add or remove multiple members in bulk to a space, use the Bulk Member Manager app for Google Chat. With the app, you can:

  • Copy and paste email addresses.
  • Add a comma-separated values (.csv) file (computer only).

Before you begin

  • To use the Bulk Member Manager app, you must be a space owner, manager, or member who has permission to manage members.
  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.

Set up the Bulk Member Manager app in Chat

  • On your computer, open Chat.

  • Search for the space.

  • Next to the reply area, click Action .

  • In the search bar, enter “Bulk Member Manager.”

  • Click the app Add to space.

  • To update memberships, you can use either: Email addresses

  • In the reply area, enter a slash command.

    • To add members, enter /addDialog.
    • To remove members, enter /removeDialog.

  • On your keyboard, press Enter.

  • In the window, copy and paste the list of email addresses.

    • Use commas to separate email addresses in the list.

  • Click Send request. A .csv file

  • In the reply area, enter a slash command.

    • To add members, enter /addCsv.
    • To remove members, enter /removeCSV.

  • To add the .csv file, click Upload file .

  • On your keyboard, press Enter. Add app to space

Tip: You can also add the app from the:

  • “Apps & integrations” page in Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them in Chat.
  • Side panel in Gmail and Chat. Learn how to use Google products side by side.

Use the Feeds app in Google Chat

To get messages about updates from news, blog posts, or other content through the Atom or RSS data format, use the Feeds app in Chat. The integration sends new posts from the feed to Chat.

Add Feeds to a direct message or space

  • On your computer, open Chat.

  • To find the Feeds app, enter: /Feeds.

    • Or, on the left side of the compose bar, click Add .
    • Enter: /Feeds.

  • Select Manage your subscriptions.

    • The Feeds module pops up.

  • In the text box, under “Add a subscription,” enter the subscription URL.

  • Click the Add Subscription button. Tips:

  • You need to set up subscriptions in each space where you add the app.

  • The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member and it’s configured.

Edit or delete Feeds subscriptions

  • On your computer, open Chat.
  • Open a direct message or go to a space where you have a feed set up.
  • Edit or delete a subscription.
    • To edit:
      • Open the Manage Subscriptions Module.
      • Next to the subscription you want to edit, click Edit Save Subscription.
  • Or, you can:
    • Enter: /Feeds.
    • Select Manage your subscriptions.
    • In one of the feed outputs, click More Manage Subscription.
    • To delete: Next to the subscription you want to delete, tap Delete . Tips:
  • If you remove the app from a space, it deletes all the space’s subscriptions.
  • Only the person who created the subscription can edit or delete the Feeds. The space manager can delete it, but not update.

Use the Giphy app in Google Chat

Use the Giphy app in Chat to add GIFs to your chats.

Tip: You can also send GIFs from your computer. To send a GIF, click Add GIF .

Before you begin

  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.

Use the Giphy app in Chat

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Enter a search query, using any keyword, such as “cats” or “funny:”
    • query—Adds the first GIF that matches the query with the set rating.
      • In spaces, enter @Giphy query or /Giphy query.
      • To remove the GIF, click the GIF Try again or Delete.
    • choose query—Adds a group of 25 GIFs that match the query with the set rating.
      • In spaces, enter @Giphy choose query or /Giphy choose query.
      • To move through the GIFs, click Next or Back.

Change the content rating of GIFs

The app shows GIFs that are rated G unless you change the default setting. You can find the current rating and change it.

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Enter rating.
    • In spaces, enter @Giphy rating or /Giphy rating.
    • The app displays the current content rating.
  • Enter rating [Y,G,PG,PG-13,R].
    • In spaces, enter @Giphy rating [Y,G,PG,PG-13,R] or /Giphy rating [Y,G,PG,PG-13,R].
    • For example, to set the content rating of GIFs to G, enter rating G.

Use the GitHub app in Google Chat

Use the GitHub app in Chat to get notifications about GitHub events, such as issues, pull requests, and comments. All notifications, links, and text checklists render with rich, clean GitHub-enhanced markdown (including tables, code blocks, checklists, and blockquotes) for improved readability.

Before you begin

To use the GitHub app for Chat:

  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • You need a GitHub account.
  • You need to install the Google Chat app for your GitHub repository. Understand GitHub app & OAuth app authentication mechanisms

This outlines the distinct characteristics and operational models of GitHub apps and OAuth apps, which serve as primary mechanisms for third-party services to integrate with and access GitHub resources. A comprehensive understanding of these differences is critical to maintain an optimal security posture within an organization.

1. Comparative analysis: Key distinctions

The fundamental differences between the 2 models reside in the identity used for access (the Principal) and the mechanism that governs resource authorization.

Attribute

GitHub app (Recommended sign in)

OAuth app (Legacy sign in)

Principal identity

Acts as an independent Application Identity, separate from any user, or on behalf of the authorizing user, depending on the use case.

Acts on behalf of the authorizing user, inheriting their privileges.

Authorization model

Fine-grained permissions (Recommended): Utilizes the Principle of Least Privilege, allowing access to specific repositories and resource types. For example: Read access for metadata only.

Broad scopes: Access is defined by wide scopes like granting access to all resources visible to the authorizing user.

Credential longevity

Short-lived tokens: Access tokens possess a limited lifespan (typically 1 hour) and require frequent renewal, significantly mitigating risk in the event of compromise.

Long-lived tokens: Access tokens persist until manually revoked by the user, representing a prolonged exposure risk.

Installation requirement

Must be installed by an Administrator or Organization owner, establishing a formal link to the account or organization and authorized by the user for use cases where the app is acting on behalf of the user.

Must be authorized by an individual user, linking access directly to that user’s identity.

For more comprehensive documentation, refer to Differences between GitHub Apps and OAuth apps.

2. Recommendation

Based on security best practices, the GitHub App authentication mechanism is recommended for all third-party and organizational integrations. This model enforces the Principle of Least Privilege and employs robust, time-limited credentials, thereby maintaining a higher standard of security and operational stability compared to the delegated authority model of OAuth Apps.

Install the Google Chat App for GitHub repositories.

Set up the GitHub app in Chat

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • To open the configuration window, click Sign in.
  • Click Configure Access Sign in to GitHub.
  • Complete the sign-in process then close the popup.
  • To update the Chat dialog, click Refresh.
  • Under Add Repositories, type the GitHub repository you want notifications for.
  • Check the boxes for the events you want notifications for.
  • Click Save. Tip: You need to set up notifications in each space where you add the app. The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member.

Migrate from OAuth app (Legacy) to GitHub app (Recommended)

To migrate your current connection from the older OAuth app authentication method to the recommended GitHub app method:

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message or space with the GitHub app.
  • In the message field, click Google Workspace tools .
  • In the command list, select GitHub Reauthorize.
  • To complete the migration and reauthorization process, follow the on-screen instructions in the Chat dialogue.

Use the GitHub app in spaces

To use the app in spaces, you need to @mention or /mention the app in each message and in replies to the messages from the app.

The @mention or /mention confirms you’ve sent the message to the app and not to others in the space.

  • Open the Chat app .
  • In a space, enter @github or /github followed by the command.
    • When you mention @github or /github, the message is sent to the app and not to others in the space.

Change app settings

In spaces, only the person who added the app can change the settings.

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • To open the current settings for the app, enter: /github_settings.
  • Change the settings as needed.
  • Click Save. Removing the app from a space deletes the app settings.

Learn about commands for the GitHub app in Chat

In the message field of a direct message or space with the GitHub app in Chat, you can use:

  • Slash commands:
    • /github_settings: Opens the settings dialogue.
    • /github_reminders: For personal or team open pull requests, set up and edit scheduled reminders.
    • /github_subscribe: Subscribes to a GitHub <repoURL> or <owner/repo>. To receive notifications only when specific users are mentioned, you can configure username filters within your subscription settings after subscribing.
    • /github_openIssue: Opens a new GitHub issue.
    • /github_logout: Logs out of your GitHub account.
    • /github_help: Displays the help message.
    • /github_feedback: Send feedback about the GitHub app.
  • Quick commands: To access the quick commands, click Google Workspace tools .
    • GitHub Connect: Displays a message with a “Sign in” and “Legacy Sign in” option.
    • GitHub Reauthorize: Allows you to migrate to a new connection method. To get a full list of supported commands:
  • On your computer, open Chat.
  • Open a direct message or go to a space where the GitHub app is installed.
  • Enter: /github_help.

Troubleshoot issues with GitHub app in Chat

If you get an error when you subscribe to real-time notifications

GitHub app

To set up real-time notifications in spaces:

  • In your browser, go to GitHub profile settings.
  • Under “Integrations,” click Applications Authorized GitHub apps.
    • After you connect the GitHub app in Google Chat, your list of authorized apps shows “Google Chat.”
  • Install the Google Chat App for GitHub repository.
    • Or, you can request installation from the organization/repository owner.
  • Wait until installation is complete.
  • In Google Chat, open a direct message or space with the GitHub app.
  • In the message field, to create a subscription, enter: /github_subscribe [organisation/repo] or /github_settings.
OAuth app

To set up real-time notifications in spaces, you must:

  • Be an organization owner of the proposed repository.
  • Authorize the app on the GitHub organization.
    • In your browser, go to GitHub profile settings.
    • Under “Integrations,” click Applications Authorized OAuth apps.
      • After you connect the GitHub app in Google Chat, your list of authorized apps shows “Google Chat.”
    • Grant the app access to the organization you want to access. If you receive too many notifications from the GitHub app

You can filter repository notifications so you only receive alerts when you or specific team members are directly mentioned.

  • In the message field, enter: /github_settings.
  • Click Notification settings.
  • In the repository settings dialogue, locate the “Filter by mentioned user” field.
  • Enter the GitHub usernames you want to track, separated by commas.
    • Important: Do not include the @ symbol before the usernames. For example, enter user1,user2 instead of @user1,@user2).
  • Click Save. If you don’t get @mentioned in scheduled reminders

To get mentioned in scheduled reminders, you must’ve connected your Google Chat account to the GitHub account.

  • In the message field, enter: /github_settings.
  • To connect your account:
    • In the pop-up, click Configure access Sign in to GitHub.
    • Sign in to your GitHub account.
    • Authorize the app.
  • In the message you receive from the GitHub app, select Schedule reminders for your team.
  • In the pop-up:
    • Click Create new reminder.
    • Configure the reminder settings.
    • Click Save. If you don’t get reminders with GitHub app

On the repository from where you want to receive reminders, verify the installation of the Google Chat App for GitHub.

Use the GitHub app in Google Chat (Computer)

Use the GitHub app in Chat to get notifications about GitHub events, such as issues, pull requests, and comments. All notifications, links, and text checklists render with rich, clean GitHub-enhanced markdown (including tables, code blocks, checklists, and blockquotes) for improved readability.

Before you begin

To use the GitHub app for Chat:

  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • You need a GitHub account.
  • You need to install the Google Chat app for your GitHub repository. Understand GitHub app & OAuth app authentication mechanisms

This outlines the distinct characteristics and operational models of GitHub apps and OAuth apps, which serve as primary mechanisms for third-party services to integrate with and access GitHub resources. A comprehensive understanding of these differences is critical to maintain an optimal security posture within an organization.

1. Comparative analysis: Key distinctions

The fundamental differences between the 2 models reside in the identity used for access (the Principal) and the mechanism that governs resource authorization.

Attribute

GitHub app (Recommended sign in)

OAuth app (Legacy sign in)

Principal identity

Acts as an independent Application Identity, separate from any user, or on behalf of the authorizing user, depending on the use case.

Acts on behalf of the authorizing user, inheriting their privileges.

Authorization model

Fine-grained permissions (Recommended): Utilizes the Principle of Least Privilege, allowing access to specific repositories and resource types. For example: Read access for metadata only.

Broad scopes: Access is defined by wide scopes like granting access to all resources visible to the authorizing user.

Credential longevity

Short-lived tokens: Access tokens possess a limited lifespan (typically 1 hour) and require frequent renewal, significantly mitigating risk in the event of compromise.

Long-lived tokens: Access tokens persist until manually revoked by the user, representing a prolonged exposure risk.

Installation requirement

Must be installed by an Administrator or Organization owner, establishing a formal link to the account or organization and authorized by the user for use cases where the app is acting on behalf of the user.

Must be authorized by an individual user, linking access directly to that user’s identity.

For more comprehensive documentation, refer to Differences between GitHub Apps and OAuth apps.

2. Recommendation

Based on security best practices, the GitHub App authentication mechanism is recommended for all third-party and organizational integrations. This model enforces the Principle of Least Privilege and employs robust, time-limited credentials, thereby maintaining a higher standard of security and operational stability compared to the delegated authority model of OAuth Apps.

Install the Google Chat App for GitHub repositories.

Set up the GitHub app in Chat

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • To open the configuration window, click Sign in.
  • Click Configure Access Sign in to GitHub.
  • Complete the sign-in process then close the popup.
  • To update the Chat dialog, click Refresh.
  • Under Add Repositories, type the GitHub repository you want notifications for.
  • Check the boxes for the events you want notifications for.
  • Click Save. Tip: You need to set up notifications in each space where you add the app. The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member.

Migrate from OAuth app (Legacy) to GitHub app (Recommended)

To migrate your current connection from the older OAuth app authentication method to the recommended GitHub app method:

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message or space with the GitHub app.
  • In the message field, click Google Workspace tools .
  • In the command list, select GitHub Reauthorize.
  • To complete the migration and reauthorization process, follow the on-screen instructions in the Chat dialogue.

Use the GitHub app in spaces

To use the app in spaces, you need to @mention or /mention the app in each message and in replies to the messages from the app.

The @mention or /mention confirms you’ve sent the message to the app and not to others in the space.

  • Open the Chat app .
  • In a space, enter @github or /github followed by the command.
    • When you mention @github or /github, the message is sent to the app and not to others in the space.

Change app settings

In spaces, only the person who added the app can change the settings.

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • To open the current settings for the app, enter: /github_settings.
  • Change the settings as needed.
  • Click Save. Removing the app from a space deletes the app settings.

Use the Google Cloud Build app in Google Chat

Use the Google Cloud Build app in Chat to get notifications about your Cloud Build projects.

Before you begin

Enable the Cloud Build API for any project where you want to use the Cloud Build app. Learn more about Cloud Build.

  • You need a Google Cloud Platform account.
  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.

Set up the Cloud Build app notifications

Tip: You need to set up notifications in each space where you add the app. The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member.

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Choose an option:
    • Open a direct message with the app and enter settings.
    • Go to a space with the app and enter @Cloud Build settings or /Cloud Build settings.
  • The current settings for the app opens.
  • Click Edit Settings.
  • Sign in to your Cloud Build account.
    • The Cloud Build app configuration window opens and loads the Cloud projects that are available to you.
  • Enter the name of a Cloud project.
    • You can find a list of triggers.
  • Select a Cloud Build trigger from the list.
  • From the Thread messages by menu, choose an option:
    • No threads
    • Project
    • Trigger.
  • Select the states for which you want to send Chat notifications.
  • Click Save.
  • Optional: To configure another project and trigger notification, click Add.

Change app settings

In spaces, only the person who configured the app can change the settings.

  • Open Google Chat.

  • Choose an option:

    • Open a direct message with the app and enter settings.
    • Go to a space with the app and enter @Cloud Build settings or /Cloud Build settings.

  • The current settings for the app opens.

  • Click Edit Settings.

  • Sign in to your Cloud Build account.

    • The Cloud Build app configuration window opens.

  • Click Edit and change the settings as needed.

  • Click Save. Once the app is removed from a space, the app settings get deleted.

  • To get a list of all available commands, enter @Cloud Build help or /Cloud Build help.

  • To find the currently configured notifications, enter @Cloud Build settings or /Cloud Build settings.

  • To send feedback about the app, enter @Cloud Build feedback feedback text or /Cloud Build feedback feedback text. Use the Google Drive app in Google Chat

You can use the Google Drive app to get notifications in Google Chat about activity in Drive.

Learn about Google Drive notifications in Chat

If you have the Google Drive app for Google Chat installed, you get direct messages about Google Drive events, such as:

  • A new file or folder that’s shared with you.
  • A new comment in a file you own, a comment, or an action item that mentions you or is assigned to you.
    • New mentions also show up in Chat’s Mentions shortcut.
    • You can reply to comments directly from the Google Drive app for Google Chat. For example, to mention a colleague, type “@” followed by their name or email address.
  • An access request to a file you own.
    • To share the file, select the access level you want to provide, such as:
      • Editor
      • Viewer
      • Commenter
    • Select an option:
      • Click Share.
      • Decline access. The notifications from the Google Drive app for Chat have a few limitations compared to Drive notifications that you get through email, browser, or mobile apps. These limitations include:
  • To reduce notification volume, email notifications are delayed and grouped together. Notifications in Google Chat are sent immediately and not grouped together.
  • If a user edits a comment after they post it, the notification doesn’t update. To find the updated comment, you need to access the original document through the link in the notification.
  • You don’t receive notifications when tasks are assigned to you in documents.
  • You don’t receive notifications when there are edits or suggestions in documents you own.
  • You don’t receive notifications for emoji reactions to comments. You can’t provide emoji reactions from the Google Drive app.

Before you begin

If the app isn’t installed, add the app to Chat. Learn how to use apps in Chat.

Manage Google Drive notifications in Chat or Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • On the left, under “Direct messages,” click Google Drive.
  • Click More options Notifications.
  • Select All or None.
  • Optional: To prevent Google Drive from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

Uninstall the Google Drive app

Important: For work or school accounts, you can’t uninstall apps your admin installs.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • On the left, under “Direct messages,” click Google Drive.
  • Click the app name Uninstall.

Block a sender or report a specific file

Important: This option is only available on a shared file owned by a user outside your organization.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • On the left, under “Direct messages,” click Google Drive.
  • At the bottom of the relevant notification card, click Block sender or report.

  • You don’t receive notifications when there are edits or suggestions in documents you own.
  • You don’t receive notifications for emoji reactions to comments. You can’t provide emoji reactions from the Google Drive app.

Before you begin

If the app isn’t installed, add the app to Chat. Learn how to use apps in Chat.

Manage Google Drive notifications in Chat or Gmail

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • On the left, under “Direct messages,” click Google Drive.
  • Click More options Notifications.
  • Select All or None.
  • Optional: To prevent Google Drive from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

Uninstall the Google Drive app

Important: For work or school accounts, you can’t uninstall apps your admin installs.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • On the left, under “Direct messages,” click Google Drive.
  • Click the app name Uninstall.

Block a sender or report a specific file

Important: This option is only available on a shared file owned by a user outside your organization.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • On the left, under “Direct messages,” click Google Drive.
  • At the bottom of the relevant notification card, click Block sender or report.

Use the Google Drive app in Google Chat (iPhone and iPad)

You can use the Google Drive app to get notifications in Google Chat about activity in Drive.

Learn about Google Drive notifications in Chat

If you have the Google Drive app for Google Chat installed, you get direct messages about Google Drive events, such as:

  • A new file or folder that’s shared with you.
  • A new comment in a file you own, a comment, or an action item that mentions you or is assigned to you.
    • New mentions also show up in Chat’s Mentions shortcut.
    • You can reply to comments directly from the Google Drive app for Google Chat. For example, to mention a colleague, type “@” followed by their name or email address.
  • An access request to a file you own.
    • To share the file, select the access level you want to provide, such as:
      • Editor
      • Viewer
      • Commenter
    • Select an option:
      • Click Share.
      • Decline access. The notifications from the Google Drive app for Chat have a few limitations compared to Drive notifications that you get through email, browser, or mobile apps. These limitations include:
  • To reduce notification volume, email notifications are delayed and grouped together. Notifications in Google Chat are sent immediately and not grouped together.
  • If a user edits a comment after they post it, the notification doesn’t update. To find the updated comment, you need to access the original document through the link in the notification.
  • You don’t receive notifications when tasks are assigned to you in documents.
  • You don’t receive notifications when there are edits or suggestions in documents you own.
  • You don’t receive notifications for emoji reactions to comments. You can’t provide emoji reactions from the Google Drive app.

Before you begin

If the app isn’t installed, add the app to Chat. Learn how to use apps in Chat.

Manage Google Drive notifications in Chat or Gmail

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app .
  • In your list of direct messages, tap and hold the Google Drive app.
  • Tap Notification settings.
  • Select All or None.
  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

Uninstall the Google Drive app

Important: For work or school accounts, you can’t uninstall apps your admin installs.

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • In the bottom navigation menu, tap Direct messages Google Drive.
  • At the top, tap the app name Uninstall.

Block a sender or report a specific file

Important: This option is only available to a shared file owned by a user outside your organization.

  • On your iPhone or iPad, open the Chat app or Gmail app .
    • In Gmail: At the bottom, tap Chat .
  • In the bottom navigation menu, tap Direct messages Google Drive.
  • At the bottom of the relevant notification card, tap Block sender or report.

Use the Jira app in Google Chat

Use the Jira app in Chat to get messages about updates to your Jira Software projects. The app sends messages from Jira to Chat.

Before you begin

  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • Install the Chat Jira plugin from the Atlassian Marketplace. Your Jira admin may need to approve this.

Set up the Jira app in Chat

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
    • After installation, you get a welcome message and a card that prompts you to connect to Jira.
    • If you connect in a direct message for personal notifications, notifications are automatically enabled when you connect the app. You can set up which issues you receive updates on, such as issues that you:
      • Report
      • Watch
      • Are the assignee on
      • Are mentioned in
    • These notifications apply across one or more Jira sites.
  • Click Connect.
    • If you already set up Jira, the app uses the site from the previous connection.
    • After you connect the app to Jira, you can:
      • In a direct message: Select the projects from where you want to receive personal notifications.
      • In a space: Select projects quickly to subscribe to issues.
    • After a successful connection, you’ll receive a confirmation message and a list of connected Jira sites or projects. To edit filters or change these settings, click Edit notification settings.
  • Enter the project names to receive notifications.
  • Optional: You can use the multi-select search to enter the projects.
  • Click Save.
  • Optional: To edit notifications, click Edit notification settings. Tip: You need to set up notifications in each space where you add the app. The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member.

Update Jira app notification settings

Jira app notifications are displayed with styled formatting in Chat. This includes elements such as headers, lists, code blocks, checklists, quotes, and links. If a notification includes a table, it will be displayed as structured plain text.

You can manage your personal-notification settings within the Jira app’s direct message.

Manage personal filters

To select the types of personal updates you want to receive:

  • On your computer, open a direct message with the Jira app.
  • If prompted, to open the settings dialogue, select Edit notification settings.
    • Or, you can type: /jira_settings. Then, press Enter.
  • Select or deselect the types of personal updates you want to receive on issues:
    • You’re watching
    • You’ve reported
    • You’re the assignee on
    • You’re mentioned in
    • Ignore changes made by myself (on by default)
  • Optional: You can also manage connected Jira sites from this page.
  • Click Save.
Filter notifications by project (single-connected site)

When you have only one Jira site connected, you can filter your personal notifications to specific projects.

To locate the project-filtering options in the settings dialogue:

  • On your computer, open a direct message with the Jira app.
  • If prompted, to open the settings dialogue, click Edit notification settings.
    • Or, you can type: /jira_settings. Then, press Enter.
  • In “Send updates from only these projects,” select the specific projects you want to filter for.
  • Click Save. Tip: The default interface provides “All Projects.”
Filter notifications by project (multiple-connected sites)

When you have multiple Jira sites connected, you can filter your personal notifications by project for each site.

To locate the project-filtering options for each connected site in the settings dialogue:

  • On your computer, open a direct message with the Jira app.
  • If prompted, to open the settings dialogue, select Edit notification settings.
    • Or, you can type: /jira_settings. Then, press Enter.
  • To receive notifications for a site, in “Send updates from only these projects,” select specific projects.
  • Optional: Repeat for other connected sites as needed.
  • Click Save. Tip: Each Jira site provides an option like “sitename: All Projects.”

Use Jira app commands in Chat

Important: To get available commands, enter: /

You can use these slash commands in a direct message or space with the Jira app in Chat:

  • /jira_connect: Connects the Jira app to your Jira site.
  • /jira_create: Creates a new issue.
  • /jira_view [issue_id]: Provides the specified Jira issue info.
  • /jira_disconnect: Disconnects the Jira app or this space from your Jira site.
  • /jira_help: Displays the help message.
  • /jira_feedback: Sends feedback about the Jira app.
  • /jira_subscriptions: Shows settings to manage subscriptions for Jira projects with specific filters.
  • /jira_settings: Shows settings for personal notifications and space subscriptions. You can also use the “Create issue” and “Settings” buttons for quick access to related actions.

Change app settings

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Type /jira_settings and press Enter. The settings page opens.
  • Change the settings as needed.
  • Click Save.

Delete app settings

  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • To delete the configuration, enter delete config. In spaces, enter /jira_settings. Note: Removing the app from a space deletes the app settings. Removing the app from a direct message only pauses notifications. To fully disconnect and revoke your Jira credentials, you need to run the /jira_disconnect command.

Use the PagerDuty app in Google Chat

Use the PagerDuty app in Google Chat to get notifications about PagerDuty incidents and acknowledge, resolve, and record new incidents.

Before you begin

  • You need permission from your Google Workspace administrator to install apps.
  • You need to add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • You need a PagerDuty account with Admin or Account Owner permissions in order to first set up the integration.

Set up the PagerDuty app in Chat

  • Open Chat.
  • Select an option:
  • Open a direct message with the app.
  • Go to a space with the app.
  • To sign in to your PagerDuty account and subdomain, click Authorize. To set up the app, you must sign in to a PagerDuty account with Admin or Account Owner permissions in the subdomain.
  • Complete the sign-in on the PagerDuty website.
  • Allow the PagerDuty Chat app to access some PagerDuty permissions.
  • If prompted, select the correct PagerDuty account to use.
  • Once the connection is successful, configure your notification settings by entering “/pd_settings”.
  • Click Create New Settings.
  • Select the PagerDuty source you want to receive notifications from.
  • Check the boxes for the items you want to get notifications about in Chat.
  • Click Save.
  • (Optional) To add another project, enter “/pd_settings” again. Then, at the bottom of the dialogue, click the Authorize button. You must set up notifications in each space where you add the app. The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member.

Change app settings

Only PagerDuty Admins or Account Owners can change the settings.

  • Open Chat.
  • Select an option:
    • Open a direct message with the app.
    • Go to a Space with the app.
  • Enter settings.
    • In the Space, enter “/pd_settings”. The current settings for the app appear.
    • If you’re in a direct message with the app, you can view all your active PagerDuty connections.
    • If you’re in a Space, you can view all the PagerDuty connections that are active in that Space.
  • To edit or delete any visible connection, click Edit or Delete.
  • In order to make new PagerDuty connections, click Authorize. Removing the app from a space deletes the app settings.

Use the app in spaces

To use the app in spaces, you can use various commands by entering “/”. To see the full list of commands, enter “/pd_help”.

Use the Poll app in Google Chat

You can quickly gather team input and make decisions with Google Chat’s Poll app.

Important:

  • If you use a work or school account, your admin manages the apps you can access in Chat, such as the Poll app.
  • If you’re an admin, learn how to allow users to install Chat apps.

Create a poll

You can create a poll in direct messages, group messages, or spaces and people can vote on it.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat .
  • Add the Poll app:
    • Select a direct message, group message, or space.
    • In the reply field, enter /poll or @poll.
    • Select the Poll app.
      • If you use the app for the first time, in the dialogue box, click Add app & send.
  • Create a poll: In the dialogue box, enter a question and up to 4 choices:
    • Optional:
      • To add up to 6 more choices, click Add more choices.
      • Under “Advanced options”:
        • Check the box next to “Allow multiple votes.”
        • Check the box next to “Hide name of participants.”
        • To set a voting deadline, select Set voting deadline. Then, choose a date and time.
      • To translate your poll:
        • Click Change poll language.
        • Select the language.
  • Click Create. The set closing date and time appears in the poll message. A private message notifies you when your poll closes.

Edit a poll

After creating a new poll, you receive a private message. This message includes an “Edit poll” button. You can use this button to modify your poll.

Vote in a poll

When someone creates a poll, you receive a chat notification.

  • To vote in a poll, next to your preferred choice, click Vote.
  • To find more details about the poll results, click Show results.

Use the Salesforce app in Google Chat

Use the Salesforce app in Chat to search for accounts, contacts, leads, and opportunities in Salesforce.

For Salesforce Admins: Learn how to integrate Salesforce with Google Chat

Salesforce & Google Chat Integration Guide for Salesforce Administrators
1. Introduction

This guide provides step-by-step instructions for configuring your Salesforce organization to support the Google Chat integration. This integration uses a per-user authentication model, allowing users to securely connect their own accounts to use Salesforce functionalities directly from Google Chat.

2. Prerequisites
  • Salesforce Edition: Enterprise, Unlimited, Performance, or Developer Edition. API request limits and allocations are available at the following link: Salesforce API limits
  • Administrator Permissions: You must be a Salesforce Administrator with permissions to create External Client Apps and Permission Sets.
3. Configuration
Step 1: Install and Authorize Salesforce chat app
  • Open Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Click the “Sign in” button. If you don’t see it, then initiate /sf_search command.
  • In the opened dialog click configure.
  • Sign in to Salesforce using your Salesforce admin account.
  • At the “Allow Access” window, click Allow and then close your browser tab.
Step 2: Install Salesforce Connected app
  • Sign in to Salesforce using your Salesforce admin account.
  • Navigate to Setup Apps Connected Apps Connected Apps OAuth Usage menu item.
  • Find “Salesforce for Google Chat” Connected app and Install the app
Step 3: Create a Custom Permission Set for Users

This Permission Set will grant users the specific object and field access needed to use the integration’s features.

  • A. Create the Custom Permission Set:
    • Navigate to Setup Users Permission Sets.
    • Click New.
    • Enter the following details:
      • Label: Google Chat Integration Access
      • API Name: Google_Chat_Integration_Access
    • Click Save.
  • B. Configure Object and Field Permissions:
    • In the newly created Permission Set, click Object Settings.
    • For each object, click its name, click Edit, and configure the specified Object Permissions and Field-Level Security. To be searchable, objects must have Read access enabled.
    • Click Save.
  • C. Configure System Permissions:
  • In the newly created Permission Set, click System Permissions.
  • Click Edit.
  • Check the box for API Enabled and click Save. This permission is required for users to make any API calls. For more comprehensive documentation, please refer to the following link: Create a Salesforce Permission Set
Step 4: Assign Permissions to Users

Assign the new Permission Set to all users who need to use the Google Chat integration.

  • Navigate back to the Google Chat Integration Access Permission Set.
  • Click Manage Assignments.
  • Click Add Assignments.
  • Select the checkboxes next to all users who should have access to the integration.
  • Click Assign.
Step 5: Post-Installation

Newly provisioned users may initially encounter limited or absent results when utilizing the /sf_search command within the Google Chat application. This occurs until a search activity profile is established within Salesforce, a process that typically spans a few days. To enable full functionality of the /sf_search command in Google Chat, users are required to perform searches via the Salesforce user interface during this initial period. To expedite this process, users can also pin the most important record types in the Salesforce classic search results.

  • At the “Allow Access” window, click Allow close your browser.

Use the Workday app in Google Chat

You can complete Workday quick actions from Chat with Google Chat and Workday integration. To access features, a Workday admin has to configure the app for their domain or organization. You can then install the app from within Chat. A Workspace admin can also install the app on your behalf.

For Workday admins: Learn how to integrate Workday with Google Chat

Step 1: Configure Integration System and Credentials

  • Sign in to Workday.
    • Go to your Workday tenant.
    • Sign in with your administrator account.
  • Configure event subscriptions to enable notifications:
    • Create integration system:
      • In the search bar, enter “Create Integration System” and select the task.
      • When the window opens, enter a system name (for example, Chat_Integration).
      • For Template, select Subscriber_Integration from the list.
      • Select OK.
    • Set up event subscription:
      • In the created “Integration System View,” open the Related Actions menu. This is under the dot button located next to the System Name.
      • Select Integration System Edit Subscriptions.
      • Select Subscribe to all Business Processes.
      • Set Notification URL: workday-bot-production.appspot.com
      • Select OK.
    • Enable OAuth 2.0 clients:
      • In the search bar, enter “Edit Tenant Setup - Security”.
      • Select the task.
      • On the settings page, find the “OAuth 2.0 Settings” section.
      • Make sure the OAuth 2.0 Clients Enabled checkbox is selected.
      • Click OK.
  • Create a new API client:
    • In the search bar, enter “Register API Client” and select the task.
    • You are prompted to set up the connection.
    • On the registration screen, fill out the following fields:
      • Client Name: Google Chat Workday Integration
      • Client Grant Type: Authorization Code Grant
      • Access Token Type: Bearer
      • Redirection URI: workday-bot-production.appspot.com
      • Non-Expiring Refresh Tokens: Checked
      • Scope: Contact Information, Staffing, Expenses, Time Off and Leave, Adaptive Planning for Financial Plans, Adaptive Planning for the Workforce, Tenant Non-Configurable, System
    • Save information from the following fields as you will need it later:
      • Client ID
      • Secret ID
      • Workday REST API Endpoint
      • Workday Token Endpoint
      • Workday Authorization Endpoint
  • Create an ISU account: This special account handles the connection securely.
    • In the search bar, enter “Create Integration System User” and select the task.
    • You are prompted to set up the account.
    • On the setup screen, fill out the following fields:
      • User Name: Google Chat Workday ISU
      • New Password: Enter and verify new password
      • Session Timeout Minutes: 0
      • Do Not Allow UI Sessions: Should be unchecked
    • Select OK.
  • Create a security group for the user (ISSG):
    • In the search bar, enter “Create Security Group” and select the task.
    • You are prompted to fill out the following fields:
      • Select Type of Tenanted Security Group: Integration System Security Group (Unconstrained)
      • Name: ISSG Google Chat Integration
    • Select OK.
    • Assign ISU to this ISSG.
  • Assign ISSG permissions (domain security policy):
    • In the search bar, enter “Maintain Permissions for Security Group” and then select the task.
    • On the task page:
      • For “Operation,” select Maintain.
      • For “Source Security Group,” select the ISSG you just created (ISSG_GoogleChat_Integration).
    • Add the following Domain Security Policy Permissions to the ISSG:
      • View or Modify Access: View and Modify, Domain Security Policy: Workday Query Language, Functional Areas: System
      • View or Modify Access: View Only, Domain Security Policy: Worker Data: Public Worker Reports, Functional Areas: Staffing
      • View or Modify Access: View Only, Domain Security Policy: Business Process Administration, Functional Areas: System
      • View or Modify Access: View Only, Domain Security Policy: Worker Data: Current Management Level Information, Functional Areas: Staffing
    • Activate pending security policy changes.
      • In the search bar, enter “Activate Pending Security Policy Changes” and then select the task.
      • Enter a comment (for example, Permissions for Google Chat integration).
      • Select OK.
        • This applies all the permissions you just configured.
    • Continue with an ISU:
      • Log out of your Workday account.
      • Select Next to open the Workday setup.

Step 2: Provide API client details

  • Prepare your API client details.
    • If you have not prepared the API client details, refer to information in Step 1.
  • Fill in the following fields:
    • Client ID
    • Client Secret
    • Workday REST API Endpoint
    • Token Endpoint
    • Authorization Endpoint
  • Select Next.

Step 3: Connect to Workday using an ISU account

This step securely authorizes Google Chat to access your Workday instance.

  • Prepare your ISU account credentials.
    • If you have not created the ISU account, refer to information in Step 1.
  • Select Next.
  • Select Configure Access to open the Workday sign-in page in a new window.
  • Sign in using your Integration System User (ISU) account credentials.
    • Use the Integration System User (ISU) account. Your personal Workday account is not supported for this step.
  • After signing in and granting access in Workday, return to Google Chat.
  • Select Refresh. This takes you to the final step.

Step 4: Sign in to Workday with your personal account

  • Go to your Workday browser tab. If you see an error, an ISU session might still be active in another browser tab or window. Make sure you are only signed in to Workday with your personal account before continuing.
    • Sign out of the Integration System User (ISU) account.
    • Sign back in using your personal Workday account.
  • Return to Google Chat.
  • Select Next.
  • Select Configure Access.
    • You are taken to a successful connection message.

Before you begin

  • You need permission from your Google Workspace administrator to install apps.
  • You need to add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • Before you can set up your Workday app in Chat, your Workday Admin has to activate OAuth and create a new API client for the Google integration setup. Your Workday Admin will need the following information to proceed:
    • Client ID
    • Secret ID
    • Workday REST API Endpoint
    • Workday Token Endpoint
    • Workday Authorization Endpoint

Set up the Workday app in Chat

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app.
    • You get a welcome message with info about the app and a prompt to connect your Workday account.
  • To sign in to your Workday account and subdomain, click Authorize.
  • Tip: To set up the app, you must sign in to a Workday account with Admin or Account owner permissions in the subdomain.
  • Complete the sign in on the Workday website.
  • Allow the Workday Chat app to access some Workday permissions.
  • If prompted, select the correct Workday account to use.
  • If the connection is successful:
    • To find a list of all available commands:
      • Select Menu .
      • Click the help command or type: /workday
    • Some examples of what you can do:
      • Submit, track, and review time off requests.
      • View your time-off balance.
      • Check company holidays.
      • Find contact details.
      • Start a new expense report.
      • Check tasks.
      • Get notifications when a new task is:
        • Assigned to you.
        • Completed.

  • Chat apps available from Google
