      • Session Timeout Minutes: 0
      • Do Not Allow UI Sessions: Should be unchecked
    • Select OK.
  • Create a security group for the user (ISSG):
    • In the search bar, enter “Create Security Group” and select the task.
    • You are prompted to fill out the following fields:
      • Select Type of Tenanted Security Group: Integration System Security Group (Unconstrained)
      • Name: ISSG Google Chat Integration
    • Select OK.
    • Assign ISU to this ISSG.
  • Assign ISSG permissions (domain security policy):
    • In the search bar, enter “Maintain Permissions for Security Group” and then select the task.
    • On the task page:
      • For “Operation,” select Maintain.
      • For “Source Security Group,” select the ISSG you just created (ISSG_GoogleChat_Integration).
    • Add the following Domain Security Policy Permissions to the ISSG:
      • View or Modify Access: View and Modify, Domain Security Policy: Workday Query Language, Functional Areas: System
      • View or Modify Access: View Only, Domain Security Policy: Worker Data: Public Worker Reports, Functional Areas: Staffing
      • View or Modify Access: View Only, Domain Security Policy: Business Process Administration, Functional Areas: System
      • View or Modify Access: View Only, Domain Security Policy: Worker Data: Current Management Level Information, Functional Areas: Staffing
    • Activate pending security policy changes.
      • In the search bar, enter “Activate Pending Security Policy Changes” and then select the task.
      • Enter a comment (for example, Permissions for Google Chat integration).
      • Select OK.
        • This applies all the permissions you just configured.
    • Continue with an ISU:
      • Log out of your Workday account.
      • Select Next to open the Workday setup.

Step 2: Provide API client details

  • Prepare your API client details.
    • If you have not prepared the API client details, refer to information in Step 1.
  • Fill in the following fields:
    • Client ID
    • Client Secret
    • Workday REST API Endpoint
    • Token Endpoint
    • Authorization Endpoint
  • Select Next.

Step 3: Connect to Workday using an ISU account

This step securely authorizes Google Chat to access your Workday instance.

  • Prepare your ISU account credentials.
    • If you have not created the ISU account, refer to information in Step 1.
  • Select Next.
  • Select Configure Access to open the Workday sign-in page in a new window.
  • Sign in using your Integration System User (ISU) account credentials.
    • Use the Integration System User (ISU) account. Your personal Workday account is not supported for this step.
  • After signing in and granting access in Workday, return to Google Chat.
  • Select Refresh. This takes you to the final step.

Step 4: Sign in to Workday with your personal account

  • Go to your Workday browser tab. If you see an error, an ISU session might still be active in another browser tab or window. Make sure you are only signed in to Workday with your personal account before continuing.
    • Sign out of the Integration System User (ISU) account.
    • Sign back in using your personal Workday account.
  • Return to Google Chat.
  • Select Next.
  • Select Configure Access.
    • You are taken to a successful connection message.

Before you begin

  • You need permission from your Google Workspace administrator to install apps.
  • You need to add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • Before you can set up your Workday app in Chat, your Workday Admin has to activate OAuth and create a new API client for the Google integration setup. Your Workday Admin will need the following information to proceed:
    • Client ID
    • Secret ID
    • Workday REST API Endpoint
    • Workday Token Endpoint
    • Workday Authorization Endpoint

Set up the Workday app in Chat

  • Open the Chat app or Gmail app .
  • Open a direct message with the Workday app.
    • You get a welcome message with info about the app and a prompt to connect your Workday account.
  • Below the welcome message, click Help.
  • To sign in to your Workday account and subdomain, tap Authorize.
  • Tip: To set up the app, you must sign in to a Workday account with Admin or Account owner permissions in the subdomain.
  • Complete the sign in on the Workday website.
  • Allow the Workday Chat app to access some Workday permissions.
  • If prompted, select the correct Workday account to use.
  • If the connection is successful:
    • To find a list of all available commands:
      • Select Menu .
      • Click the help command or type: /workday
    • Some examples of what you can do:
      • Submit, track, and review time off requests.
      • View your time-off balance.
      • Check company holidays.
      • Find contact details.
      • Start a new expense report.
      • Check tasks.
      • Get notifications when a new task is:
        • Assigned to you.
        • Completed.

Use the Zapier app in Google Chat

Use the Zapier app in Chat to get notifications about Zap actions. The app sends messages from the Zap to Chat.

Before you begin

  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.

Set up the Zapier app in Chat

Set up Chat to get messages from a Zap.

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Enter the command allowzaps.
    • In spaces, enter @Zapier allowzaps or /Zapier allowzaps.
    • The app shows a card to allow Zaps.
  • Click Click To Allow Zaps.
  • Sign in to you work or school account.
    • A message confirms that Zaps can send messages to this chat for you.

Stop Zaps in Chat

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Enter the command stopzaps.
    • In spaces, enter @Zapier stopzaps or /Zapier stopzaps.
    • The app shows a card to stop Zaps.
  • Click Click To Stop Zaps.
    • A message confirms that Zaps can no longer send messages to this chat for you.

Connect a Zap to Google Chat

To integrate with Chat, you need to set up a Zap action. Here’s a summary of the steps in Zapier. For detailed instructions, visit the Zapier website.

  • Open Zapier.
  • Create a Zap or open an existing Zap.
  • Add an action step to the Zap:
    • Choose the Google Chat app.
    • Save the Create Message action.
    • Connect your Google Account. This is the work or school account you use for Chat.
    • Set up a template for the messages. You can choose Chat spaces where you added the app and allow zaps. The Zap can now contact the Zapier app and send messages to Chat.

Use the Zendesk app in Google Chat

Use the Zendesk app in Chat to get notifications when issues occur in Zendesk.

Before you begin

  • You need permission to install apps from your Google Workspace administrator.
  • Add the app to Chat. Learn how to find apps and add them to Chat.
  • You need a Zendesk account with admin privileges.

Set up the Zendesk app in Chat

Tip: You need to set up notifications in each space where you add the app. The app sends notifications to all spaces where it’s a member.

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Click Sign in to your Zendesk account.
    • The configuration window opens.
  • Enter your Zendesk subdomain.
  • Click Next.
  • Enter your Zendesk username and password.
  • Click Sign in.
  • Under Choose Group, to get notifications, click the Down arrow Zendesk group.
  • Under Priority greater than or equal to, click the Down arrow .
    • Set the priority level for your notifications.
  • Under Thread messages by, click the Down arrow .
  • Choose a threading option.
  • To get the notifications of the items in Chat, check the boxes next to the items.
  • Click Save.
  • Optional: To add another project, click Add.

Change app settings

You can access the Zendesk app settings in a direct message with the app or in a space that has the app added.

In spaces, only the person who added the app can change the settings. Once the app is removed from a space, the app settings get deleted.

  • Open Google Chat.
  • Open a direct message with the app or go to a space with the app.
  • Choose an option to find the settings for the app:
    • In a direct message with the Zendesk app, enter settings.
    • In a space, enter @Zendesk settings or /Zendesk settings.
  • Click Edit Settings.
  • Click Edit .
  • Change the settings as needed.
  • Click Save. Google, Google Workspace, and related marks and logos are trademarks of Google LLC. All other company and product names are trademarks of the companies with which they are associated.

Miscellaneous

Join a space in Google Chat (Miscellaneous)

When you’re invited to join a space, you can preview the space and view its message history.

When you leave a space, you can’t:

  • Rejoin unless another member adds or invites you.
  • Get updates on active conversation threads. If you rejoin a space, you can view all message history. If someone removes you from a space, you’ll need to be invited again.

Tip: If the space is open, you can rejoin at any time. Learn about open spaces.

Join a space

Important: If the space owner or manager turns off the request option, you can’t request to join a space.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, click New chat Browse spaces .
  • Search for a space.
    • The spaces that you’re invited to appear at the top of the list.
  • Click the space name or View.
    • If the space is open, click Join. You can also preview the messages.
    • If the space is private or discoverable and the space allows it, you can submit a request to join. Tip: If you request to join a space, your username, email address, and avatar are shared with the space owner and manager once they receive your request. Some spaces may not allow requests to join.

Leave a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • Next to a space name, click More options Leave Leave space.

Rejoin a space

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.
  • On the left, click New chat Browse spaces .
  • Search for a space.
  • Click the space name or View.
    • If the space is open, click Join. You can also preview the messages.
    • If the space is private or discoverable and the space allows it, you can submit a request to join. Tip: You can delete a space you created. Learn how to delete a space.

Personalize your Google Chat display settings (Miscellaneous)

To personalize your experience in Google Chat, you can select your color, mode, and density settings.

Change the appearance of Chat

Important: These appearance settings apply for chat.google.com and the Chat standalone app. These settings don’t apply to Chat in Gmail. Learn more about Chat in Gmail.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings .
  • In the side panel, click Appearance .
  • Select an option:
    • Under “Color,” select the color palette you want.
    • Under “Mode,” select: System, Light, or Dark.
      • Tip: The “System” option is based on your OS or browser setting.
    • Under “Density,” select Comfortable or Compact. Learn more about density settings for Chat in Gmail.
      • Tip: Use Compact mode to find more information at a glance in Chat. Comfortable (Default)

Compact

  • Sender and recipient message bubbles are on opposite sides.
  • Narrower message bubbles.
  • More space in the left bar, conversation list, and Home.
  • Sender and recipient message bubbles are on the same side.
  • Wider message bubbles.
  • Less space in the left bar, conversation list, and Home.
  • Click Close . Tip: Appearance settings in Chat comply with accessibility guidelines. Learn more about Accessibility in Google Chat.

Adjust density settings for Chat in Gmail

When you adjust the density settings in Gmail, your changes apply to both Gmail and Chat in Gmail.

Important: These changes don’t apply to Chat when you access it through:

  • chat.google.com

  • Chat standalone app To change the density settings:

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings .

  • In the settings side panel, under “Density,” select:

    • Default
    • Comfortable
    • Compact Tip: In Chat in Gmail, the “Default” and “Comfortable” options use the same Chat density layout.

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off (Miscellaneous)

Notifications appear on the devices you used most recently. If you’re not active in Chat, notifications appear on all devices signed in to your Google Account.

By default, you receive notifications when:

  • Someone @ mentions you
  • Someone reacts or responds to your message If you mute a specific conversation or set your Chat status to “Do not disturb,” you won’t receive notifications.

In this article, learn how to:

  • Turn notifications on or off.

  • Customize notifications for specific conversations & spaces.

  • Customize notification sounds.

  • Get notifications in the Chat mobile app.

  • Update device or browser notification settings for Chat on a computer. Tips:

  • If email notifications are on, you get email reminders for Chat messages you haven’t read for more than 12 hours.

  • If you have multiple Google Accounts, you can set different notification settings for each account.

  • Some Google Chat apps can ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status or notification settings, to send updates, including:

    • @notify messages: These messages are for critical or time-sensitive information. They work like @all messages to get immediate attention and ignore your “Do Not Disturb” status, muted conversations, or notification settings.
    • @silent messages: These messages are for low-priority updates. They minimize disruption by working like system messages.

Google Chat: Manage your settings

Turn Google Chat notifications on or off

Turn on notifications

Turn on notifications in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • To turn on notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • If you don’t get Google Chat notifications after you turn it on, allow Google Chat notifications in your operating system and browser.

  • To turn email notifications for unread messages on or off, under “Email notifications,” select Only @mentions & direct messages or Off.

Manage combined notification permissions

Web users can grant browser notifications and idle detection permissions through a single flow. This occurs in two ways:

  • Enabled but blocked: If “Allow chat notifications” is enabled but the browser blocks notifications, a “Turn on” button appears. Click it to trigger permission dialogs.
  • Disabled toggle: If “Allow chat notifications” is disabled, turning on the toggle triggers permission dialogs.
Check if notifications are on
  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.
  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .
  • Under “Desktop notifications,” click Show an example.
  • If an example notification doesn’t appear:
    • Your notifications may be muted because of your availability status.
    • Turn on notifications for the device and browser you use with Google Chat.
Turn on notifications in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • To turn on notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Allow chat notifications.”

Check if notifications are on

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat notifications settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” click Show an example.

  • If an example notification doesn’t appear:

    • Your notifications may be muted because of your availability status.
    • Turn on notifications for the device and browser you use with Gmail. Turn off notifications
Turn off notifications in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • To turn off notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.” Learn how to change your availability status in Google Chat.

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn off Google Chat notifications in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • To turn off notifications for Google Chat messages, under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Allow chat notifications.” Tips:

  • To temporarily mute notifications, set your status to “Do not disturb.” Learn how to change your availability status in Google Chat.

  • When you mute a conversation or space, the threads you follow still appear in Home. If someone mentions you directly in a thread, you follow that thread automatically. Learn how to mute conversations in Google Chat.

Turn Google Chat reaction notifications on or off

Turn on reaction notifications

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” check the box next to “Reaction notifications.” Tips:

  • For reaction notifications to work, turn on Allow chat notifications.

  • The existing notification settings apply to the reaction notifications of a conversation.

  • You can’t get reaction notifications in Announcement Spaces. Turn off reaction notifications

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Desktop notifications,” uncheck the box next to “Reaction notifications.”

    • This also turns off reaction notifications on mobile.

Customize Google Chat notifications for spaces & direct messages

Customize notifications for a space with in-line threading

By default, only threads you follow are bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list. To control how thread updates show in Chat, customize your notification settings.

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.

    • In Gmail: On the left, click Chat.

  • Next to the space name, click More options Notifications.

  • Select an option for notifications:

    • All: Notifications for all new messages and replies to threads.
      • Tip: If you select “All,” it automatically follows all new threads for that space. To unfollow a thread, click Active Threads Following.
    • Main conversations: Notifications for all new main conversations, @mentions, and replies to threads you follow.
    • For you: Notifications for @mentions and replies to threads you follow.
    • None: No notifications, just an indicator for @mentions.

  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

  • Click Save. Turn notifications on or off for a direct message

  • On your computer, open Google Chat.

  • Next to the direct message or group DM, click More options Notifications.

    • For group DMs, you can select to get notifications for:
      • All: All new messages
      • For you: Only @mentions
      • None

  • Select All or None.

  • Optional: To prevent the conversation from being bolded and moved to the top of your conversation list, select the box next to “Mute conversation.”

Customize Google Chat notification sounds

Customize notification sounds in Google Chat

  • On your computer, go to Google Chat.

  • At the top right, click Settings Notifications .

  • Under “Notifications sounds,” select the sound to use for notifications. Customize Google Chat notification sounds in Gmail

  • On your computer, open Gmail.

  • At the top right, click Settings See all settings.

  • At the top, click the Chat and Meet tab. Go to Gmail settings for Chat

  • Next to “Chat settings,” click Manage chat settings.

  • Under “Notifications sounds,” select the sound to use for notifications.

Grant idle detection permissions

Idle detection delivers notifications to your active device. Granting this permission helps reliably send notifications and pauses mobile alerts when you are active on desktop.

If you are idle on Gmail or Google Chat on your computer, notifications go to your mobile device. You are considered idle if you’re inactive for over 30 seconds, even if you still have a web browser open.

For Chrome users, you can adjust settings to receive chat notifications on mobile only when you’re inactive on Chrome.

Respond to the permission prompt

When you enable Chat notifications, a dialog may appear. This dialog asks you to “Pause mobile notifications when you are active on this device.” Click Continue to grant idle detection permission.

Adjust Chrome settings manually

If the permission dialog doesn’t appear, you can manually enable idle detection in your Chrome settings.

  • Go to chrome://settings/content/idleDetection.
  • Check the box for “Sites can ask to know when you’re actively using your device.”
  • Under “Customized behaviors,” add mail.google.com or chat.google.com to the allowed sites list.
  • To add a site, click Add.

Update device or browser notification settings

Update device notifications

Each computer operating system has different steps to turn on notifications. For more info, go to your operating system’s online help.

Some computer operating systems have settings that mute notifications. If you don’t get the notifications, make sure notifications aren’t muted.

Update browser notifications

To turn notifications on or off, you might need to update your browser notification settings. Learn how to allow Google Chat notifications.

Use Gemini conversation summaries for unread messages

To catch up on important discussions in a space in Google Chat, you can use Gemini to summarize unread messages.

Feature availability

  • This feature is available as part of Gemini Beta.
  • Your administrator controls access to Gemini Beta. If you can’t find these features, your administrator may not have Beta features enabled for your organization.
  • This feature is also available as part of our early access testing program, Google Workspace Experiments.

Summarize unread messages in a conversation

  • On your computer, open Google Chat or Gmail.
  • Choose a conversation with unread messages that you want to summarize.
  • Click Summarize unread.
    • You can find a summary list of the recent messages that you haven’t read under the “Recent discussions” section.
    • Tip: For messages with many unread messages, summaries will automatically expand without clicking.
  • Click Close summary.

Give feedback about Gemini conversation summaries

Google Workspace with Gemini is constantly learning and may not be able to support your request.

If you get a suggestion that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can submit feedback. Your feedback can help improve AI-assisted Workspace features and broader Google efforts in AI.

Because feedback may be human readable, do not submit data that contains personal, confidential, or sensitive information.

  • At the top right of the generated output, select Good summary or Bad summary .
  • In the pop-up window, you can select the data you want to share along with your feedback, with additional context and output. If you don’t want to share certain data, you can uncheck it.
    • If you select Bad summary : To select the issue and enter additional feedback, select Next.
  • Select Submit. To provide general feedback on this feature, select Help Send feedback to Google. Learn how to send feedback in Google Chat.

To report a legal issue, create a request.

Learn about Gemini feature suggestions

  • Gemini feature suggestions don’t represent Google’s views, and should not be attributed to Google.
  • Don’t rely on Gemini features as medical, legal, financial or other professional advice.
  • Gemini features may suggest inaccurate or inappropriate information. Your feedback makes Gemini more helpful and safe.
  • Enterprise end users can submit feedback about their experience using this feature. End users are informed before they submit feedback that the feedback data shouldn’t contain personal, sensitive, or confidential information.
